items.body: Second time at the Bezau Beatz festival, located in a small, beautiful, and most peaceful village in the Austrian Alps, but much closer to Switzerland, Italy and Germany than to the Austrian free music scenes. Thanks to the festival's artistic directors and producers - drummers Alfred Vogel and Valentin Schuster - the festival has managed to create a friendly and highly attentive community of music lovers and musicians that is welcoming and shares all kinds of musical adventures and experiments. A perfect place to take a vacation from the local or global disturbing reality and its abhorrent horrors and stupidities, and find some nurturing, fresh air - literally. This festival will celebrate its 20th anniversary next year. 1st Day, Aug. 6 The festival opened with the Danish-Norwegian quartet Emmeluth’s Amoeba - alto sax player and bandleader Signe Emmeluth, her partner, guitarist Karl Bjorå, pianist Christian Balvig, and drummer Ole Mofjell - which stormed the intimate space at the festival’s headquarters, Hotel Post. This quartet has already released four albums and has developed a tight, telepathic interplay, using Emmeluth’s skeletal compositional motifs for exploratory, intense rhythmic improvisations. There were times that the interplay sounded as if Bjorå, Balvig, and Mofjell challenged Emmeluth’s commanding, natural flow of ideas with playful, even disruptive moves. Still, she used their tactics to steer the quartet into collective, even more powerful, cathartic eruptions. Later, down at the hotel’s basement - the SuBBwayZ - the duo NarrSteidle - German guitarist and electronics player Steffi Narr and drummer and electronics player Oliver Steidle (of The Killing Popes and Ilog), who has released a debut album on Vogel and Schuster’s Boomaslang label ( Ghost Ants , 2025), weaved resonant acoustic, electronic, and processed sounds into fragmented rhythmic patterns, that slowly evolved into rich yet twisted and restless grooves. The evening program moved to the main space - The Remise, a vintage locomotive garage most days of the year (with a strong aroma of grease), where Danish guitarist Teis Semey (who confessed that he has never seen mountains so high before) led his Amsterdam-based quintet: alto sax player José Soares, tenor sax player Jesse Schilderink, double bass player Jort Terwijn and drummer Giovanni Iacovella - with a set of playful pieces that flirted with free jazz, fusion and even pop songs, charged with youthful, passionate uplifting energy. The following performance of the German, all-female quartet Hilde - vocalist Marie Daniels, violinist Julia Brüssel, cellist Emily Wittbrodt, and trombonist Maria Trautmann - was completely different. This quartet has already released three impressive albums (the most recent, Timbre, on Boomslang, 2026) and offered its refined aesthetics that search for unexpected ties between abstract timbral invention, chamber art song format, and free improvisation, with elegant grace, organic interplay, and wit, always highlighting the four distinct voices. Hilde never chose familiar routes, and it explored coordinates of time and space with its own mysterious and thoughtful inner logic. There were some arresting musical games, especially when trombonist Trautmann contrasted Daniels’ warm and beautiful vocal delivery with her subversive, ironic trombone vocalization. The day ended at the Hoel Post with Schuster’s new quartet WOBBLE8 - baritone sax player Sofia Salvo (of Kuhn Fu), guitarist-vocalist Dan Peter Sundland (of Frank Gratkowski's Entrainmen, and Lina Allemano's Ohrenschmaus), vintage synth player Sebastian Pfeifer, and Schuster with a drum set with two pedals on the bass drum. This quartet prepares for the release of its debut album soon, The Moon is not there when nobody looks and exploded on the small stage with manic energy, propelled by Schuster’s massive, metal-like drumming, Salvo’s merciless Ayler-ian blows, Pfeifer’s prog-rock keyboard layers, and Sundland’s spiky guitar lines. The endless Dadaist-apocalyptic energy could supply enough electricity for the whole region for months. Looking forward to exploring WOBBLE8’s new album. 2nd Day, Aug.7 Austrian, New York-based Luisa Muhr opened the day’s program with an early performance of her conceptual work TEUFLIN/SHE-DEVIL (released on Boomslang, 2024), a feminine, irreverent interpretation of original, rich German texts from Goethe’s Faust, accompanied by cellist Elisabeth Coudoux and tenor sax player Jonathan Reisin, all dressed in black, and performing in the small church, Kloster Bezau. This work is based on a graphic score and questions the concept of "evil" from a female perspective, the separation of "good" and "evil," as it is particularly ingrained in Western traditions, and contemplates issues of life, death, and morality. It centers on Goethe’s phrase “Was glänzt, ist für den Augenblick geboren; / Das Echte bleibt der Nachwelt unverloren” (What dazzles, for the moment spends its spirit; / What’s genuine, shall Posterity inherit). Clearly, not the easiest issues to process early in the morning, but the wise, graceful performance of Muhr, Coudoux, and Reisin charmed and deeply moved the audience, some even to tears. Luckily, the next performance of the free improvising trio of Portuguese alto sax hero José Lencastre and bassist João Hasselberg and Danish master drummer Kresten Osgood changed the atmosphere. This trio released its debut album last year, This Anger is a Liar (Fundacja Słuchaj!; the title is taken from a song by Kip Hanrahan), and the performance suggested how three idiosyncratic and opinionated improvisers converse and explore the unique space of the local artist locksmith’s workshop, Kunstschmiede Figer, and its artifacts. Lencstre opted for exploring brief melodic and introspective ideas; Osgood, with a Ninja Turtles T-shirt, was, as usual, all over, playing his drum kit as if he was making love to it, with commanding pathos but equipped with a profound musical sensibility, provoking the audience with his eccentric antics, but completely bewitching all; and asselberg was torturing his bass guitar (titled “Lily”) with feedback sounds, aggressive hammering, and effects. Somehow it all made perfect sense, as the trio relied on its deep listening dynamics to search for uncharted timbres and resonances, even when Osgood sang solo the Hanrahan’s song. The performance ended with Hasselberg dismantling the neck of the guitar and rubbing the bass string against the pickups, offering a symbolic interpretation of Eric Dolphy's immortal saying: “When you hear music, after it's over, it's gone, in the air. You can never capture it again”. All left this performance with a big smile on their faces, agreeing that our world needs many more Krestens desperately. The afternoon performances returned to Hotel Post with a performance by the German, Cologne-based Philip Zoubek Trio - Zoubek on piano and synth, double bass player David Helm, and drummer-percussionist Dominik Mahnig. This trio has released five albums (including one in its electric version as Placebo Domingo) and is about to release its sixth one soon on Boomslang. It played a highly powerful set that highlighted its tight, inexhaustible, resonant kinetic-rhythmic energy as if it were a three-headed sonic entity, synchronized to the most minute detail, while following the intricate, composed score. Down at the SuBBwayZ, the futurist trio Meat.Karaoke.Quality.Time. - EWI and Moog synth players Florian Walter and Jan Klare, and Karl-F. Degenhardt on sensory and AI percussion, all dressed in black, as mad scientists from another planet. They cooked otherworldly - literally - weird but accessible sonic spices. Back in the Remise, Argentinian, Berlin-based tenor sax player Camila Nebbia presented her sextet, The Hanged One, inspired by the tarot card number 12, representing letting go, patience, reassessment, insight, and sacrifice, which is usually a symbol for new perspectives. This band: : cellist Julia Biłat, guitarist Arne Braun, electronics player Andres Marino, double bass player Vinicius Cajado, and drummer Lukas Akintaya, is about to release a new album by Relative Pitch. The sextet explored the tension between jazz-tinged composed parts with powerful grooves and experimental improvisation and timbral explorations, with Biłat and Marino more active on this edge. Nebbia encouraged individual, generous solos that allowed all ideas to be turned upside down, and new perspectives to emerge without fear of clash, but Nebbia’s economic, soulful solos glued all contrasting poles into an impressive, coherent statement. Next, at the same location, French drummer Edward Perraud presented his Sauvages Paradis (White Paradise) quartet - organ player and pianist Eve Risser (the leader of Red Desert Orchestra), flutist Delphine Joussein (of Nout trio and the Flöjter duo with Mats Gustafsson) and guitarist Arthur Delaleu. This collective quartet just released its criminally short debut album, Wild Thing (Gigantonium, 2026), and immediately captured the audience with its hyperactive, ever-inventive, and inspired sonic paradise. This quartet created cathartic, hypnotic, and trance-like textures that demonstrated how these resourceful improvisers keep feeding and pushing each other, with generous doses of humour, ecstatic storms, and dream-like, cosmic soundscapes. Perraud sang in gibberish, played on a strange guitar, Risser introduced North African meditative pulses on the piano, and Joussein transformed her flute into a mean, effects-laden electric guitar, and only Delaleu sat still as if the exhilarating sonic mayhem did not touch him. This quartet delivered on its promise from its album: “surrendering to the collective fever and opening yourself up to a journey of no return”. Day 3, Aug 8 The morning performance began with "Three men in a church with no Maria", the Littorina Saxophone Trio - Finnish Mikko Innanen, Swedish Fredrik Ljungkvist, and Lithuanian Liudas Mockūnas - playing within the beautiful acoustics of the ancient Kirche Reuthe, but without its founding member, Estonian Maria Faust, who had another engagement. This quartet of reed masters, who play the saxophone family, from the sopranino to the bass, is titled after the original name of the Baltic Sea and released a debut album last year. Leaking Pipes (NoBusiness, 2025). The touching, beautiful set stressed the profound, emphatic, and playful dynamics of this trio and its own independent aesthetics, rooted in Nordic folk motifs and European schools of modern jazz. Ljungkvist’s soulful, moving ballad “Nils-Olof”, dedicated to his father-in-law who passed away, and the trio’s interpretation of Ljungkvist's “Oslo”, were the highlights of this set, which could have been much, much longer, as far as the attentive audience cared. In the afternoon, Israeli-born, New York-based tenor sax player Jonathan Reisin presented his thought-provoking, complex compositions from his album Too Good X Unreality (Boomslang, 2025) at the Remise, with Korean-born, Amsterdam-based pianist Chaerin Im and Italian drummer Francesca Remigi (neither played on the album). Reisin introduces post-Cageian extended techniques and Steve Reich-like minimalism, and his sax playing and his compositions suggest a distant, sober, often even ironic perspective on the jazz legacy. This performance allowed his demanding, intricate compositions to blossom with the new voices of Im and Remigi, and often Reisin simply stood aside and enjoyed how they breathed new, unpredictable fresh air into his ideas, letting this ad-hoc trio push the boundaries of its instruments. At the same location, Finnish, Berlin-based guitarist Kalle Kalima presented his new trio Detours, with German drummer Christian Lillinger (who plays with Kalima in the KUU! quartet) and Argentinian, Brooklyn-based keyboard player Leo Genovese, who played the Hammond organ, Crumar electric piano, Korg synth, and piano. This trio was formed in the 2025 edition of the Saalfelden Jazz Festival, but this was one of its first-ever performances, and music was composed, focusing on the high-energy, dense, and physical rhythmic outputs of these gifted, versatile improvisers, with little variance in the radical, electric textures. But there were times that I could swear that Genovese had at least four hands, if not much more. The night ended at the same location with the first-ever performance of the Vanish trio - the one and only American vocal artist Shelley Hirsch, Swiss master double bass player Christian Weber, and master drummer Alfred Vogel. This trio released its debut album earlier this year on Boomslang that revolved around Hirsch’s stream of thoughts, observations, insights, and stories. It was clear from the first moment that Hirsch is a natural on stage, with a deeply sensual, touching presence that immediately bewitched the audience, as well as Weber and Vogel, who kept challenging her with fragmented rhythmic patterns. Hirsch transformed this performance into a funny, moving, and thoughtful love letter to the festival, to the appreciative audience, and especially to the “beautiful white-haired women of Bezau” and to Weber and Vogel. She did so with a remarkable, commanding ability to shape the English and the German languages to her needs, with amusing onomatopoeic games, and poetic quotes from jazz standards. I hope that this trio will find more opportunities to explore its great potential. Day 4, Aug. 9 The festival ended with a morning performance at the Remise with a guest band from a twin festival in Porto, Portugal. Portuguese, Amsterdam-based Vocal artist and composer Vera Morais presented her new quintet EUPNEA - with vocalists Līva Dumpe, Sarah van Eijk, and flutists Teresa Costa and Ketija Ringa-Karahona - that just released a debut album. Morais’ compositions offer a beautiful, touching synergy of breath, air, and vocal pitches, flirting with contemporary music and influences of Meredith Monk ensembles, and encapsulate the quintet as a human organ that explores highly immersive chamber music. Morais is a creative force worth following. Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook

items.body: Eye New Dark Adore self-released Eye New Dark is the solo project of Null Device’s Jill Sheridan, and while it shares that modern synthpop act’s lushness and melodic bent, departs from it in some interesting ways. Sheridan has always been a powerful vocalist with excellent control and feeling, and the major contrast in the material on Adore is in hearing her over some more bright and even brash sounding material. Single “Backwards Through That Door” features spritely synth arpegios and peppy drum programming, with Sheridan riding the beat, choosing her spots to move into her upper range for emphasis, the phrasing as important to the song’s feeling as any given sound design element. Similarly, when she sings on the rhumba-beat driven “Real Life”, its her clarity and measured performance that allows her to cut through the brushy percussion sounds, big pads and swelling bells, recalling some of OMD’s more baroque moments. Perhaps the most revelatory moment is closer “Eyes in the Dark”, a track that is musically designed around a sort of stop-start rhythmic movement, the spaces between each small burst of instrumentation smoothed by the lush and layered vocal recordings, filling the space without crowding it. It’s a lovely collection of tracks that shows off versatile takes modern and classic synthpop styles, driven by a genuinely skilled performance. Adore by Eye New Dark Circa Tapes Climbers LVLZ You’ll always be getting a slightly rejiggered formulation of the styles and influences which shape Adam Sieczka’s work as Circa Tapes every time you check in with it, and new EP Climbers is no exception in that regard. Traces of left-field pop and post-punk, along with some of the project’s longstanding interest in minimal wave can still be found in the corners of these four tracks, but it’s a dark and metallic approach to body music rhythms which holds sway (Ortrotasce might be the only other current American act pulling from the same corners, though the trajectories of the projects have been quite different). The metallic reverb which swirls above the snares of “Pulse Fate” might connote either vintage Underworld or possibly Sieczka’s previous work in Kill Memory Crash, while the smoky and dense waves of feedback chopped into “Stukka”‘s acidic EBM brings the underrated work of European experimentalists NTRSN to mind. Colour, funk, and a distinctly American sardonicism blur the jagged edges of Climbers‘ beats. Climbers by Circa Tapes The post Observer: Eye New Dark & Circa Tapes appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._genre: synthpop / minimal wave / EBM / darkwave
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑评介了两组独立电子音乐人的新作品。Eye New Dark 是 Null Device 主唱 Jill Sheridan 的个人项目，在合成器流行框架内展现了歌手的演唱功力——清澈的声线在明亮的合成琶音与活泼的鼓机节奏之上灵活游走，收尾曲以断续节奏配合层次丰沛的人声堆叠，营造出精妙的留白感。Circa Tapes 的 EP 则走向更暗的领域，金属质感混响缠绕军鼓，酸性 EBM 节拍与浓密反馈波浪交织，将后朋克、左翼流行与极简暗潮元素熔于一炉，呈现出鲜明的美式冷峻讽刺气质。两组作品均为独立或自发行，评论文字对声音设计细节着墨较多。整体来看，这些作品在合成器流行的躯壳内融入了暗潮与工业元素，对偏好电子与暗潮交叉领域的听众具有较高参考价值。

items.body:
Techgnostic pied piper of Latin club, Tra Tra Trax co-founder Verraco hustles a class handful of techno, electro and hard groove bustlers for German compilation series The Third Room.

The Colombian producer-DJ takes The Third Room’s brief, to create a “place where different cultures existing and correlating to each other, mix and transform into hybrids” his own way, after precedents laid by Oscar Mulero, Freddy K, and GiGi FM, among others.

An exclusive ’Stone Version’ of Substance & Vainqueur’s 2007 dub techno ace ‘Libration’ opens a set spanning Skee Mask’s frisky deep techno swanger ‘Clear Sky 909’, thru the shearing sound design of Verraco’s own ‘Untitled (Teamgeist Mix)’, to the polyrhythmic hard groove charge of LA’s 1morning, and compatible tackle of ‘PatumPa’ by Monterrey, Mexico’s Regal86.
items._genre: techno / electro / hard groove / dub techno
items._cn_summary: 哥伦比亚制作人Verraco为德国The Third Room厂牌策划的混音合辑，延续了Oscar Mulero、Freddy K等前辈的策展理念。他从Skee Mask的灵动深度 techno、Substance & Vainqueur经典的2007年dub techno名作，以及自己带有尖锐声音设计的作品，到LA硬groove制作人1morning与墨西哥Regal86的多层次节奏作品，编织出一套横跨拉丁俱乐部根源与欧洲工业传统的选曲脉络。Verraco以拉丁俱乐部的文化视角重新诠释techno谱系，将地域碎片与电子舞曲的历史层叠拼贴，呈现出一种带有混血特质的俱乐部美学。整体内容偏新闻稿式介绍，缺少深入的声音分析与艺术评论，信息密度有限，但选曲视角本身具有一定的跨界实验价值。

items.body:
Since everyone else has written something about the centennials of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, why not join the parade? It is a good opportunity to look at the timeline of bassists the legendary trumpeter and saxophonist used. Born just under four months apart, the pair worked together under the elder Davis’ name periodically between Fall 1955 and Spring 1957 before a more steady affiliation in 1958-1960.

It is in that latter period that this analysis will begin, as it gives a convenient bit of serendipity: the fact that two of the their most famed albums were made in that period, Davis’ Kind Blue (March 2nd and April 22nd, 1959 for Columbia) and Coltrane’s Giant Steps (May 4th–5th and December 2nd, 1959). And the analysis will end with Coltrane’s death in 1967, which came during the tenure of Davis’ “second great quintet” and before his groups swelled and electrified during his fusion period.

As such, we begin with the same man, the bassist on both those albums: Paul Chambers. He had taken up the bass a decade earlier in his adopted home of Detroit (where he was a student at the seminal Cass Technical High School ... more on that later). He arrived in New York in 1954 at 19. By the time of Kind of Blue and Giant Steps, he had been on over 100 sessions from dozens of leaders, with multiple dates under Davis (with whom he had started working in late 1955) and Coltrane (who had used him for several albums in 1957-58 as well as both fellow sideman for many others and Chambers also hiring Coltrane for his own sessions). In addition to the five albums he led, Chambers played on sessions for Benny Golson, Curtis Fuller, J.J. Johnson, Lee Morgan, Red Garland, Sonny Clark, and Sonny Rollins.

The collaboration between Davis and Chambers was remarkably fruitful before and after Kind of Blue and solidified a part of Davis’ music that had previously seen widely differing players like Tommy Potter, Oscar Pettiford, Al McKibbon, and Percy Heath. The rest of 1959 saw multiple engagements around the country and closed with recordings that would be part of another monumental record, Sketches of Spain, that paired Davis’ group with the Gil Evans Orchestra. 1960 continued that momentum with more Sketches of Spain recording and almost non-stop touring, including two stretches in Europe, from Spring onward. 1961 and 1962 had more of the same activity, the documents being Someday My Prince Will Come and Quiet Nights. Then, quite suddenly, Chambers left Davis’ group in early February 1963.

It should be stated that Chambers did not restrict his activities solely to Davis, recording over four dozen albums during the period with, among many others, Jackie McLean, Wynton Kelly, Benny Golson, Hank Mobley, and Curtis Fuller. And after leaving Davis, he worked steadily with an array of leaders through the end of 1968, sadly passing away from tuberculosis caused and/or aggravated by drug abuse at only 33.

Stepping right into the Davis group was another Cass Technical High School alumnus: Ron Carter. Nearly 26, Carter was already prophesying his prolific career, participating in over three dozen albums since 1960, with the likes of Charli Persip, Yusef Lateef, Eric Dolphy, Don Ellis, Coleman Hawkins, Cecil Payne, Jaki Byard, Wes Montgomery, Bobby Timmons, Tadd Dameron, Dizzy Reece, Ken McIntyre, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson and others, plus waxing his leader debut, Where?, for Prestige subsidiary New Jazz in 1961.

It was Carter’s arrival that heralded Davis’ soon-to-be seminal band, though it took until Fall 1964 for its personnel to solidify. With Carter, Davis recorded Seven Steps To Heaven and played the Antibes festival in 1963. What is interesting though is while the “second great quintet” is thought of as a monolith, the bass chair had some upheaval/fluidity, depending on how you look at it. Gary Peacock – already a veteran and likely the only person to work for both Bud Shank and Albert Ayler – took the chair for nearly six weeks in the spring of 1964, Carter returning thereafter through the end of the year. 1965 began auspiciously with the January recording of E.S.P. but then things derailed with a convalescing Davis unable to play. And when he could, in November and December, Carter, a hot commodity, was absent, spelled by Peacock once more, then Reggie Workman, who had come up around the same time as Carter and had already come and gone in the groups of Coltrane. In 1966, Carter would return to the group but only partially, participating in East Coast performances, shows elsewhere having either Richard Davis, Carter’s only real equal in terms of fecundity, or in the Peacock mold of eclecticism, Eddie Gomez, returning permanently in October, just before the album Miles Smiles. 1967 was similar: Carter was on board when not busy elsewhere, Gomez on call, then Albert Stinson for one show (a little over two years before his passing – see Bass Tragedies column in Issue 94) and then another veteran, Buster Williams, for a tour (and playing on one track of the 1981-released compilation album Directions). Carter would fill a fixed point for all of 1967, including the albums Sorcerer and Nefertiti and would continue with Davis through the middle of 1968.

Like Chambers or perhaps even more so, Carter was also on the greater jazz scene during his tenure with Davis. He recorded on sessions led by his fellow Davis bandmates but also by everyone from Bobby Timmons, Charles Lloyd, Donald Byrd and Bobby Hutcherson to Jimmy Smith, Shirley Scott, Eddie Harris, and Stanley Turrentine, to name only a handful. He has, of course, gone on to be likely the most recorded bassist in jazz history.

Paul Chambers’ time under Coltrane was shorter and more intermittent. After Giant Steps he was part of, along with the rest of Davis’ period band, November 1959 recordings that would partly comprise Coltrane Jazz and be brought back 18 months later as one of three individual bassists taking part in the Africa/Brass recordings (though his contribution was only heard on the 1995 complete sessions version).

Also in 1959 was a Birdland engagement for Coltrane where either Ahmed Abdul-Malik or George Tucker, both established and close in age to Coltrane, were on bass.

In 1960 Coltrane hired the slightly younger Steve Davis in what seems to be his first professional engagement. Davis stayed in the band through the end of the year for all its live dates and played on music recorded in October and released piecemeal on My Favorite Things, Coltrane Jazz, Coltrane Plays the Blues, and Coltrane’s Sound. Though Davis lived until 1987, his credits after Coltrane were slight: the Mangione Brothers, Dave Burns, McCoy Tyner, Kenny Dorham, James Moody, Freddie McCoy, and Eddie Jefferson, all made in the ‘60s. One deviation in the year came via Coltrane’s shared date with Don Cherry, The Avant-Garde, where bass was handled by either Charlie Haden or Percy Heath.

1961 was a year in flux, bassist-wise, for Coltrane. He introduced a concept to which he would return later in the decade by using two bassists for an engagement at Chicago’s Sutherland Lounge in March: Raphael Don Garrett and Workman, the former, about six years younger, working with Roland Kirk, Paul Serrano, and Eddie Harris, the latter 11 years younger, sideman for Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd, Duke Jordan, Richard Williams, and Dave Pike.

Workman would be part of the aforementioned Africa/Brass, as would, separately, another bassist, Art Davis, already with credits under Max Roach, Lee Morgan, Booker Little, Hal Mooney, Ernestine Anderson, Dizzy Gillespie, Leo Wright, Clifford Jordan/Sonny Red, Abbey Lincoln, and Booker Little. But in May they were together for Ole Coltrane and nearly a month at the Village Vanguard in August. Workman would become the fixed bassist for Coltrane through the end of the year for concerts, including a European tour, and a small portion of the Ballads album from the end of the year. An exception was Workman either alternating or alongside Jimmy Garrison for a November stint at the Village Vanguard.

If not for a family health crisis forcing Workman to leave the group at the end of 1961 and return to his native Philadelphia, he likely would have stayed with the band and jazz history been quite different. It should be said that Workman hardly is a footnote, becoming one of the most revered players of his generation. But it was Garrison who became the anchor. Born between Garrett and Workman, prior to joining Coltrane he had worked with Philly Joe Jones, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Dorham, Jackie McLean, JR Montrose, Walter Bishop, Jr., Ornette Coleman, Bill Barron, and Ted Curson.

Unlike Carter and Davis, once Garrison was on board, he stayed there. That was mostly to do with Coltrane’s packed schedule of touring and albums and that, unlike Davis, he was healthy and non-combustible. From 1962-1964, Garrison was omnipresent, including the bulk of Ballads, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane (where he split duties with Ellington’s period bassist Aaron Bell), 2018 discovery Both Directions At Once, John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman, Impressions, Crescent, another new millennium unearthed gem in Blue World, and closing out the year with Coltrane’s magnum opus A Love Supreme (which added Art Davis for a second day of recording, released as a second disc to the album’s deluxe edition in 2002).

In 1965 Garrison was still the main man but occasionally Davis would be alongside him: partially on The John Coltrane Quartet Plays in February and fully for June’s Ascension. Otherwise, Garrison was the sole bassist for performances and most of the other albums: Transition, Sun Ship, and Meditations. The exceptions without Davis were overdubs of Haden for the posthumously released Infinity and Garrett returning to play both bass and clarinet for Live In Seattle (as well as the 2021 archival release A Love Supreme: Live In Seattle), Om, and part of Kulu Se Mama.

1966 was even more Garrison-centric, with the only documented work including a second bassist shows in November and December with Lionel “Sonny” Johnson, the brother of Dewey Johnson, who had played on Ascension. The last year of Coltrane’s life, Garrison was there as well, with one notable absence: the Coltrane/Rashied Ali duet Interstellar Space.

Unlike Chambers or Carter, Garrison was kept so busy during his time with Coltrane that his outside discography at the time is meager, though it does include his sole leader date, Illumination! with the Elvin Jones/Jimmy Garrison Sextet. Otherwise it was sessions with Lorez Alexandria, Coltrane bandmate McCoy Tyner, Sonny Rollins, Bill Dixon, and Robert F. Pozar.

After Coltrane’s death, Garrison kept working but his documentation slowed, his two Blue Note dates with the Jones trio rounded out by Joe Farrell being the most enduring. There were also dates with Rolf and Joachim Kuhn, Clifford Thornton and Nathan Davis, and regular work with Alice Coltrane and Archie Shepp. His final recording came in early 1975 with Beaver Harris and Dave Burrell’s 360 Degree Music Experience. Garrison died of lung cancer in 1976 at 42.

items.body:
1970 (April 10th, 1970 – IBC Studios, London)

Negotiations were now underway between Sean Murphy and several labels including Deram, CBS and Harvest, the EMI sub-label that had distributed Volume Two in the UK and already had Kevin Ayers in its stable. “They are still not an attraction in the very top bracket, so it was a pleasant surprise to see major companies throwing in genuinely massive bids earlier this year when the group was looking for a recording deal,” Richard Williams revealed. Ultimately, Soft Machine signed with CBS, but Third was self-financed, taken partly from studio sessions, but also from live recordings (“Facelift”) and edits and loops of tapes made by Mike Ratledge and Hugh Hopper at the home of Bob Woolford, who had let them use his Brenell and Stellavox tape recorders. Such infringements of accepted professional practices were only possible because CBS, having acquired a finished album, were no longer in a position to force the band to comply with them.

The benefit for Soft Machine in terms of artistic freedom is easy to measure. But this has to be balanced against the fact that the production on Third is, to put it bluntly, an unmitigated disaster. IBC, at the time the studio of choice for such notorious perfectionists as The Who and the Bee Gees, are probably less to blame than the band themselves who, in spite of the issues with Volume Two, are again credited as sole producers. The sound suffers from almost constantly saturated low frequencies and extremely vague mediums, the drums are much too low in the mix, as if played behind a closed door; and the organ is deprived of much of its biting impact through overwhelming equalization. Unfortunately the 2007 remaster, while an improvement, fails to rectify this.

What is problematic is that, as well as making the album an uncomfortable listen, its sub-par production lessens the claim, widely held at the time of its release, that Third represented musical state-of-the-art. This claim was based on Soft Machine’s ability, unparalleled among their contemporaries, to draw from and amalgamate an exceptionally wide range of influences. Starting out as a rock band, and then gradually moving towards jazz to invent a uniquely personal, and absolutely valid, British answer to American fusion, Soft Machine went even further, incorporating the influence of Stockhausen’s avant-garde and Terry Riley’s repetitive minimalism. Third’s ‘total’ vision, encompassing the entire spectrum of known musical genres, placed Soft Machine at the forefront of musical “progress” in 1970. However, horizons have since expanded to such an extent, beyond the Western tradition in particular, that this concept of universality has aged considerably.

In his insightful review of Third for Actuel, Paul Alessandrini wrote of “music to really listen to, no longer aiming for a purely physical vibration, more interiorized. Soft Machine have re-thought their musical influences – Riley, Cecil Taylor, Coltrane – to really make them their own, abandoning their aesthetics of random explosion in favor of a much more thought-out approach.” There are still occasional reminders of these sonic excesses that, as Alessandrini noted, had now largely disappeared from their music. Mike Ratledge's lengthy solo introduction to “Facelift” almost sounds like an electric exorcism, as if to rid Soft Machine of what still remains of that violence in order to reinvent their music in a more controlled manner, setting formal perfection as their new objective.

Considered as a whole, Hugh Hopper's piece represents the last remnant of Soft Machine’s early days, when they still favored spirit over form - here found lacking in both sound quality and performance, with a few train wrecks along the way - and were intent on disregarding the accepted rules. “Facelift” includes free sections increasingly at odds with Ratledge’s preoccupation with structure – and while as a keyboard player, he still embodies the band’s more radical leanings, Ratledge’s own compositions reveal a much less iconoclastic temperament. Hopper described his own approach at the time as “halfway between” that of Dean, “whose thing is really total improvisation, without any structure, and on the other extreme, [that of Ratledge] who's into entirely formalized musical forms.

“Moon in June” completes Robert Wyatt’s donation to Soft Machine of the material originally intended for his first solo album in 1968. It is interesting to note that Wyatt does this at the exact point where Soft Machine had shed any remaining reference to pop in their live repertoire. Looking back, Wyatt was certainly justified in saying that his side of Third was “the last chance I had to use all the things we'd done without being a jazz band. I wanted to get twenty minutes of it down somewhere.” And since his colleagues, reluctant to act as mere accompanists, had made no secret of their lack of interest in his songs, he recorded most of “Moon in June” on his own, repeating the modus operandi of the 1968-69 demo. Hugh Hopper and Mike Ratledge’s participation is again limited to the organ solo halfway through (Hopper also plays a short melodic theme earlier in the piece). Elton Dean wasn’t asked to contribute anything – Wyatt’s unconvincing justification being that he “hadn’t yet worked out how to work on [his] stuff with the added wind instruments.”

As there was no mention of this breach of band discipline in the sleeve notes, only the most astute listeners noticed that the organ heard during the first ten minutes was a Hammond rather than Ratledge’s signature Lowrey, that the playing clearly wasn’t Ratledge’s, and that most of the ‘bass’ parts were played on an electric piano. When the truth was finally revealed, Wyatt gave contradictory versions of what had happened – in one interview claiming that Ratledge and Hopper had “refused to play [on “Moon in June”] and I had to play it all myself,” in another that he’d “almost had to force them to get them to play on it, which I thought was rather unfair as I’d done my best to get into the music they were writing.” Probably the most objective and believable of Wyatt’s rationales was that he was “terrified it’d be played wrong” if he didn’t perform it all himself.

To approach “Moon in June” as a ‘message’ song would misrepresent Wyatt’s more mundane intent, insofar as the phonetic qualities of the words often seem to matter more to him than their meaning. In other words, “Moon in June” is above all a musical composition, a suite of instrumental sections, some of which are adorned with melodies and lyrics, and others not. The singing accompanies the music rather than vice-versa. In this respect, outside of a possible rivalry with Elton Dean and Wyatt’s inability to sing while drumming, there was no theoretical incompatibility between Soft Machine’s move towards jazz and the continued presence of Wyatt’s voice (even if limited to the Echoplexed scat singing of his solitary interludes during the band’s concerts). Dispensing with vocals was the single most questionable move in Soft Machine’s entire musical evolution, not to mention one whose commercial consequences cannot be underestimated. In different circumstances, Hugh Hopper would surely have joined Wyatt in lobbying for having at least some vocals, but in addition to his increasingly strained personal relationship with Wyatt, Hopper had at this point completely lost interest in non-instrumental music. “I find that using the human voice means asserting limitations to your music right from the start”, he explained in 1972. “I am more interested in the sounds generated by instruments, or electronic devices, because the possibilities offered by songs are much more limited than when experimenting with sounds.”

Even if there was no future for singing in Soft Machine, “Moon in June” at least offers evidence that Robert Wyatt, in a voice-free context, could still be more than “a session drummer for an interesting new species of jazz groups,” as long as he contributed to the writing. When it came to extended pieces, he could stand comparison with Mike Ratledge, even though he lacked any comparable academic background. In addition to its constant melodic inspiration, “Moon in June” is very skillfully constructed (indeed, its instrumental architecture had remained intact since 1968), and confirms Wyatt’s seemingly innate talent for making a coherent whole out of ill-assorted musical ideas.

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评详细剖析了Soft Machine第三张专辑《Third》的制作背景与音乐价值。乐队在与多家厂牌谈判后签约CBS，凭借已完成的作品获得了创作自由，专辑素材来源于录音棚、现场演出以及成员在家用磁带机上制作的循环片段。在音乐上，Soft Machine从摇滚出发，逐步融入爵士元素，试图构建一种融合Stockhausen先锋音乐与Terry Riley简约主义的英式综合视野。然而，乐评尖锐指出专辑的混音制作堪称灾难——低频饱和、中频模糊、鼓声被压制、管风琴失去穿透力，连2007年的再版也未能彻底修复。尽管如此，乐评肯定了Third在1970年所代表的音乐前沿意义，认可其将爵士、摇滚与先锋音乐融为一体的实验精神。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了70至80年代圣多美与普林西比群岛的音乐，延续了第一卷的方向。乐评首先介绍了当地特殊的地理与历史背景——两个小岛曾是葡萄牙殖民地，音乐风格Puxa融合了来自其他非洲葡语国家的节奏以及merengue、Kompas、Soukouss等元素，据说舞蹈可以召唤灵魂或驱除邪灵。合辑收录15首作品，展示了Puxa的典型编排：多重吉他交织盘旋，主唱与和声交替呼应，乐器层让位于绵长的律动。Pedro Lima的乐队在《Sossegado》中以闷音吉他与鼓组对峙；Sangazuza的曲目展示了贝斯与键盘退出后鼓手与吉他如何主导律动；Africa Negra的作品则展现了Puxa现场演出中音乐如何持续数小时。整张专辑由瑞士独立小厂牌Bongo Joe发行，聚焦一个被边缘化但风格丰富的非洲音乐场景。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的这张专辑以中提琴、簧风琴、击弦古钢琴和钢琴为核心乐器，部分曲目加入鼓、贝斯与合成器，大量采用即兴演奏与一次性录音完成，营造出朦胧、神秘、近乎宗教冥想式的氛围。评论特别提及三首作品：约翰·克莱尔诗作谱曲的《I Am!》在持续低鸣中展开超凡旋律；《Sprigs of Heather》以中世纪圣咏开篇转为钢琴主导的缓慢级进，被视为整张专辑的精华；《The Final Harvest》则是关于父亲最后一次探访他所钟爱的菜园之作，饱含深情。专辑同时是 Cotton 父亲于 2024 年底去世后的纪念之作，悲伤情绪贯穿始终。光与暗在曲中交替渗透，风格游离于民谣、前卫与古典之间，不刻意归类却自成一体。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: Analog Africa厂牌推出的第44号发行，收录贝宁歌手Antoine Dougbé与Orchestre Poly-Rythmo于1977至1982年间合作的作品。Dougbé以其独特的Cavacha节奏——由打击乐手Belobi Meridjo从火车节奏启发而来——闻名，录音生涯虽短仅三张专辑加几张单曲，却展现出强劲的创作力量。音乐融合伏都教仪式元素、古巴son影响以及当时席卷撒哈拉以南非洲的刚果伦巴，合成器与闪亮吉他交织在高帽主导的律动之上，音色因年代而带有塑料质感。贝宁作为非洲音乐场景中相对小众的地区，以及Analog Africa这一专注于挖掘非洲复古音乐的独立厂牌，使此合辑在世界音乐领域具有独特的文化档案价值。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 这是挪威Camilla Hole Trio继融合科幻合成器与民间素材的前作之后的最新录音，整体回归更为脚踏实地的方向，但仍延续了对本国传统音乐之外素材的探寻。主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，爵士影响显著，曲目源自挪威西部的传统舞蹈音乐。乐评以开场曲为例详述了三人组的演奏逻辑：Hole先以萨克斯陈述旋律，Kalman与Nesheim以贝斯与鼓提供节奏支撑，随后叠加模块合成器与颤音琴增添色彩；而该三重奏的特质在于角色分配始终流动不定，Kalman的中低音贝斯会接过旋律与萨克斯齐奏，Nesheim则进一步拓展节奏维度，作品在反复陈述旋律之间逐步走向自由的即兴展开。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 三位来自挪威与瑞典的乐手以传统舞曲为素材，却并未追求适合舞蹈的常规演出，而是将其转化为私密、克制的室内乐对话。竖笛手主导旋律，小提琴手提供流动或抽象的音色纹理，鼓手则以细微声响拓展节奏。评论尤其指出作品会突然解体、停滞，借此揭示北欧舞曲表面欢快之下所隐含的阴暗、神秘与不安，使传统旋律获得偏向现代作曲和自由即兴的重新诠释。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家 Omar Sosa 在意大利法奇奥里音乐厅完成两小时独奏即兴录音，后期加入人声采样、打击乐、循环音效与田野录音，形成以钢琴为核心的即兴专辑。他主张打破风格分类，拒绝被流媒体算法与市场逻辑框定，强调首遍即兴录制的直觉感与自然性。专辑强调精神共鸣，借鉴蒙古呼麦概念，融合古巴传统与自由爵士元素。从开篇《Inside the Spirit》的琴弦拨弄与共振探索出发，作品展现出冥想式的创作姿态。整体属于跨文化即兴钢琴范畴，兼具世界音乐底色与实验精神。

バスクラリネットは不思議な楽器だ。アンサンブルの一員として加わっただけで、ビロードのような深い底光りが全体を一変させる。エリック・ドルフィーのソロにとどまらず、ギル・エヴァンス、ストラヴィンスキーやラヴェルなどのオーケストレーションの低音域で輝きをみせ、ほんのわずかなパッセージ のソロでも深い印象を残す。肉声に近い息づかいであっても、似た音域のベースやバリトン・サックスとはぜんぜん違う。人が発する音を真のヴォイスに昇華できるこの楽器に心を奪われた方は多いはずだ。

八巻志帆が「ソロバスクラリネットの音楽家」として傑出した個性を発揮した新作が『EVOKE』 。

「私はジャズプレイヤーでもクラシックプレイヤーでもなく、自分自身をソロバスクラリネット奏者と名乗っています。『EVOKE』では、これまでの人生の旅のなかで、美しい音楽だな、とか、こういう形でバスクラリネットのサウンドを知って欲しいな、と思った曲を素直に揃えました。」（本人のライナーより）

八巻のアルバム作りの出発点はクラシック楽曲を中心としたファースト『Bassclarinet Recital』（2009）だ。セカンド『My Sweet Hometown』（2014）では童謡からキース・ジャレットまで懐かしい情景をキュレート。サードにあたる前作『HAZAMA』 （2018） は全てが自作曲で、続く『EVOKE』が４枚目のリーダー作となる。全てALM コジマ録音。

「２本のバスクラリネットのためのプロジェクト」として八巻以外に中村奈央〈バスクラリネット〉、柳原由佳〈ピアノ〉、伊東佑季〈ベース〉、則武諒〈ドラム〉が参加。
フロントの２バスクラ＋ピアノトリオという編成はジャズ的だ。しかし、一聴するとジャズだけではない個性に満ちた成り立ちが分かる。バスクラゆえに曲調が一変して各曲が持つさまざまなユニークネスが浮かび上がる。そして、ワンテイクで録られたよう迫真性が胸を打つ。

もう一人のバスクラプレイヤー中村奈央の音楽はアグレッシヴでありながら、八巻と競い合うことはなく、時にまるで分身のような錯覚までを引き起こす。二人だけの２曲のデュオでの相互作用は美しいドッペルゲンガーのよう。他の楽器ではありえない音響的愉悦に富んだサウンドだ。

全９曲は静かな表情の２曲で始まる。バスクラの２本のみの２曲、５曲目からはさまざまに劇的な展開が訪れ、ふたたび静かに幕を閉じる。「バスクラリネットのサウンドを知って欲しい」というメッセージが見事に体現されている。

カヴァーの７曲は八巻が世代的にリアルタイムで接したと思われるラインナップだ。「これまでの人生の旅のなかで出会った音楽」。

オープニング（01.）はイギリスのオルタナティブ・ロックとして知られるコールドプレイの <Viva la Vida>（美しい生命　２００８）。オリジナルとは異なり驚くほど繊細な表情を見せる。（03.）スティーヴン・フェルヘルスト<Devil’s Waltz>（悪魔のワルツ）はバストロンボーンのためのテクニカルな「ツーボトム」楽曲をバスクラにリアレンジ。（04.）アメリカの作曲家マーク・メリッツの <Black> も木管二重奏のバージョンがオリジナル。（03.）と（04.）の二曲はバスクラ二本のみの演奏。一転して、（06.）リシャール・ガリアーノ <SERTAO> はガリアーノが　ビレリ・ラグレーン（G）とニューヨークに乗り込んで凄腕のジャズミュージシャンたちと作ったアルバム『New York Tango』から。八巻たちのプレイもガリアーノの高いテンションを引き継いでアルバム中のハイライトのひとつだ。（07.）<Time After Time> （タイム・アフター・タイム）はシンディー・ローパーのオリジナル（１９８４）。というより後期マイルス・デイヴィスがカヴァーし、ライヴでも名演奏を重ねた曲。２本のバスクラのアレンジと演奏はマイルスとも異なり、ユニークそのもの。八巻はどちらのバージョンにインスパイアされたのだろうか。

４曲の自作では（02.）<Dolphins> ２バスクラのみによる穏やかなテンポ、静かな展開が美しい。（05.）<Ditto+> 八巻と中村のコンビネーションが光る。作曲とアレンジが渾然一体となったオリジナル。（08.）<mélancolie manège>（憂鬱な回転木馬）はリシャール・ガリアーノ作曲の <SERTAO> 以上にガリアーノ的。さらに背後には、『HAZAMA』で２曲を取り上げたアストル・ピアソラの影響がありそうだ。メランコリーと陰影に満ちて、絡み合う２本のバスクラの表情は豊かで、インスピレーションとアドリブ性が迸る。前作よりの曲を再録したのは大きな意味がある。（09.）<For>  ふたりのバスクラから聞こえる呼吸すらが楽しい。八巻の作曲、アレンジ独自の静謐な世界だ。

最近、特殊楽器に転じた音楽家からきいた愉快な話。
彼は都内の楽器店の片隅で「今はじめればパイオニア」という傑作キャッチコピーを発見してふるい立ったそうだ。
もっとも、「そんなキャッチが出回る頃には、もうパイオニアになれないんですけどね（笑）」とも言っていたが。
パイオニアを目指すことが彼らのエナジーの源泉だ。王道の路線から１８０度舵を切り、新しい視座から未知のフィールドに乗り出していく。
例えば１７世紀フランスの牧歌趣味（pastorale）のバグパイプの一種「ミュゼット」（いわゆるパリのアコーディオン音楽ではなく、その源流のひとつです）、ロシア、トゥヴァ共和国の喉歌「フーメイ」（モンゴルのホーメーと似ているけれど、かなり違います）などなど。
歴史の中で忘れ去られていた楽器、世界の辺境に置き去りにされた音楽。絶滅危惧種を救い出して、自らが伝道師となり、一生がかりで追求する。そんなフレッシュな感性を持つ若い音楽家に出会うのは愉しい。

もちろんバスクラは１９世紀後半には、すでにオーケストラの中でポジションを確立しているので「特殊楽器」ではないけれど。現代において一般に「バスクラ奏者」とはクラシックや吹奏楽のオーケストラに所属するトッププレイヤーたち。あるいは（楽器持ち替えを含む）ジャズなどの腕利きの演奏家を意味する。

他方、中学生の時に偶然に巡り合い、この楽器の魅力にとらわれた八巻。その後、現在まで音楽ジャンルにとらわれない貴重なソロ楽器として位置づけ、追求しているのは十分「特殊」なことだ。

八巻志帆は「ソロバスクラリネット奏者」としてこの楽器だけが表現できる新しい地平を切り拓いている。「EVOKE」とは呼び起こすこと。バスクラリネットの音色が呼び起こすイメージはあまりにも蠱惑的だ。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以两支巴塞单簧管为核心，辅以钢琴三重奏的室内编制，呈现九首跨越多种风格的曲目。曲单横跨酷玩乐队、辛迪·劳帕等流行作品的爵士化改编，加利亚诺的探戈语汇，以及巴塞单簧管改编的古典二重奏作品。自作曲展现了八巻志丰作为独奏巴塞单簧管演奏者的音乐脉络，从童年歌谣到基斯·贾勒特再到阿斯托尔·皮亚佐拉的影响。两支低音单簧管的声部交织形成独特音色共鸣，配合钢琴、贝斯与鼓，在现场一次录制的紧迫感中完成。整张专辑从安静开场、经历多样戏剧性展开，最终以静谧方式收束，完整呈现了低音单簧管这一乐器的表现潜能与独特音色魅力。

items.body:
CD/DVD DISKS
NO. 340
#2448 『ギドン・ヌネス・ファズ~カール＝マーティン・アルムクヴィスト／池の中のかわず』『Gidon Nunes Vaz～Karl-Martin Almqvist Quintet / Frogs In A Pond』
2026年8月15日
常見登志夫　

text: Toshio Tsunemi  常見登志夫

Gidon Nunes Vaz ¥3,410（税込） 6月23日発売（ディスクユニオン）
※Sound Liaisonレーベルで2027年秋、DXD (Digital eXtreme Definition)フォーマットでのCDを発売予定
https://diskunion.net/jazz/ct/detail/1009229301

Gidon Nunes Vaz (tp,flh)
Karl-Martin Almqvist (ss,ts)
Timothy Banchet (p,fender rhodes)
Cas Jiskoot (b)
Martijn Vink (ds)

1. FROGS IN A POND
2. SHORTER’S BRUSH
3. GALAXEN
4. YUGEN
5. BLUES FOR MARA
6. STILTJE
7. WE ALL KNOW
8. CPH

Produced by Gidon Nunes Vaz, Karl-Martin Almqvist and Peter Björnild,
a cooperation with Sound Liaison
Recorded at the MCO Studio 2, Hilversum, The Netherlands on September 5th, 2025
Recording, mixing and mastering by Frans de Rond
Cover design by Pontus Dahlström
Cover photos by Zofia Niewcas

オランダの若きトランペット/フリューゲルホーン奏者、ギドン・ヌネス・ファズ Gidon Nunes Vazと、スウェーデン出身のベテランサックス奏者、カール＝マーティン・アルムクヴィスト Karl-Martin Almqvistとの双頭クインテットによる新しいアルバム、『Frogs In A Pond』が届いた。

後述のファズの説明にもある通り、型番を付さない自主製作盤となっている。
（日本国内のディストリビューターであるディスクユニオンのHPでは、レーベルを「Gidon Nunes Vaz」としている。

ファズはまだ35歳ながら自己のグループ（カルテット、クインテット、セクステット）で精力的にリーダー作をリリースしており、作品の多くはオランダ出身のトランペット奏者にしては珍しく、ハードバップに根差したストレートアヘッドな演奏スタイルに徹している。
2021年のワン・ホーンのバラード集『Ebb Tide』（国内発売盤）の帯のキャッチ・コピー（「オランダが誇るトランペットの詩人」）が示すとおり、中音域のふくよかな音色と流麗なフレージングが魅力的なトランぺッターである。

レヴューを書くにあたり、オランダ在住のピアニスト、小橋敦子氏によるファズへの詳細なインタビュー（2018年11月3日）を参考にさせていただいた。

ファズは自己のグループだけでなく、他のバンドのサイドメンや多くのビッグバンドに長年参加していたが、2023年からはデンマークラジオ・ビッグバンド the Danish Radio Big Band（DRBB）にオーディションを受けて加入、第５（ソロ）トランペット奏者のメンバーとして活動している。
今秋11月には、アルムクヴィスト(sax)とともに、挾間美帆＋DRBBでの３度目の来日ツアーに参加が決定している。

『Frogs In A Pond』の収録曲は、ファズとアルムクヴィストが各４曲を作曲した、すべてオリジナル曲である。

各曲の作曲の背景や構成の意図がライナーに書かれているので、下記に転記した。

■Tracklist
①FROGS IN A POND （Karl-Martin Almqvist）　06：24
Sat late one evening in the dark with one of my biggest musical idols/role models.
Listend to the frogs from the pond nearby.
It really sounded like they were conversing with each other.

②SHORTER’S BRUSH （Gidon Nunes Vaz）　7：50
This piece was inspired by the late Wayne Shorter and his use of colours in his compositions.
Initially I wrote it in 3/4 time but when Karl-Martin suggested to try it in 5/4 it worked better.
The composition convinced me to have the Fender Rhodes in the recording.

③GALAXEN （Karl-Martin Almqvist）　06：26
I was inspired by creating melodic lines based on different fixed intervals.
I wrote a number of lines that I thought would fit nicely with the rhythm section’s ostinato.
I think it all had a vibe of space.

④YUGEN （Gidon Nunes Vaz）　7：18
Is the Japanese word for mysterious profundity.
A subtle, and profound beauty that is felt more than seen.
The many rthythmic layers over the 3/4 waltz together with the harmonic movement gives a kind of floating sensation.

⑤BLUES FOR MARA （Gidon Nunes Vaz）　6：42
Is a blues in two key signatures at the same time during the melody.
In the solo it moves from one key to the next and back, like a dance, in which the key of A represents my beloved fiance Mara and the key of B♭represents myself.
The friction between the tenor and trumpet during the drum solo reveals the many aspects of a loving relationship, dissolving into the last theme.

⑥STILTJE （Karl-Martin Almqvist）　06：26
I wanted to write something that symbolizes the wonderfully calm and relaxing feeling of an ocean or a large lake when it is completely still, no wind.
The mirror-like surface, not a ripple.

⑦WE ALL KNOW （Karl-Martin Almqvist）　06：51
I have always loved playing the beautiful ballad You Don’t Know What Love is.
I wrote a new melody, a so-called paraphrase.
Some reharmonization gave it a different vibe and feel.

⑧CPH （Gidon Nunes Vaz）　7：01
Reflects a new part of my life, playing music and being on the move in and around Copenhagen.
It represents the vibrant energy of the city and the love for jazz, propagated by its scene.
The song is a fuse of modernity and tradition, using more modern cluster chords in first theme and in the bridge Coltrane’s Countdown cycle, changing the regular chords into minor seven, suspended dominant chords and having the trumpet and tenor play in counterpoint.

ベテラン・アーチストである、Almqvist（1968年11月24日生まれ）との双頭クインテット結成や、すべてオリジナル曲で制作した狙いや経緯などをNunes Vazが教えてくれた。

「デンマークラジオ・ビッグバンド（DRBB）のオーディションのためにラジオ局の建物の廊下に入ったとき、最初に会ったのがカール＝マーティンですぐに友人になりました。彼は最初からとても親切で温かく接してくれました。
DRBBでの彼のソロ演奏では、心からの情熱と創造的なリスクを冒してプレイしているのが分かり、毎回刺激を受けています。ミュージシャンとして、そして人として本当に尊敬しています。

DRBBのバンドツアーで何時間も一緒に過ごすうちに、私たちは新しい曲を小編成であるクインテットで演奏するというアイデアが浮かびました。
ビッグバンドでは個人の自由が制限されるため、私たちはこのアイデアを喜んで受け入れました。ビッグバンド以外にクリエイティブな決定と、成長できるプロジェクトが欲しかったのです。

2025年の夏に全曲作曲しました。作曲にあたっては互いにとても自然に補完し合っていると思います。

音楽的な決断をする際、カール＝マーティンとはほとんどの場合、方向性が同じなのです。私にとって本当に特別なプロジェクトでした。うち４曲をファースト・テイクでわずか３時間半で録音できたからです。
スタジオではヘッドホンも使わず、録音ブースも分けずに１つの部屋でレコーディングしました。
録音の２日前に一度だけリハーサルを行い、録音スタジオでは、常に自発的、直感的な感覚がありました。

これは、オランダのジャズシーンで活躍する、非常に優秀で才能豊かなリズムセクションのおかげでもあります。

これまで演奏してきたスタンダード曲やあまり知られていない名曲（2018年のアルバム、『There’s No End』で取り上げた〈No End〉のこと）に対する想いや愛情は、以前と変わりません。
個人的には、ビッグバンドで演奏することが多いので、何か新しいものを作りたいという衝動に駆られました。
より創造的な自由を求めたわけです。
新しく作曲することは、ミュージシャンとして成長し続ける上でとても重要です。

ただ、オリジナル曲をプレイするのは難しいと感じることもあり、他の作曲家の曲を好んで演奏することが多いけれど、今回の挑戦は私にとってとてもよかった。学び、成長できた、と思う。曲はカール＝マーティンと私が半分ずつ、各４曲を作曲することにしました。

作曲するにあたり、他の作品からアイデアを持ち込むことはせず、私たちは直感的なアプローチを大切にしたかった。
ピアノの前に座って曲を書くことで、自然にどんなものが生まれるかを見てみたかったのです。

〈SHORTER’S BRUSH〉で使いたい音（Fender Rhodes）は頭の中にありました。Miles Davisのアルバム『In A Silent Way』は私のお気に入りのアルバムの一つで、こうした様々な音色を使ったのも、すべて直感的に出てきたものです」

来年（2027年）4月にはこのクインテットでオランダでコンサートツアーを予定している。
また、アルムクヴィストとのクインテットでのアルバムは将来的にも制作していきたい、と語ってくれた。

items._cn_summary: 专辑由小号手吉东·努内斯·法斯与萨克斯手卡尔－马丁·阿尔姆奎斯特共同领衔五人乐团，以八首原创作品延续硬波普与主流爵士语汇。编曲强调可辨识的旋律动机、复杂拍号及层次化节奏，五拍子华尔兹、复合调性蓝调与固定音程构成的主要素材，为即兴提供不同方向；钢琴与电钢琴则补充和声色彩。整张作品结构清晰、演奏均衡，在传统爵士框架内保留现代构思，但对实验音色、开放即兴及跨界元素的展开相对有限。

items.body:
CONCERTS/LIVE SHOWS
NO. 340
#1422 Ben van Gelder & Reinier Baas (ベン・ヴァン・ゲルダー&レイ二エル・バース)　岡山公演
2026年8月15日
岡崎凛

text & photo at the concert: Ring Okazaki 岡崎 凛

2026年７月２９日（水）　岡山市・蔭凉寺（Inryoji-temple in Okayama City）
open 17:00 / start 18:30
「NewYork Contemporary Cool Jazz」/
Ben van Gelder (ベン・ヴァン・ゲルダー）: alto sax
Reinier Baas (レイ二エル・バース) : guitar


Ben van GelderとReinier Baasはオランダから来日し、７月２６日(日) ～８月１日(土) 静岡市、京都市、岡山市、東京都でのツアーを行った。
このうちの岡山市、蔭凉寺（いんりょうじ）のコンサートに行き、リハーサルから見学し、開演前にOffice Zooの川上浩平氏と出演者の２人に短いインタビューを行った。
２人はオランダ出身で米国のジャズシーンとのつながりが深いが、欧州ジャズシーンの最新の部分を掘り下げ、母国の音楽歴史との融合の中で発展させていくような音楽家でもある。今回の公演では、ジョン・コルトレーン曲が演奏されて旧知の馴染み深いサウンドに出会ったと思ったら、その先には全く初めて出会う風景が広がっていた。サックスとギターが描く細かな波紋を追うような体験があった。

二人が奏でる音に、まるで肌に触れるような感触がある。レイニエルのギターが紡ぎ出す音の複雑な変化に魅了され、聴き耳を立てて追わずにいられなくなる。その不思議なギターソロを真横で聴くサックス奏者の表情には、深い共感と信頼が満ちているように思えた。そのギターに応えるサックスの音も、細やかな変化を繰り返し、柔らかな光に満ちては陰りを宿らせる。
彼らのデュオを聴くということは、二人の音楽探求の生々しい現場に立ち会うことであるようだ。リラックスして音楽に浸るひと時もあったが、聴き耳を立て、目の前で生れる音楽の変容を隅々まで体感したいという思いにかられた。

レイニエルとゲルダーや、彼らの共演仲間であるドラマーのジェフ・バラードの曲などのオリジナル曲のほかに、セロニアス・モンクの〈work〉やカルロス・ジョビンの〈How Insensitive〉のように著名な曲が演奏された。耳馴染みのいい曲を聴くのは嬉しかったが、この公演でとりわけ貴重だったのは、２人が描き続ける微細な絵を延々と眺めるような時間だった。その詳細は水の泡のように記憶から抜け落ちていくのだが、それでもなお、その体験が愛おしく思えてくる。このコンサートを、蔭凉寺本堂内の音響環境で聴くことができたのも、とても幸運だった。デュオの奏でる音と落ち着いた色の和室の内装、演奏する二人の表情が一つに溶け合う体験は、忘れられないものになった。

garden of Inryoji Temple
at rehearsal before the concert
Reinier Baas at rehearsal in Inryoji

ベン・ヴァン・ゲルダーの2023年のアルバム『Manifold』、レイニエル・バースの2024年作『Relief Party』はどちらも興味深い作品である。２人のライブが始まる前の短いインタビューの機会に、２つのアルバムの両方に参加するピアニスト、Kit Downes (キット・ダウンズ) について彼らに話した。彼らが２人ともキット・ダウンズと共演していることは、それだけで世界のジャズシーンの最先端を行く存在だと判断できる、というのが自分の考えである。もちろんこれらのアルバムには、キット・ダウンズが共演者であるということ以外に、興味深い点がたくさんある。できることなら、ベンとレイニエルの二人にそれぞれの近作アルバムに関して詳しく語ってもらいたかったが、自分の英語力ではコンサートの開演直前にそこまでの話を進められなかった。２人のアルバムとその共演者への賛辞を告げる程度で話を切り上げた。
（リハーサル時の写真にベン・ヴァン・ゲルダーの姿がないのは、撮影時に彼がステージ横の襖の奥でサックスを吹いていたためで、その姿をカメラに収められなかった）

この夜に聴いたのは、上記のアルバムのように多数の出演者が加わるものではなく、２人だけのコンサートだ。しかしこのデュオは、彼らのイマジネーションの源泉となっているのではないかと思った。２人が出会ったのは、あるインタビューの情報によれば2009年頃で、デュオ活動の始まる数年前に遡る。米国でのプロデビューの早かったゲルダーと、彼より４歳年上のレイニエルは、かなり若いころに米国で知り合い、これまでデュオライブを２００～３００回くらいこなし、数えきれないという。二人の関係は、ただ相性がいいという言葉では収まり切らないだろう。互いにインスピレーションを与え、それぞれの音楽活動の糧とする関係ではないかと想像している。

Ben van Gelder
Reinier Baas
Ben & Reinier

コンサート会場の物販用テーブルに並んでいた2024年リリースのアルバム『This Is Water』のCDとLPはバンドキャンプでも試聴、購入ができるようだ。１曲目のタイトル曲は、今回のデュオ・コンサートの重要テーマを体現したような作品である。


『This Is Water』はYouTubeでも聴くことができる。（2026年8月現在）

https://youtu.be/E9kOJL5ck9I?si=B1n6rzy6H695njF_

コンサートの前の出演者の二人へのインタビューで、彼らの母国のジャズ歴史について触れると、オランダが誇る1942年生まれのレジェンド・ドラマー、Han Bennink（ハン・ベニンク）について話が及んだ。「オランダのミュージシャンは、即興とユーモアを大切にするんだ」とゲルダーは語った。「オランダのジャズ歴史はハン・ベニンクとともに始まったと言ってもいい」という彼の言葉を聞くと、あらためてこのレジェンドの過去作品をもっと聴いておきたいという気持ちが湧いた。
２人のアルバム『This Is Water』には、彼の参加曲が収められている。また３人の共演する最近の動画では、Han Benninkがカホンとシンバルを叩く姿が収められ、シンプルだがエッジの効いた演奏で若い二人を盛り立てている。

主催者のコンサート情報より出演者紹介：
Ben van Gelder ベン・ヴァン・ゲルダー：alto sax 
オランダ出身のアルトサックス奏者。
１７歳でニューヨークに移り住み、１０年間にわたり世界で最も進歩的なアーティストたちとコラボレーションし研鑽を積む。彼は先進的な考えを持つ仲間たち（サム・ハリス、クレイグ・ウェインリブ、リック・ロサト、ピーター・シュラム）とクインテットを結成し自身の名義で３枚のアルバムをレコーディングしてヨーロッパ、日本、そしてアメリカで精力的にツアーを行う。
特に日本ツァーにはマーク・ターナーをゲストに迎えて来日し演奏は各地で好評を博した。
ニューヨーク滞在中は芸術的卓越性を育み才能の跳躍台として知られる「ジャズ・ギャラリー」と強い絆を築き公演を通して様々なグループやレパートリーを試み、デイヴィッド・ビニー、マーク・ターナー、アンブローズ・アキンムシーレ、ベン・ストリートなど多くの現代ジャズの精鋭たちと演奏やレコーディングを行ってきた。
また、彼はジャズ・ギャラリーから作曲の委嘱を受け、抽象画家フランティシェク・クプカの絵画にインスピレーションを得た作品『Among Verticals』をレコーディングし発表する。この作品は世界中のメディアで称費を浴びる。
楽曲は、グラミー賞を受賞したメトロポール管弦楽団、スイス・ジャズ・オーケストラ、コンセルトヘボウ・ジャズ・オーケストラなど、いくつかの大規模なアンサンブルによって編曲および演奏される。
デロイト・ジャズ・アワード、全米芸術振興基金ゴールドアワード、そして兄ギデオンとのデュオでプリンセス・クリスティーナ・コンクールなど、数々の賞を受賞してる。最近では、アムステルダムのBIMHUISから初の作曲依頼を受ける。
オランダに戻ってからは自身のカルテットを率いるほか、ギタリストのライナー・バースと頻繁に共演しており、メトロポール・オーケストラとのライブ録音によるアルバム『SMASH HITS』と『Mokum in Hi-Fi』をリリースしている。
現在はオランダで作曲や演奏活動の他に教育にも熱心で、アムステルダム音楽院の教授を務めている。
アルトサックスの権威として国際的に認められ、その独特なサウンド、叙情性、そして作曲への独自のアプローチは、同業者や批評家から高く評価されいる。
彼の音楽はジャズの伝統に深く根ざしながらも、他の多くの音楽ジャンルや領域を包含しており特に視覚芸術は彼の音楽活動において重要な役割を果たし、しばしば作曲の枠組みとして用いられている。

Reinier Baas： レイニエル・バース：guitar
1985年オランダ生まれのギタリスト／作曲家。
2010年にアムステルダム音楽院を最優秀の成績で卒業。
2013年の『Mosty Improvized Indie Music』と2016年作「Reinier Baas vs. Princess Discombobulatrix』の２作はともに名誉あるエジソン賞（オランダで最も権威のある音楽賞）を受賞している。
“彼の音楽は「予測不可能でありながら、全体的な形式に安心感がある」という特徴を持っている”とニューヨーク・シティ・ジャズ・レコード誌の解説には記されている。彼の音楽は特別な方法で構成されている。不可解なハーモニーはバルトークやストラヴィンスキーを彷彿とさせるが、構造が崩れヒップホップのリズムが突如として力強く響きそして全てが激しい流れと即興のカコフォニーへと変化した後、音楽は厳粛で整然とした形式へと戻る。
現在、バースはハモンド・トリオ「DEADEYE」と、ベンジャミン・ハーマン率いるパンク／ジャズ・グループ「BUGHOUSE」のメンバーとして活動している。相棒のベン・ヴァン・ゲルダーとはデュオで定期的に活動しており、伝説のドラマー、ハン・ベニンクやジェフ・バラードをゲストに迎えることもある。作曲家としては、ピュナレロ交響楽団、メトロポール管弦楽団、西ドイツ放送交響楽団ビッグパンドのために作品を書いた他、ノースシー・ジャズ・フェスティバル、ロイヤル・コンセルトヘボウ、ビムハウス、南チロル・ジャズ・フェスティバル、ノヴェンバー・ミュージックのための委嘱作品も書いている。またソリストとして、「メトロポール管弦楽団」「国立ユース管弦楽団」「国立ユース・ジャズ・オーケストラ」「コンセルトヘボウ・ジャズ・オーケストラ」「WDR ビッグ・パンド」「CVAコンサート・ビッグ・バンド」「ニュー・ロッテルダム・ジャズ・オーケストラ」などと共演している。
バースは、ルイス・コール、デイヴィッド・ビニー、フエンサンタ、コリー・スマイス、マルタ・ワレリス、ハンス・ティーウェン、ラモン・ヴァッ、ノラ・フィッシャー、ジェシー・ファン・ルラー、メアリー・ハルバーソン、グレゴリー・ポーターなど、多くの著名なミュージシャンと共演しいる。
演奏や作曲の他に教育者としても高い評価を得ており、アムステルダム音楽院とバーゼル・ジャズキャンパスで教鞭を執っている他にオランダ・ユース・ジャズ・オーケストラ（NJJO）の2025/26年度生の芸術監兼指揮者も務めている。

以下は今回のコンサートのフライヤー。この岡山公演の開催に尽力していた平井康嗣氏、Office Zooの川上浩平氏、蔭凉寺住職の篠原真祐氏に、今回の取材で非常にお世話になったことを、最後に記しておきたい。

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评记录了荷兰爵士乐手Ben van Gelder与Reinier Baas在冈山蔭凉寺的本堂内举办的二重奏现场。两人以阿尔托萨克斯与古典吉他搭配，在寺庙独特的声学空间中展开细腻的即兴对话。文章详述了从排练到采访再到正式演出的完整过程，聚焦于两位音乐家之间深厚的信任与默契，以及他们演奏中细密音色的不断变化。曲目涵盖了原创作品以及Monk、Jobim等知名作曲家的作品，同时融入了对荷兰爵士历史（以Han Bennink为代表）的探讨。文章亦介绍了两人各自的近期专辑以及专辑中关联的Kit Downes等多位合作者，整体评论具有较强的现场纪实色彩与音乐历史纵深感。

NO. 340
#1420 権代敦彦 オペラ《ZEN》

調布国際音楽祭2026
2026年6月26日（金）19:00開演　 調布市文化会館たづくり くすのきホール

オペラ≪ZEN≫（世界初演）

作曲：権代敦彦

ヘアメイク：原美沙紀

https://chofumusicfestival.com/ja/program/e4SkbHmS

構想から10年！
台本は出来たものの、一度は崩壊。
その後、世界で唯一人、オペラ実現に向けて手を挙げてくれた
鈴木優人氏によっていよいよ音に・・・・・。
しかし、物語に縛られ、言葉に管理され・・・・・
「時間芸術」たる「音楽」の入り込む余地無き作曲。
これら多くの困難ーーそれは恰も（禅）の修行の如くーーを経て、
物語を置き去りにし、言葉を踏み台として、
言語世界を抜けた「音世界」を目指すオペラが完成。
終章で、読経と尺八の印象的な音に集約されるその「音世界」こそ、
まさにZEN（禅）が目指す境地でもあろう。ーーーーー権代敦彦
（フライヤーより）

権代敦彦の新作オペラ《ZEN》を観る。

まず、ホールが実に良い。響きもいいし大箱すぎずクラシック音楽に相応しい品格がある。休憩時のバーカウンターがないのが公共ホールらしいが、酒類メーカーのスポンサーが現物支給（ワインとか）という形で支援すると音楽祭感が高まるとは思ったが、そこは「禅」なのでストイックに鑑賞するのが筋ではある。

作曲家本人の言葉がそのまま曲の構造を語っており、クオリティも保証されている。間違いない。ソールドアウトになるわけである。調布という開催地を考えて1日公演だったのか、音楽祭のスケジュールのせいか。公演日が2日でも集客は楽勝だったのではないか。一期一会とはいえ1日とは勿体無い。

素敵なホールで素晴らしい演奏家と歌手による巨匠の作品を堪能した。バッハ・コレギウム・ジャパン（BCJ）はやはりBCJで素晴らしく、オペラ歌手も上手い。合唱も権代作品の「鳴り」を底上げして観客を陶酔に導く音作りに貢献した。尺八奏者も場面転換を担ったように空気を変えた。全て予定調和と言っても差し支えないほどの完成度だった。流石であった。権代氏が新たに挑戦しようとしたことが達成されたかはともかく、皆にとって幸せな一晩だった。

権代氏は演奏家によって自作が化学反応を起こすことを前提としている作曲家だと私は思っている。例えば、メシアン、ライヒの作品が分かりやすいので例えにするが、彼らの曲はきちんと上手に弾くか、下手に弾くか、というような2択しかないような印象を私は受ける。それが悪いという訳ではない。上手に弾ければ精神的なカタルシスも得られ演奏家冥利にも尽きる。そういう意味ではラヴェルのピアノ作品に近い。ちゃんと弾ければ曲として鑑賞に耐えうる構造になっている。

《ZEN》の初演を聴き、その圧倒的な終盤の陶酔感に浸りながらも私は「この曲は再演ではまた違う表情を見せて大化けする可能性がある」と感じた。高い完成度の演奏という芳醇なる大地の中に仕込まれた作曲家の新たな試みの種がある気がするのだ。

「物語に縛られ、言葉に管理され」と作曲家本人が書いている通り、オープニングは「禅」をテーマにしているのに、日本語のテキストが多すぎると感じた。禅本来の「不立文字（文字に頼らない）」「言葉を超えた体験」は終章の尺八、合唱とアンサンブルで音量（デシベル）が劇的に上がったことも含め禅の境地に達した感を味わった。だが、そこに至るまでの過程において、なぜ「禅」なのに出演者はスーツ姿でクールビズっぽい着こなしだったり、しかもベルカントでアンサンブルが古楽器なのか？という違和感があったのは否めない。ベルカントは本来、言葉を歌として美しく流す技法だが、《ZEN》の冒頭は長いテキストをほとんど切らずに歌わせる場面が続く。結果として、ベルカント的な滑らかな歌唱、日本語の長い文章、禅的な反復が重なり、「説法」や「読経」のような印象になり、作品のテーマには合ってはいるが推進力に欠けた感があるのだ。権代氏はもっとラップのようにやりたかったのではないだろうかと邪推しながら聴いていた。

「言葉を踏み台にして」作曲したと権代氏はサラッと書いている。権代氏の1作目のオペラはリトアニア語の脚本に作曲した「桜の記憶」で、リトアニア語と3年格闘したという記述を見た。楽譜を見ていないので断定は出来ないが、今回も日本語の抑揚や韻律をかなり意識して葛藤したのではないだろうか。歌手が「オペラ歌手として完璧なベルカント歌唱法を作品に提供する」ほど、作品の意図から離れた可能性があるのではないかと思ったのだ。

ここでいうラップは、ヒップホップのスタイルという意味ではなく、言葉のリズムを優先、アクセントが重要で韻律やフレージングで推進力を生むという意味で、「日本語のプロソディ（言葉の自然なリズム）」をもっと前面に出すと印象がまるで違ったのではないかということだ。現代の作曲家は権代氏に限らず、ジャズ、ロック、テクノ、ラップ、民族音楽いろんなものを無意識に吸収しているはずなのだ。それがそのまま引用されなくても、時間感覚やリズムの設計として作品の中に潜んでいる。作曲家本人は「ラップを書いた」と思っていなくても、身体のどこかにその感覚が入っていることは珍しくないと思う。だから歌手が「私はクラシックの発声で忠実に歌いました」だけだと、その身体性を拾えない。

その点で木村正子役のカウンターテナー、村松稔之氏の日本語が生きていると感じた。この人はヒップホップのラップもイケるのではないかと思わせる推進力が言葉のリズムにあった。作品のテキストに合わせて身体をチューニングしたのではないか。オペラのメジャー言語ではない他の言語のオペラをイタリア・オペラ風に歌われると、作曲家の意図とは離れてしまうことがあるのを分かっているのだろう。《ZEN》も「オペラ歌手なら歌える」という作品ではなく、日本語の言葉を音楽としてどう生かすかという別の能力が求められたのではないかと思っている。ただ美しく歌えばいいわけではないところが難しい。美しく歌うことだって相当に難しいのだから。

ここに私はクラシックの教育の問題も少し感じる。クラシックは、「正しく歌う／弾く」ことは徹底的に教えるが「作品によって自分をチューニングする」ことは、教えない。でも現代作品ではそこが問われる。現代音楽は未来のクラシック音楽であり全てのクラシック作品はかつての現代音楽だったのだ。

初演に携わるということは、まだ存在しないものを立ち上げる行為だから演奏家は「再現者」ではなく「創作者」でもある。未来の音楽に共同作業として参加する姿勢が要る。演奏家は決して過去の技術を守るだけが使命ではない。もし再現と自分の様式を作品に適用するだけならAI歌手があと何年もしないうちに人間を超えてしまうかもしれない。

ベルカントが気になったのは第1幕の小編成での古楽アンサンブルということもある。古楽器でしかも小編成だから当然ではあるのだが、音量が足りない。フルオーケストラで歌う前提のベルカントに対してボリュームが低いのだ。もちろん、BCJだからこそ得られた透明感や細部の明晰さというのは小さい音でも伝わってはくるが、作品全体のスケール感と微妙に一致しておらず、前半だけでも軽くPAをかけた方がいいのではないか？現代音楽なんだしという気はした。権代敦彦はもともと大きな時間軸で音を積み上げて、音響の厚みを設計し、クライマックスを構築することに長けている作曲家だ。その資質を考えると、「古楽器アンサンブル」という制約が、かえって本来の長所を抑えてしまったのではないか、フルオーケストラならどう響くだろうという発想を持ってしまうのが自然な気持ちではある。

公開リハーサルでは観客もいなくて音も響いてバランスも良かったのかもしれない。それが満員の聴衆にアンサンブルの音が吸われてバランスが崩れたという可能性もあるし、もし《ZEN》が本質的にもっと圧倒的な音響、身体を包み込むような響き、劇場を満たす音圧を必要とする作品だったとしたら、BCJの方向性とは少し違っていたのではないかという気もするが、私は単にアンサンブルにPAをかけて再演を聴いてみたいと思っている。本作の小編成の楽器パートも緻密に作られているはずだ。チェンバロにPAをかけるとそれはそれはカッコよくなるのだ。まるでパンク。ぜひそれでアンサンブルでも聴いてみたい。衣装もスーツはやめて、最後の舞台挨拶での作曲家と脚本家が同じ色のシャツで衣装合わせをしてたようにコーディネートしてほしい。コンサート形式とはいえテキストのイメージとのギャップが気になった。作曲家と脚本家は木下正子役に次いで派手で素敵だったなぁ。尺八奏者もまんまZENぽくて衣装も所作も素晴らしい。

余談だが、現代音楽のオペラに限らずオーケストラ作品や小規模な編成、ソロ器楽曲などであっても「難解」「1度聞いただけでは理解できない」というようなことが書かれている記事を目にする。音楽であれ今回のような哲学的なテキストの扱いについてであれ、分からないものを「分からなかった」と書くのは随分勇気があるなと思う。創作者にとっては最大の営業妨害の言葉でもあるからだ。それに1度聞いて分からないものを何度か聞けば分かるのか？とも思う。このような記事は分からないながらも理解しようとして挫折したという善意の心理の吐露なのかと創作者に誤解させがちだ。その結果、ついサービス精神で「分かる」作品を作りたい気持ちにさせてしまうことになりかねず、商業的にはともかく音楽の未来のためにはならない。

権代氏は十分に権代敦彦ブランドへの期待に応えた。観客は最後に、「さすが権代」と私も含めて歓喜。ただ途中までの新しい試みがその「権代らしさ」に吸収されてしまったようにも私には思えた。ぜひ前半アンサンブルにPAをかけて確認してみたい（しつこいけど。絶対おすすめ）。

矢沢朋子 Tomoko Yazawa  ピアニスト/ DJ / プロデューサー
東京出身。フランス近代、現代音楽の演奏で特に定評のあるピアニスト。多くの有名作曲家が曲を献呈。桐朋学園大学、パリ・エコール・ノルマル高等演奏家資格取得。第16回中島健蔵音楽賞受賞。2001年よりマルチメディア・プロジェクト、エレクトロ・アコースティック・プロジェクト「Absolute-MIX」をプロデュース。CDをAmazon、iTune、Spotifyなどで40カ国以上に配信、販売するGeisha Farmも主宰。
items._genre: contemporary opera / baroque ensemble / Japanese traditional / experimental vocal
items._cn_summary: 権代敦彦的Opera《ZEN》以禅宗哲学为概念框架，历经十年构思，融合巴洛克器乐编制（古乐器合奏BCJ）、尺八独奏、男声合唱与歌剧独唱，试图超越文本束缚进入纯粹音响世界。作曲家本人将语言视为踏脚石，在终章以诵经与尺八构建听觉高潮。然而评论指出，开场段落密集的日语歌词与bell canto唱法形成'说教感'，推进力不足；countertenor村松稔之的演唱因其贴近日语自然韵律而展现出rap式推进力，暗示作品若更强调日语prosody可能获得不同效果。整体制作精良，BCJ演绎完成度高，但跨语种歌剧与bell canto传统之间的张力构成了作品的核心矛盾，作曲家对演奏家化学反应的依赖也预示再演潜力。
