items.body:
CONCERTS/LIVE SHOWS
NO. 340
#1417 マリア・シュナイダー・オーケストラ
2026年8月15日
ゲスト・ コントリビューター

text & photos: Seigen Ono オノセイゲン
Photos: Yuka Yamaji 山路ゆか except as indicated

今さらながら初めて聴いた感動、その２。

スライドショーには JavaScript が必要です。

マリア・シュナイダー率いるジャズ・オーケストラ最高峰、ギル・エヴァンスやボブ・ブルックマイヤーに師事し、第58回グラミー賞で２部門を受賞、現代ジャズを牽引する作編曲家、マリア・シュナイダーの９年ぶりとなる日本公演（ブルーノート東京のインフォより）。

マリア・シュナイダー。もちろん名前は知っていたし、ギル・エヴァンスに師事し、第58回グラミー賞では２部門を受賞した偉大な作曲家、バンドリーダー、8月4日から8日までブルーノート東京、全席完売、気になりますねえ、これは観ておかないと。ブルーノート東京の最終日1stステージのカウンター席（ここはPAのバランスもいちばんいい）に入れた。１曲目の管楽器のまるでストリングスオーケストラのような繊細なハーモニーで、あ、もうこれは来てよかった！この曲が一番好き。『Data Lords』に収録された楽曲で、第63回グラミー賞の最優秀インストゥルメンタル作曲賞を受賞。２曲目の世界中でさまざまな決断やクリエイティブまでAIに支配されそれでいいのか？！というレジスタンスのようなメッセージの曲<Don’t Be Evil> は重い。ビッグデータ・カンパニーが世界中の情報を集め、コントロールし、政治や趣味趣向にさえ影響を及ぼしている危険性を不協和音の抵抗で分かりやすいけど、パンクロックにしてくれた方が楽しめるかも。この音は不快で（それが狙いだと思うが）好きではなかった。<Sputnik> スプートニク（と日本語発音してみせた）は、空を見上げて今や無数に飛び交っている人工衛星、それが肉眼でどれくらい見えるのか分からないが、映画「インターステラー」や「スペースX」、古くは「E.T.」、夜空を飛び交う、光、衛星を目に浮かぶような景色として分かりやすかった。バリトンサックスのスコット・ロビンソンの奥様が物理学者で彼女のことを描いたような話があったようななかったような、後半、出身地ミネソタの大草原・農風景、景色や故郷を描いた、子供時代の思い出や <The Thompson Fields> だったと思いますが、まさにミネソタ州の、ああ、アメリカの田舎と分かりやすい曲（色々間違いでしたらすみません）。

1stステージと2ndステージでセットリストや演出の構成が変わるとのことでしたので、特に１曲目がもう一度、聴いておきたくて、翌日は音楽評論家の佐藤英輔さんや映画ドットコムのボクの連載「オノ セイゲンPresents＜映画の聴き方＞」担当の松村果奈さんも誘って日本公演最終日の高崎芸術劇場へ小旅行となりました。そやけど、ブルーノート東京最終日の1stステージと高崎はぼくの記憶ではまったく同じセットリストでした。MCもスコット・ロビンソンの奥様の話がなかっただけで他はほぼ同じ。もしかしたら１曲くらい違ったかも知れませんでしたが、まあそれでもこの世界ナンバーワンのジャズ・オーケストラの同じ曲を２日続けて、ライブハウスと大劇場で、まるでレコードをカートリッジ違いで聴き比べるような楽しみ方をしてしまったのは少し反省です。もちろんソロ内容は違いますからそれはそれで。ドラムを務めたのは現代ジャズ・ドラム最高峰の一人と称されるジョナサン・ブレイク（Jonathan Blake）、今ごろBill Frisell のthe Village Vanguard NYCですね！
嬉しかったのは、友人といっしょのプチ国内旅行でした。

https://eisukesato.exblog.jp/36602023/
https://eiga.com/news/20260813/7/

音楽評論家でもないボクが彼女について寄稿するのは、いささかおこがましい気もする。ただ、自由に書かせてもらえるJazzTokyoなので、ここはあくまで個人的な主観として、そしてここから録音エンジニアとしての視点から書いてみたいと思います。かつてボク自身も、90年代の若気の至りで大編成のアンサンブルをやっていたことがあります。そんな経験も踏まえて、今回注目したのは、マリア・シュナイダー・オーケストラというこれだけの人数のアンサンブルを、現代の「ライブ空間」でバンドリーダーとしてどう鳴らしているのか、という点です。もちろん1960年代ではないので、ライブにはPAシステムも使われます。もう一つのテーマとして浮かび上がってきたのが「音響」です。それもクラブと高崎芸術劇場の大劇場（永田音響設計が音響設計の2,027席）に注目して考察をしてみました。これだけの人数のオーケストラを、どのように響かせ、どのように聴かせるのか。マリア・シュナイダーの音楽そのものだけでなく、「この音楽を、この人数で、この空間にどう響かせるのか」という、もう一つの視点から考察してみます。

ちなみに高崎芸術劇場の412席の音楽ホールはボクは録音には日本で２番目に好きな響きです。一番好きなのはサラマンカホール（708席、残響2.1秒）の響きです。３番目は、まもなく30周年を迎える京都コンサートホール、こちらも永田音響設計が音響設計のホールです。
https://www.nagata.co.jp/news/news1910.html
https://salamanca.gifu-fureai.jp/information/
https://www.nagata.co.jp/projects/3129

ボクの青春時代は80年から六本木・新宿ピットインをはじめ、ジャズ・ミュージシャンのPAやツアー、スタジオ（とライブの）レコーディングをやってきました。Jazz Tokyo の Kenny 稲岡編集長ともトリオ・ケンウッド・レーベル、Tokyo Meeting 1985、一連の渡辺香津美DOMOレーベルほか、業界の端くれにはいるつもりなのですが、気づくと実は滅多にライブに足を運ばなくなっていました。ジャズはライブだから行け！音楽もの企画上映の「オーディオルーム新文芸坐」（池袋）、新宿ピットイン（新宿三丁目）、晴れたら空に豆まいて（代官山）、それ以外はSDMO Studio、SDLab （明治神宮前）に引きこもっています。すべてメトロ副都心線沿いの３０分圏内になっています。とくにこの３年は引きこもって「マイルス・デイヴィス生誕100年」（今年2026年）のイベントなどのために私的リマスタリングに特化し、DSDデータが 37 時間分までできあがっています。日本企画SACD化の可能性を探るべくミーティングを重ねていますが、奇跡的にパッケージ化がオーソライズされるまで、その音は一般の方は聴けません。ボクと小川隆夫さんとソニー・ミュージック・レーベルズの渡辺巧さんだけがその検討用にDSD Walkmanでも保持しています。あ、聴ける機会が２回あります。①９月３０日、最高の音でマイルス作品を聴く─マイルス・デイヴィス生誕100年記念 トーク＆リスニング・イベント“第二弾” 。出演：オノセイゲン／小川隆夫　司会：原田潤一（ARBAN / Montreux Jazz Festival Japan CEO）／楠元伸哉（ARBAN 編集長）
https://www.arban-mag.com/article/113462
② ８月３０日（日）『Jaz.in Plus』グランドオープン記念特別企画に当初予定していた出演者の一人が急遽入院となりトラでオープニングと終演後にボクがマイルスのDSD リマスタリングDJやります！「海野雅威ライブ＆トーク・セッション in 晴れ豆〜NYレジェンドたちが愛したピアニスト，その軌跡と真実〜 [出演] 海野雅威 (p) / 佐藤俊太郎（MC)
https://haremame.com/schedule/82435/

ブルーノート東京がまだ骨董通りにあった頃、ボクと作曲家・プロデューサーの（故）佐久間正英氏で、ここ（写真①）今のブルーノート東京の楽屋口の突き当たりの二階建てのこの小さな家の一階にv.f.v.studio という録音スタジオ（といってもFostex B16という16チャンネルのアナログハーフインチ・レコーダー）兼オフィスを作りました。1984〜1994?、ここでもいくつもアルバムを制作しました。いま思い出しましたが、渡辺香津美、佐久間正英、オノ セイゲンで録音したアルバムが未発表でどこかに眠っているはずなのだが ．．．。すぐ近くに家具のIDÉEや「ダイニズテーブル（DAINI’S table）」(ヌーベル・キュイジーヌ、フレンチ・サービススタイルで中華）もあり、ボクのセカンドアルバム（Virgin UK）のタイトル曲『The Green Chinese Table』はこの店に通っていたことから生まれました。98年にここに移転してきたブルーノート東京は 約２８０席、大きな四角いハコなのに徹底した吸音／遮音対策がなされていてジャズ以外の大音量クラブイベントにも余裕で対応できるPAシステムと富裕層向けとも言える食事メニューも充実していてジャズライブハウスというより、財布と心に余裕のある方たちが最高のエンタテイメントを楽しめる東京の夜のスポットとして海外にまで名前が知られています。

2000 年 3 月 12 日、当時のブルーノート東京のプロデューサー宮本端くんのブッキングで「Seigen Ono Ensemble」(オノ セイゲン、三宅純、村田陽一、竹内直、緑川英徳、五十嵐一生、山口とも、佐藤 慎一、ヲノ サトル、江波杏子、柚楽弥衣、石川智、Den and Cokky) の日本初ライヴはその１日で収録されました。ファースト・セットが終わって楽屋に戻ると岡田大貮さんからのダイニーズテーブルのケータリングが並んでいたのです！あまりに嬉しく美味しくてセカンド・セットに上がるのを忘れそうになりましたがSACD Hybridには２セットともMC以外ノーカットで入っています。ちなみに Seigen Ono Ensemble（14〜17人編成）は、1993年モントルー・ジャズフェス創始者（故）クロード・ノブス氏によりスイスでデビューしたのを知っていた宮本さんが日本企画を実現してくれたわけです。

スライドショーには JavaScript が必要です。

その後、2003年にも「Seigen Ono Septet 2003 LIVE」(Seigen Ono、Hidenori Midorikawa、Hiroki Miyano、Febian Reza Pane、Satoshi Ishikawa、Shinichi Sato、Tetsuya Ochiai、Toyonoの９人編成）

スライドショーには JavaScript が必要です。

2000年、世界的にもどこでもやっていない開発されたばかりのSONY 「DRE S-777 Sampling Reverb」
https://blog.denon.com/9850/
という（現在ならほとんどのDAWでも可能な）コンボリュージョン・リバーブを会場に持ち込みました。「徹底した吸音」空間は、アコースティックのジャズやクラシックには大敵で、一番びっくりしたのは、毎日そこで働いているブルーノート東京のスタッフで、「なんで今日はまるでコンサートホールのような響きなの？」って。宮本さん談「チック・コリアはガチで絶賛してました。あそこ、箱としてはデッドですからね。」そして当時の支配人は「なんだこれは？すぐ購入しろ！」と正式導入となりました。その後、（故）チック・コリアはソロ・ピアノ公演で大絶賛、ボクとトニオ松重さん（当時ソニーの企画者）は楽屋に呼ばれ後日、ご自宅のピアノルームにも導入することになりました。チックのソロはプリンスも観に来て満足そうだったと。アル・ジャロウも「クラブにはあまり出たくないけど、音が良いし、ここには出たい」、（故）マイケル・ブレッカーは「（デッドだと）腕を縛られて演奏してるみたいな感じになるけど、これなら大丈夫」と宮本さんに言ってたそうです。

「それです！」ミュージシャンは適度な反射音がないと楽器が鳴りません。ボクはこの開発チームに商品企画段階から外部スタッフとして参加していて、「これはソニーが作ったプロオーディオで最高の製品で最高のマシンです！このように使いたい、画期的だ！大ヒットします！」と会議では発言しましたが、日本の商業録音スタジオの多くは「使いにくい、（値段が）高すぎる」．．．と不評だったのです。アメリカの有名どころのスタジオでは今でも（うちもですが）使用している著名なエンジニア、プロデューサーが何人もいます。現在の技術では同様の試みは「CL5」デジタル・コンソールの内蔵のプラグインでもリバーブだけを別チャンネルに送ることも簡単にできます。

オーケストラ（アコースティック楽器）には必須の初期反射と美しい響き。ホールVSライブハウス

後述する現在の音響担当若手のひとり梅原さんと終演後の会話は後日付記させていただきたいと思います。昔、メインスピーカーがJBLだった時代、コンソールはCREST V12、ヤマハSREV1、ソニーDRE-S777は常設されていたが、経年変化に耐えられずというか、ブルーノート東京は常に進化しているようで、2024年9月に26年ぶりとなるスピーカー・システムの更新。メイン・スピーカーとして選ばれたのはフランス製のL-Acoustics A15システム、コンソールはヤマハ製のデジタルミキシングコンソール「CL5」。南青山だけでなく、丸の内「コットンクラブ」、恵比寿「BLUE NOTE PLACE」、そして高崎芸術劇場の大劇場やスタジオシアターでは、ブルーノート東京がプロデュースするジャズ公演も「CL5」。

ジャズオーケストラの場合、フィーチャーソロの部分はFOHエンジニアがMCと同じくピックアップしてやらないといけない。また現代のマルチマイクセットアップが普通になっていてもマリア・シュナイダー・オーケストラのように繊細で複雑なハーモニーをカラー（音色）として簡単に聴かせるには、ステージ上の楽器のかぶり、特にホーンは空気中に出て、二つの波紋がぶつかってからでないと発生しない倍音もあり、近接マイクだけだと音色の魅力は半減してしまう。オフめに立てるか、ステージのフロア、舞台上で生音の一時反射音が美しく響く空間は音の混ざり方は本来の生オーケストラで狙う響き、音色になる。つまりデッドな空間でオンマイクにリバーブを付加するのではなく、はじめから楽器がよく鳴るセッティング、位置決め、かぶり、返し、全てはほどよくしかも、客席に作曲家が意図したバランスで音楽が届けられないといけない。これだけの人数で繊細かつ複雑なセクションのブラスに加えて、アコーディオンやエレキギター、ピアノのコンピング、ソロ、さらにベース。ドラムはすごく重要でトップのマイクは柔らかい曲想部分ではアンビエンス的にも被ってくるブラスの音も重要で、逆にマイクのボリュームを上げすぎるとブラスの繊細なハーモニーは埋もれてしまう。面白いのはこういう場合でもステージやそのエリアの初期反射音が多いと、マイクを通していない音も、ステージ上でうまく鳴っている。高崎芸術劇場の大劇場はブルーノート東京よりはるかに大きな空間であったが、このようなオケの繊細なハーモニーはこちらの方が美しい響きに聞こえた。

ブルーノート東京の音響チームは最新のデジタル機材を使用しながらも（当たり前のことなのですが）適正音量です。クラブイベントならドーンと上げてるのかもしれませんが、このチームなら大音量DJイベントでも決して耳が痛いようなことにはしない安心感があります😀というのは、特に日本人オペレーターに多いのですが、経験が少ないからか、誰に指示されるのか知りませんが、最新のデジタルアンプ、ラインアレイスピーカーを大量に買わされて、それをリミッターかかりっぱなし、ひどい音のイベントが多すぎる。ジャズ以外のいわゆるロック、ポップイベントのPAの音量がデカすぎて破綻している。FOHエンジニアまで耳栓をしていたり、おそらくオーディエンスの９０％は難聴になっていますよ。誰かが警告しないといけないと思います。
https://www.bestecaudio.com/2411case_bluenote
https://www.snrec.jp/entry/onkyoeizousetsubi_manual_l-acoustics_a15

今さらながら初めて聴いた感動、その１

南仏、コート・ダジュールのリゾート地アンティーブのジュアン・レ・パン（Juan-les-Pins）の海辺、松林の特設会場で開催されるJazz à Juan festival （1960年に始まったヨーロッパでもっとも古い歴史を持つ野外ジャズ・フェス）に来たのは32年ぶりでした。ボクは1995年から10年ほどニースの旧市街、コルシカフェリー発着所の近くにワンルームの小さな部屋を持っていたことがあり、このあたりから地中海をイタリア沿いに降りて、トスカーナ、ローマ、シチリア、バリは世界中でいちばん好きなエリアです。アンチョビ、オリーブオイル、トマト、パスタ、ブラジルも好きですが人生がもう一度あるなら、きっとこの辺りの漁港近くに住んでいたと思います。で、日本でジャズ好きなら知らない人はいない（知らないならジャズは語るな！）なんとボクとしては初めてのBanksia Trio を観たのは先月号にリポートしたように、Jazz à Juan Festival 2026（南フランス ジャズ・ア・ジュアン）July 14, 2026 7:30pmが初めてでした。１ユーロ＝１９０円超え、もう日本は世界で最貧国ではないでしょうか。というか貨幣価値は最悪のタイミングでしたが、アムステルダムから移動した南仏BIOT村にいたタイミングと石若駿さんのFBを追いかけていて偶然にも、ジュアン・レ・パンで初めて対面して会った須川さん、ピアノの林さんはどこにでも出てくる超多忙ミュージシャンで、みんなすごいやりくり旅スケジュールでの出演でした。クリビツテンギョー（バンドマン用語で、びっくり仰天）は（ジャズ関係者知り合いが多い）世界的なジョン・コルトレーン研究家である大阪のおっちゃん、藤岡靖洋さんにまさかジュアン・レ・パンで会うかいな！？ぼくも関西人で、関西人、ニューヨーカーは会うとモノの５分で友達になれます。今度、コルトレーンハウスにも寄せてください。しかもその場でこちらも知ってるのに会話は初めてエイトアイランド（八島敦子）さん。人生すべてインプロビゼーションですわ、知らんけど。（詳細レポートは JazzTokyo #339を！）

オノセイゲン Seigen Ono
録音エンジニアとして渡辺貞夫「ELIS」（85)、清水靖晃「うたかたの日々」（82)、坂本龍一「戦場のメリークリスマス」（82)、ジョン・ゾーン、マーク・リボウほか多数のアーティストのプロジェクトに参加。一方でスイス、モントルー・ジャズフェス4回出演、『COMME des GARÇONS SEIGEN ONO』ほかアルバム多数。アーティストとして40周年を迎えた。「SACDといい音のVinylレコード」の推進者。
Saidera Records、Saidera Paradiso Ltd.主宰

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Alien Metal by King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard is an interesting experiment for the Australian sextet, moving away from their psychedelic rock roots and going into a electronica & big beat sound from the 90s, but keeping their unique melodies, phrasing and psychedelic leanings. While their previous electronic album The Silver Cord wasn't met with overall praise, I myself was a big fan of it. But with this album it feels rather robotic and cold, and more like an experiment from only some of the band members. With more direction and a bigger conceptual grasp, it could have been more effective but it does feel like a step down from their recent output, but overall it's still fine for what it is. I'd give this a mid 6 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is Sapience.

items._cn_summary: 《异星金属》将六人组的创作重心由迷幻摇滚转向九十年代电子乐与大节拍，同时保留其特有的旋律、句法和迷幻倾向。乐评认为这并非一次全员充分投入的完整构想，机械、冷峻的质感削弱了作品的亲近感；概念若更明确，方向与执行或能更有效。不过，它仍是一次有辨识度的声音实验，对电子及实验音乐听众具有一定吸引力。整体表现约在及格线之上，但相较近期作品有所退步，推荐曲目为《智慧》。

items.body: Beyond Border started out as a duo in 2019 and has since grown into a trio comprising Kai Vincenz Németh, Michael Deiters, and newcomer Renee Brandt. With Aftermath, the German band delivers its third full-length album, produced by none other than Rob Dust. The album is also available as a double CD. Beyond Border remains true to a sound that sits somewhere between classic Electro-Pop and the slightly harder, more dance-oriented Future-Pop genre. Danceability is a key element of this record, an aspect undoubtedly influenced by Rob Dust’s involvement. The album is pure ‘power-pop’, occasionally incorporating guitar riffs to inject even more energy into the mix. What follows is a succession of sensational tracks, sounding like an imaginary fusion of bands such as Mesh, Massive Ego, and Depeche Mode. Terrolokaust and, notably, Ruined Conflict were invited to contribute, with the latter’s collaboration proving particularly infectious thanks to Xavier Morales and his distinctive voice. In terms of production, the album delivers everything one could expect from an Electro/Future-Pop release, while being meticulously crafted down to the finest detail. None of the twelve tracks disappoints. Small details sometimes build towards incredible climaxes, such as the female choral effect that emerges towards the end of the beautiful “Absolution”. The second disc features a solid selection of remixes, including contributions from Mesh themselves, as well as Eisfabrik and Ruined Conflict. While the Mesh and Eisfabrik remixes are my personal favorites, the more EBM-oriented remix by SK3RED also deserves a special mention. “Aftermath” is a fantastic album in every asspect, from its compositions and production to its impressive collection of remixes. As far as I’m concerned, this is an album that is bound to appear on many year-end lists of the best releases of the year. An absolute must-have!!! (Rating:9). Listen to “Absolution”:

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由德国乐队Beyond Border创作，是其第三张全长作品，由Rob Dust担任制作人。整体风格定位于经典电子流行与更具舞曲色彩的未来流行之间，舞曲性是核心特征。十二首曲目延续了同类型乐队如Mesh、Depeche Mode的影响脉络，吉他音色的加入为电子框架注入更多能量。专辑邀请了Ruined Conflict和Terrolokaust参与合作，Xavier Morales的声线为部分曲目增添了辨识度。制作上注重细节，女声合唱效果在《Absolution》尾段构建出层次丰富的情绪顶点。双碟版本收录了Mesh、Eisfabrik、Ruined Conflict等乐队的混音作品，其中EBM取向的SK3RED混音为整体增添了工业色彩。专辑结构完整，编曲扎实，呈现出类型化框架内的成熟制作水准。

items.body:
Trane’s first album as bandleader surfaces on Craft Recordings’ guided reissue tour of classic jazz totems, spotlighting a vital period of modal jazz development from his years with the Prestige label, circa playing with Thelonious Monk and Miles Davis.

Recorded in May, 1957 and published in September that year, ’Coltrane’ marks the point when the great saxophonist began to transcend the acclaim of his peers for much wider recognition, with record sales numbers to follow suit. At the head of band including Red Garland on keys, Paul Chambers’ bass, Albert Heath on sticks, and Sahib Shihab’s baritone sax, Coltrane’s sound matures with a unique balance of smoky quintessence and modal experimentalism that would greatly inform jazz music in moving forward, outward.

That's all ideally illustrated on the daring modal suss of opener ‘Bakai’ with its switches between dervishing brass and angular rhythm to cooler stroll, and the contrast with its proceeding ‘Violets for your Furs’, and again in the closing couplet of ‘While My Lady Sleeps’ with its almost frenzied darts between the romantic and curiously exotic, and extended jazz-blues trip ‘Chronic Blues’.
items._genre: modal jazz / hard bop / post-bop
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是John Coltrane作为乐队领袖的首张录音，1957年5月录制于Prestige厂牌时期，标志着他从同行的认可走向更广泛听众的转折点。乐队编制包括钢琴手Red Garland、贝斯手Paul Chambers、鼓手Albert Heath以及次中音萨克斯手Sahib Shihab，整体呈现出烟雾缭绕的抒情性与调式实验之间的平衡。开场曲《Bakai》在炽烈的铜管与棱角分明的节奏之间反复切换，随后《Violets for your Furs》转入更为沉静的漫步；《While My Lady Sleeps》在浪漫与异国情调间急速跳跃，末曲《Chronic Blues》则展开一段延伸式的爵士蓝调之旅。乐评聚焦于Coltrane在调式爵士成型期的探索，作为Craft Recordings对Prestige经典曲目录的再版发行之一，对爵士史研究有一定参考价值。

Chunky vocal house and kinkier depth by the German veterans of Innervisions, Kompakt, et al, doing it for Tokyo’s finest.

Disciples of Âme’s big chords and haughty NYC-style shunt will be all over the gospel house pomp of ‘Rock A Lott’, primed for the biggest rooms you can lay hands on, whilst ‘Take Me Back’ dials it down to a more purring, prowling deep house swang and parry threaded with blunted vox and Levon Vincent-Like chords.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张以粗粝人声浩室和深沉律动为核心的短篇作品，承接德国电子音乐场景中成熟、讲究俱乐部冲击力的制作传统。标题曲以宏大的和弦、昂扬情绪和宽阔动态，明显面向大型舞池；“带我回去”则收敛为低伏、游移的暗色律动，以钝化人声采样和克制的和弦营造压迫感。整体并不追求前卫结构或复杂跨界，但凭借强烈声响反差、成熟编曲及鲜明的夜间气质，仍能展现两位资深制作人对浩室尺度的精准控制。

Le Orme was formed in Venice in 1966 by Aldo Tagliapietra (voice and guitars), Nino Smeraldi (guitars), Claudio Galietti (guitar and bass) and Marino Rebeschini (drums). Their first album, "Ad Gloriam" was released in 1968. From their psychedelic and beat initial roots, the band moved into much more increasingly sophisticated musical structures. In that line, the band released two excellent albums "Collage" in 1971 and "Uomo Di Pezza" in the following year. Their 1973 album "Felona E Sorona" is widely regarded as one of the top albums in the Italian progressive rock scene. By this time, the band consisted of Tagliapietra (mostly on bass with some guitar) along with keyboard player Tony Pagliuca and drummer Michi Dei Rossi."Felona E Sorona - Deluxe Edition (English And Italian Versions)" is a very special compilation album of Le Orme that was released in 2011. This is an economic package that includes their fourth studio album "Felona E Sorona", released in 1973, in its original Italian version, and their fifth studio album, which is the same album but in its English version and that was also released in the same year. This can be a very interesting compilation album because it includes the two versions of the album. As many of us know, "Felona E Sorona" is in general considered the best work from the band and is also considered a landmark to Italian progressive rock as one of the best and most important progressive rock albums ever made, especially in the Italian progressive rock scene. So, what we have really here is a great album in its two versions, probably at a cheaper price, and what will be a very worthwhile purchase, especially for those who are collectors and huge fans of Le Orme, fans of the Italian progressive rock or fans of the great prog music in general.As I'm going to review these two albums on Progarchives, in a more extensive way, I'm not going to do it at this moment. So, if you are interested to know, in more detail, what I'll write about them later, I invite you to read both of my reviews, in time. However, here I'm going to write something about them in a shorter way. So, of course, I'm not going to analyze them track by track, as I'm going to do, but I'm only going to make a global appreciation of both albums."Felona E Sorona" - Italian Version: "Felona E Sorona" is one of the classic albums of the Italian prog rock scene. The album quickly reached the top of the Italian charts giving the band their second gold record. Like many others, I find "Felona E Sorona" to be Le Orme's most fascinating work. In less than 35 minutes, Le Orme delivers probably their greatest masterpiece. Their high level of musicianship is evident over the all album. The focus is more on mood, song structure, and texture. As a concept work and despite the nine pieces, mostly short pieces and with a lot of variety, the album sounds very homogeneous and less like a collection of individual songs. This is an album that still has a strong influence in the world of progressive rock to the point that La Maschera Di Cera paid tribute to it by extending its theme and even going so far as to take up and transform the superb original cover. "Felona E Sorona" is a true classic of the movement and it's unforgivable not to have it if you like Italian prog rock. "Felona E Sorona" is an absolute must-buy."Felona E Sorona" - English Version: "Felona E Sorona" is a beautiful album, soaked with that 70's flavour that we all prog rock fans love. Although it's by no means technical, the band presents a unique sound that combines vocal parts that exude a unique sense of song with dramatic instrumental parts that make full use of synths and organs to portray a variety of scenes, including lyricism and thrills. It's an album of the golden years of progressive. Like their compatriots Premiata Forneria Marconi and Banco Del Mutuo Soccorso, "Felona E Sorona" was also released in the original Italian version and in the English version. At the request of Tony Stratton-Smith the owner of Charisma Records, Le Orme recorded an English version of the album with lyrics translated by Peter Hammill. It was also entitled "Felona E Sorona" and was also released in 1973. The English album is very similar, except that the vocals were more expressive and appropriate in Italian. This English version is also very good but listen to the Italian version because it's much better.Conclusion: Italian and English versions of the album give the listener the opportunity to hear the English lyrics, and yet enjoy the authentic feel of the original album. Well written notes in both Italian and English, including song lyrics. The essay in these notes gave me a proper understanding of what this album is about, as well as details about the album's production. As a bonus, there are also some band photos and copies of original mixes and vinyl stickers, both English and Italian. However, there's a poor sound quality for the English version. The volume is lower than that of the Italian version, which is a pity. Besides, I strongly prefer the Italian vocals to the English. I think escape to us some of the most important parts of the original album, which are the vocals. I can understand why many people, especially the non-Latin language speakers, prefer the English version. But, definitely, the original is always better than the copy.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)

items.body: Dutch post-punk project Bragolin has cast a looming shadow across the international darkwave scene. For the past eight years, its music has passed from listener to listener through word of mouth and digital playlists assembled with the care once given to hand-dubbed mixtapes. With about 300,000 monthly Spotify listeners, the band now stands among the Netherlands’ most-listened-to contemporary wave exports, drawing an audience far beyond Utrecht. The band began there in 2013, when Edwin van der Velde transferred a guitar riff intended for his Dutch-language project Zwarte Poëzie onto a newly purchased Bass VI. The instrument changed the riff’s character and, with it, the course of his work. That piece became Into Those Woods, the first Bragolin song and a centerpiece of the 2018 debut, I Saw Nothing Good So I Left. The album has since been repressed six times on vinyl, while the track’s baritone hook carried it beyond ten million streams and onto darkwave dance floors around the world. Van der Velde expanded Bragolin in 2019 through Let Out The Noise Inside, a full-album collaboration with Adam Tristar that brought more electronic production into the project. Synth player Edwin Daatselaar joined the following year, establishing the current live duo; both musicians also play in Zwarte Poëzie. Bragolin has since performed more than one hundred shows across Europe and Latin America, including appearances at Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Amphi Festival, Cold Hearted Festival, Extramuralhas, and Kalabalik. The debut has continued to find new listeners as well: seven years after its release, This Grotesque Dance took off on TikTok and is now Bragolin’s most-streamed song, with over 7 million streams on Spotify alone. Bragolin’s third album, I Don’t Like What It Does to Me, retains the Bass VI, organ tones, and dance rhythms at the center of van der Velde’s writing while widening the arrangements with waterphone, synthetic ocean textures, seagull field recordings, strings, and a guitarless piece assembled entirely from layered Clavinets. “Visuals are what draw my attention,” van der Velde says, and references to The Lighthouse, It Follows, The Thing, and Invasion of the Body Snatchers enter these songs as stories of pursuit, artificial replication, surrender, and disappearance. Carrellee joins him on the album’s duet, Feel This Flame Unfold, extending a collaboration that will continue throughout the upcoming North American and European tours. Post-Punk.com spoke with van der Velde about the Nirvana and Björk records that first drew him toward songwriting, growing up beyond Drenthe’s blues and metal scenes, the growth of the Dutch wave underground, and Grauzone’s international role. He also discusses the unlikely longevity of Bragolin’s earliest songs, the backlash surrounding the video for Not All Are Real, the visual rules that keep faces concealed, the band’s first North American tour, and his ambition to develop concept albums and, perhaps one day, a Bragolin film. Bragolin. Photo by Lisanne Lentink Edwin, what were the first records or artists that seized your imagination growing up, and when did listening turn into the desire to write and perform your own music? When I was a kid, I mostly listened to local radio before I got a few pop music cassettes in the early ’90s, which were full of Eurodance. I didn’t care much about music until I discovered alternative music in my mid-teens. Nirvana and Björk were the artists who opened up that world for me. I was fascinated by what felt like the purity of Nirvana’s music, while Björk showed me how unconventional and unique an artist could be. Nevermind, Unplugged, and Post were the first three albums I owned. For most of those later teenage years, I listened almost exclusively to Nirvana. That inspired me to buy a guitar and start writing songs. You can still hear Nirvana’s influence beneath the surface in my music, in the song structures, the desire to write catchy melodies, and even in the way I often add the lyrics later in the songwriting process. Which books and writers had the strongest effect on you during those formative years? Were there particular novels that shaped Bragolin’s fascination with isolation, dread, and the uncanny? I’ve never been much of a reader. I have difficulty focusing on black letters on a white page. Visuals are what draw my attention. While I’m trying to translate the words into images, my mind often drifts off into its own story. I suddenly realize I’m no longer reading the text and have to go back and start again. It’s rare that I truly enjoy reading. So films have had a much bigger influence on me. It’s a shame, because all my life I’ve heard people say that books are so much more interesting than the films. Bragolin’s music and videos seem to draw from post-apocalyptic and horror cinema, including Gothic and folk horror, science-fiction paranoia, body horror, and cosmic horror. Which films first opened those worlds to you, and what do you tend to take from them—the setting, pacing, imagery, or emotional psychology? As a teenager, I was a big fan of the Terminator and Predator films. My dad has always loved action movies, so I grew up watching a lot of the classics with him. Later on, I discovered arthouse cinema, which gradually introduced me to folk horror. The Village (2004) and The Witch (2015) are great examples of the kind of settings and atmosphere I enjoy. I’m especially drawn to the vulnerability of the main character and the mystery and ambiguity of whatever they’re up against. I like to focus on that tension in my lyrics instead of the gore, although I enjoy those films as well. How did growing up in the Netherlands shape your musical imagination? Are there aspects of the Dutch landscape, culture, or temperament that have found their way into Bragolin? I don’t think growing up in the Netherlands consciously shaped Bragolin very much. I grew up in the province of Drenthe, where blues and metal were pretty much the only music scenes around. That made me realize quite early on that I had to look elsewhere to find like-minded people. Having said that, Dutch folklore is something I’d love to explore one day. I think it could make a great concept album. How would you describe the Dutch post-punk and darkwave scene today? Does it possess a character distinct from the scenes you have encountered elsewhere in Europe and Latin America? The Dutch wave scene has improved enormously over the last decade. It’s still a smaller and somewhat more reserved scene compared to our neighbouring countries, but it’s definitely moving in the right direction. Thanks to the hard work of promoters, musicians, and a new generation of fans, the scene has become much more hopeful than it was ten years ago. With festivals like Grauzone, Wavefest, and Momentum, we now have events of a high international standard. Artists like Adam Tristar, Raderkraft, Lifeless Past, De Ambassade, Silent Runners, Camy Huot, Pol, and many more are finding international success. A decade ago, the Dutch wave scene was mostly known internationally because Clan of Xymox came from here. Now there’s a much broader and healthier scene. Bragolin performed at Grauzone in The Hague earlier this year. What was that experience like, and what role has Grauzone played in connecting the Dutch underground with the wider international post-punk community? This year marked our second appearance at Grauzone. We were only announced as a last-minute replacement three days before the festival, so it was great to see such an enthusiastic response from the audience. What I enjoy most about Grauzone is seeing people from both the Dutch and international wave scene together, alongside visitors from outside the scene. Grauzone has made the genre much more accessible to people who might never have considered going to a post-punk or darkwave festival before. I think that’s played a huge role in helping the scene grow in the Netherlands and in connecting the Dutch underground with the wider international community. Can you take us back to the creation of “Into Those Woods”? Which arrived first: the baritone melody, the repeating organ hook, the rhythm, or those images of the manor, the swing, and the mysterious book? This is an interesting question because it was actually the very first Bragolin song I wrote. It all started with that guitar riff I originally had in mind for my other project, Zwarte Poëzie, in early 2013. In mid-2013, I bought a Bass VI, and when I tried the riff on that instrument, everything suddenly clicked. That Bass VI sound became the foundation of Bragolin when I decided to start it as a second project later that year. Because most of Zwarte Poëzie’s lyrics had been about my personal life, I wanted Bragolin to explore different themes. After watching The Evil Dead, I wrote the lyrics inspired by the film. Around that time I was also a big fan of the band The Organ and wanted to use an organ sound instead of relying mainly on synths like many darkwave bands. That became another defining element of Bragolin’s sound. “Into Those Woods” has surpassed fourteen million streams and become a modern darkwave classic. When did you first realize the song had taken on a life beyond the debut album, and how has your relationship with it changed since 2018? I started Bragolin without any expectations. We were just focused on making music the way we wanted to and making it as good as possible. Being in Zwarte Poëzie for eight years had taught me that success was difficult to achieve, although we did have some success with De Laatste Dagen as a minor dancefloor hit while I was working on the first Bragolin album. I assumed “Into Those Woods” might be too catchy and sound too clean for the goth scene, but fortunately I was wrong. The interesting thing is that the song’s reach kept growing year after year. Every year it felt like, “Okay, we’ve probably reached the ceiling now,” but it kept growing. What’s even more surprising is that “This Grotesque Dance” suddenly became a TikTok hit this winter, despite already being out there for seven years. Over the past year, it even surpassed “Into Those Woods” as our most streamed song. I’m very happy that our fans have embraced the new album just as much, and that Bragolin has grown beyond that one song. When we play live, it sometimes feels like we’ve already had a great show and then there’s that moment of, “Oh wait, we still have this song to come.” When you begin writing a Bragolin song now, what form does the first idea usually take? Could you walk us through the process of developing that fragment into a finished arrangement? For me, having a strong hook on top of a danceable beat and bassline is the foundation. I usually put on a drumbeat and play my Bass VI for hours until I find a riff that I like. I then record it and put it aside for weeks or even months. Listening back to a collection of these basic ideas later makes it easier to distinguish which ones have the most potential. After choosing the strongest one, I develop the riff into a song, often starting by humming vocal lines and eventually replacing those with rough lyrics. I then develop those lyrics into a story, which can be inspired by films I’ve recently watched. After that, I layer the song with additional instruments and sound recordings. On the latest album, I put more focus on that layering process than on the first two albums. For the next album, I would like to focus more on having strong foundations again, similar to the approach I took on the first album. “I Run and Hide” sounds heavily guitar-driven, yet its entire instrumental body was constructed from layered Clavinets. How did you record and process those layers, and what did that self-imposed limitation allow you to discover? After the second album, I bought a bunch of new instruments to embrace creativity. One of them was a small electric piano with different sounds built into it. For this song, I ran it through my Bass VI setup, which is why it doesn’t sound too far removed from the way the Bass VI normally sounds. Because it was a piano sound, I wanted to arrange it as if it could actually be played as a piano piece, with a low bass melody and multiple high melodies. I wanted it to feel like one instrument was playing the whole piece. It showed me that by limiting myself to one sound, I could still create a full arrangement with its own character. I Don’t Like What It Does to Me also incorporates field recordings, synthetic ocean textures, waterphones, and other unconventional sources. Could you identify a few moments where those sounds appear and explain how you manipulated them? For this album, I wanted it to have a more cinematic feel. One of the instruments I started using was the waterphone, which is often used in film scores and sound effects. It appears at various moments throughout the album, but it is especially noticeable at the beginning of the title track and This Presence Like a Breeze. This cinematic approach is also why I used a string section at the beginning of “Not All Are Real” to somewhat recreate the feeling of the opening of The Thing (2011), which is a prequel to the classic 1982 film. There are also two songs with ocean-inspired sounds: “Tar With Salt Foam” and “I Salute You Ancient Ocean”. For both songs, I created the sound of ocean waves with my Korg MS-20 by using synthesis rather than recordings of actual waves, while the seagulls were recorded as field recordings. I then processed and layered these sounds into the arrangements to create the atmosphere I was looking for. Where do your lyrics usually begin—with a personal experience, an image, a line from a book, or a scene from a film? How do you turn an outside reference into something that carries your own emotional meaning? It usually starts with a hummed vocal line, and then I look for words that fit the sounds and rhythm of that melody. From there, a few words become the basis of the lyrics. While watching films, I write down how I experience them visually and emotionally from the perspective of the protagonist. But I don’t want to create a direct interpretation of the film. It is more a starting point for my own lyrics, and often I turn it into my own story rather than sticking to the original inspiration. Which artists working in the current post-punk, darkwave, or experimental underground are exciting you most at the moment? Are there any Dutch acts in particular that you believe deserve a much wider audience? My listening has always been broader than just post-punk and darkwave, but from time to time I return to these genres, and there are still artists within the scene that I find very inspiring. I was pleasantly surprised by Carrellee’s music when she joined our record label, Young & Cold Records, with her self-titled 2025 album. I ended up listening to that album on repeat, which led to us getting in contact, collaborating on songs, and working together on upcoming tours. Other artists within our genre that I’ve been enjoying lately are Grundeis, The Woken Trees, The Soft Moon, Boy Harsher, Dead Man’s Bones, and Murder by Death. However, I have mainly been listening to a lot of 60s music, from Ennio Morricone and The Shadows to Nancy Sinatra and Roy Orbison. It is still often dark and melancholic music, and I think I know what elements to take from other genres and what to leave behind when creating my own music. Bragolin’s videos have become an important extension of the songs, from the manor and woodland imagery of “Into Those Woods” to the nocturnal pursuit through streets and cornfields in “I Run and Hide.” How closely involved are you in developing those concepts, and what do you look for in a director? I usually create at least one music video per album myself. For the others, when looking for a director or editor, the most important thing is that they understand the music, respect our visual identity, and have a fitting portfolio. With the new album, I wanted to create more original footage instead of reusing existing material as on previous albums. My role is mainly setting guidelines, such as avoiding showing faces clearly in our visual content. We call this anonymity. This connects with our album covers, which are all portraits shot from behind, and our lyrics, where we also leave room for interpretation rather than explaining everything too clearly. I Run and Hide was made by two very talented film students, Maria Gaedcke and Jonathan Eder. It was our first time working with a larger production. My idea was to combine the inspiration for the song, the film It Follows (2014), with the new album cover’s figure in the nightgown, while taking the opposite approach to the film by not showing the antagonist explicitly. The video for “Feel This Flame Unfold” was created by State of Poison, who had caught our attention with several great animated productions. Animation offered a chance to explore another style, and I’m really happy with how all the videos turned out. For “Not All Are Real,” you connected The Thing and Invasion of the Body Snatchers with contemporary anxiety about artificial replication, using intentionally unnatural AI-generated imagery. What creative and ethical boundaries did you establish for that video, and did the response to it alter your view of the technology? Even though it received quite a lot of negative responses, I still think the concept I wanted to create was only possible in this way. The video is about artificial replication, so using AI-generated imagery became part of the concept itself rather than just a production tool. Filming people in public without their consent would have raised ethical concerns. Emptying the streets of major cities around the world to create a film set and hiring hundreds of actors simply isn’t realistic within the budget of an independent band. Animation, on the other hand, wouldn’t have captured the unsettling feeling of cloned humans that I was looking for. The only real alternative would have been to abandon the concept and make a completely different video. I also found it interesting that we’d previously used existing footage in our videos, which raises ethical questions of its own, yet that never received the same criticism. That said, the reaction was enough for me to decide: never again. Bragolin will embark on its first North American tour this fall. What are you most looking forward to experiencing on this run, and when you look beyond it, where would you like to take Bragolin next—musically, visually, and geographically? We have had a following in North America for a long time, and the requests for us to come over have gone unanswered for many years. I’m mainly looking forward to finally meeting those fans who have been following us from the beginning and hopefully giving them the show they’ve been waiting for. Looking beyond this tour, I’d like Bragolin to remain a constant by continuing to make albums for many years to come. I’d also love to explore the possibility of creating concept albums, which is an element from the past I’d like to bring back to the present, and combine that with even more visual storytelling, perhaps one day creating our own dedicated film. Geographically, there are still plenty of places we haven’t visited. In early 2027, we’re planning a West Coast tour and a return to Latin America.§ Listen to I Don’t Like What It Does To Me below and order the album here. I Don’t Like What It Does To Me by Bragolin Looking towards the horizon, Edwin Van der Velde hopes to expand Bragolin through future concept albums and, eventually, a film devoted to the project’s visual world. Yet, the immediate priority is Bragolin’s first North American tour. Van der Velde and synth player Edwin Daatselaar will take the band on the road alongside Carrellee for the thirty-date North American Hope Tour, beginning September 3 at X-Ray Arcade in the Milwaukee area. Bragolin has maintained a substantial North American audience for years, yet these will be the duo’s first performances on the continent. The route continues through the Midwest, Ontario and Quebec, the Northeast, the South, and Texas before ending October 11 in Tulsa. Bragolin then returns to Europe for dates beginning October 31 in Utrecht and running through December 19 in Brussels, followed by São Paulo and Santiago in February 2027. A separate West Coast tour is also being planned for early 2027, though its dates have yet to be announced. The schedule reflects the unusual way Bragolin’s audience has grown. Into Those Woods accumulated listeners steadily until it passed ten million streams, while This Grotesque Dance found a new audience through TikTok seven years after its release and eventually became Bragolin’s most-streamed song. Those songs reached North America well before the band could follow them. After years of requests from listeners across the continent, van der Velde and Daatselaar will finally meet that audience in person this fall. items._cn_summary: Bragolin是一支来自荷兰乌得勒支的暗潮项目，由Edwin van der Velde于2013年创立，核心乐器为Bass VI，奠定了其低沉阴郁的基底音色。第三张专辑《I Don't Like What It Does to Me》在保持舞曲节奏与管风琴色调的同时，引入了水琴、合成海洋纹理、海鸥田野录音、弦乐以及完全由Clavinet层叠而成的无吉他曲目，拓宽了编曲的声学维度。Van der Velde自称视觉优先，乐曲叙事参考了《灯塔》《它在身后》《怪形》《人体异形》等影片中的追逐、复制与消逝主题。合作歌手Carrellee参与对唱曲目《Feel This Flame Unfold》，并将在北美与欧洲巡演中延续合作。乐队目前月听众约30万，首张专辑中的《This Grotesque Dance》近年因TikTok传播而突破700万播放。

items.body: Magic Wands released the single “Diamond Rain” on August 14, 2026 through Metropolis Records. The Los Angeles duo of vocalists and guitarists Dexy and Chris Valentine mix dream-pop with shoegaze, post-punk and goth, and the track is the first to be lifted from a new Magic Wands album due in early 2027. It is out digitally, with a self-made video posted to the band’s YouTube channel the same day. Diamond Rain by Magic Wands What Magic Wands say about ‘Diamond Rain’ The duo describe the song as deliberately open rather than fixed: “the song doesn’t have one fixed meaning. To us, it’s about moving toward the light, finding beauty after darkness and allowing people to discover their own meaning within it.” They made the accompanying video themselves and explain how the look was built: “using old cameras, lights and mirrors to create textures and effects that give it a dreamlike feeling.” “Diamond Rain” streams and downloads through Bandcamp and the usual digital services. No physical edition has been announced, and the duo have not named the 2027 album or given it a date. ‘Diamond Rain’ follows two EPs and a Peter Murphy remix The single closes an unusually busy eighteen months. The album “Cascades” arrived on October 24, 2025, trailed by the double single “Time To Dream” backed with “Armour (River Remix by Lost Signal)” the previous month. A Delerium remix of “Moonshadow” followed on March 13, 2026. Two EPs came after that. The “Wishing Well” EP, six songs issued on April 24, 2026, was preceded by its title track in February and by “Sacred Mirrors”, a January 2026 collaboration with John Ashton of The Psychedelic Furs. The six-track “Remixes” EP landed on June 12, 2026 and reworked material from “Cascades”. In between, the pair remixed Peter Murphy; Side-Line covered that single when Peter Murphy released “Swoon (Magic Wands Remix)” on May 29, 2026. About Magic Wands Magic Wands formed in Nashville in 2008 around Dexy and Chris Valentine, who share vocals and guitars, and later moved to Los Angeles. Metropolis Records describes their sound as heavily textured guitars, droning synths and ethereal vocals. The duo have released through Metropolis for over a decade. Side-Line first covered them in April 2022 around the single “Fortune”, then the single “Time” in May 2023 and the remix album and tour that August. The album “Switch” followed in 2023 and was reviewed here that September. “Cascades” came in October 2025 and drew the run of singles, remixes and EPs that “Diamond Rain” now brings to a close, with the next album set for early 2027.

items.body: Swedish electro artist EMMON released “Relics (Agent Side Grinder Remix)” on 14 August 2026 through Icons Creating Evil Art. The track is the third remix issued ahead of “ICONMIXED”, a remix album scheduled for 23 October 2026. Jimmy Monell produced and mixed the new version, Hans Olsson mastered it, and Emma Nylén is credited as writer. The original “Relics” is the eighth track on “ICON“, the album EMMON released on 17 October 2025 with Emanuel Åström as guestvocalist. Agent Side Grinder move it off its EBM footing and into house tempo, adding LinnDrum programming, a Euro-disco riff and acid basslines. Johan Lange of Agent Side Grinder set out what the duo changed: “Had a great time remixing my dear friend Emmon (and a certain obscure guest singer). I took the EBM-driven original and pushed it in a more ’90s house direction, with LinnDrum, a Euro disco riff and plenty of acid basslines.” Two reworkings of “Speak to Me” preceded it, one by SIIE and one by Copenhagen trio The Foreign Resort. “ICONMIXED” reworks material from “ICON” across a wider set of collaborators. Icons Creating Evil Art issued an official video for the original “Relics” the same day. Niklas Kärreskog directed it, with Tyko Lann Lundin as editing assistant and Joakim Kärreskog on technical resources. Kärreskog set out his reference points in the video credits: “Relics could easily be part of the soundtrack to a film adaptation of William Gibson’s Neuromancer. That’s why I aimed for a cyberpunk aesthetic inspired by Ridley Scott’s Alien (1979) and Shinya Tsukamoto’s Tetsuo (1989). To achieve this, the video was processed through a CRT television and many metres of cable.” EMMON has run this pattern before. “RECON” arrived in 2022 and drew a full companion remix record a year later; “ICONMIXED” applies the same treatment to the newer album. About EMMON EMMON is the solo project of Swedish artist and producer Emma Nylén, based in Stockholm and signed to Icons Creating Evil Art. Her earlier catalogue runs from “The Art and The Evil” and “Closet Wanderings” through “Nomme”, “AON” and “Under Construction”, built on hard synth basslines, clipped vocals and melodic electro structures. “RECON” followed on 7 October 2022 and reopened that catalogue after an extended gap. Its eleven tracks include “Machines”, “Like A Drum” and “Purebloods”, a duet with Agent Side Grinder vocalist Emanuel Åström that set up the working relationship behind the current remix. On 6 October 2023 EMMON issued “RECONMIXED”, a thirteen-track companion that handed “Machines”, “Reconstruction”, “Purebloods” and others to Ultra Sunn, Tobias Bernstrup, Sex Kino, Harlem, Fred White, Maschine Brennt, Majestoluxe, ZackZackZack, Potochkine and Livmødr. The “XCEPTION” EP came next, then “ICON” on 17 October 2025, a ten-track album covering “Neon Brown”, “Decisions”, “Shades of Blue”, “Cold Within”, “No Mans Land”, “Speak to Me”, “Blood on the Ceiling feat. Majestoluxe”, “Relics”, “DARK” and “Slow Running”. Icons Creating Evil Art issued it on vinyl, CD and digital. Side-Line covered that release and published an EMMON interview in February 2026. The rollout toward “ICONMIXED” started with SIIE and The Foreign Resort on “Speak to Me” and continues with Agent Side Grinder on “Relics”. The album is due on 23 October 2026.

items._cn_summary: 本文报道瑞典电子艺术家EMMON与Agent Side Grinder合作的单曲混音版本发布详情。混音将原作的EBM根基转化为九十年代浩室节奏，引入LinnDrum编程、欧陆迪斯科riff与酸性贝斯线。专辑制作由Jimmy Monell完成，Hans Olsson负责母带处理。同期发布的官方MV以赛博朋克美学为视觉方向，导演Niklas Kärreskog借鉴了《异形》与《铁男》的影像风格，通过CRT电视与大量线材实现复古画面质感。EMMON此前已通过《RECON》与《RECONMIXED》建立原专辑加混音专辑的发行模式，此次延续相同策略推出《ICONMIXED》。文章以新闻稿形式介绍作品背景、制作人员与合作历史，对音乐本身的听感与艺术价值缺乏深入评述。

items.body: London-based queer alt-metal artist Ray Noir releases “Gothstar” on 13 August 2026, a rave-metal single featuring New York alternative artist Danny Blu. The track is the final single ahead of Ray Noir’s second EP, also titled “Gothstar,” scheduled for 17 September 2026. A label, catalogue number and full tracklist for the EP have not been confirmed. Ray Noir “Gothstar” EP release date and earlier singles The “Gothstar” EP is scheduled for 17 September 2026 and follows three 2026 singles building up to the EP release. “Label Whxre” arrived on 2 April 2026, the release on which Kerrang! reported the EP as a “rave meets metalcore” record. “Black” followed on 14 May 2026, produced by Jon Cass and written with Tom Saint. “Boys” was issued as the third single. KALTBLUT magazine reported in April 2026 that the EP would include a collaboration with Danny Blu without naming the track, and now the 13 August release confirms that collaboration as the title track. “Gothstar” The single combines techno, metalcore and rave production. Promotional material for the release describes the track as moving from the Berlin club Berghain “straight into the mosh pit,” and frames its themes as goth glamour, queer confidence and self-expression. “Gothstar” is also the name of the character at the centre of the EP, and the EP’s title track. Ray Noir released an official music video with the single. Both artists of course appropriately in black leather 😉 “Gothstar” release party in London Ray Noir will host a free release party at Slim Jim’s Liquor Store in London on 19 September 2026. Tickets are listed via DICE. About Ray Noir Ray Noir is a queer alternative artist based in London. According to his official biography, his background is in Oslo’s black-metal underground, and his sound combines metal guitars with electronic club production. He began releasing solo material with the single “Double Trouble” in 2014 and has since worked with a range of underground collaborators. His 2024 mixtape “Scorpio” reached the top five of the German Alternative Charts according to his official biography, and drew coverage from Kerrang! and BBC Radio 1. The 2025 EP “Against the Machine” followed and featured guitarist Steve Stevens. In 2026 he released “Temptation” and “Breathe,” then opened the “Gothstar” campaign with “Label Whxre,” “Black” and “Boys.” Live, his official biography lists sold-out headline shows in London and Oslo, multiple UK tours, performances in Tokyo and at Flow Festival in Finland and Resistanz Festival in the UK, and support slots for Combichrist and Die Krupps. His work in fashion, including with Marc Jacobs and Vivienne Westwood, was cited by KALTBLUT magazine as an influence on “Label Whxre.” No Wikipedia article for Ray Noir surfaced during verification, and Discogs did not return a matching profile, so discography formats and catalogue numbers could not be cross-checked. About Danny Blu Danny Blu is an alternative artist based in New York and the former frontman of Echo Black. He relaunched his solo project with the single “Bubble” in 2019 and released the EPs “The Pale Horse” and “Molotov” in 2021. “Gothstar” is his first confirmed recorded collaboration with Ray Noir.

items._cn_summary: 伦敦酷儿另类金属艺人Ray Noir发布单曲《Gothstar》，与纽约另类艺人Danny Blu合作，将techno、metalcore与锐舞制作手法融合在一起，官方宣传定位为从柏林Berghain俱乐部直冲入mosh pit的跨越体验。主题围绕哥特魅惑、酷儿自信与自我表达展开，曲名同名的角色成为整张EP的核心叙事线索。音乐人背景涉及奥斯陆黑金属地下场景，将金属吉他质感与电子俱乐部制作并置，此前作品曾获Kerrang!与BBC Radio 1关注。EP将收录此前发行的《Label Whxre》《Black》《Boys》等单曲，并附有Slim Jim's Liquor Store的免费发布派对。在跨界融合方面，rave与metalcore的碰撞以及暗潮美学与俱乐部文化的衔接具有一定实验意味，但整体仍属于类型框架内的常规操作，文章以新闻发布为主，缺少对音乐本体声响与结构的深入评析。

items.body: Los Angeles band Bizou will release the six-track EP “Widow” on Moonboot Records on 25 September 2026. The band recorded, mixed and mastered the EP at The Cave Studio in Los Angeles. “Death Mag” is the track already streaming with the digital pre-order. Bizou put six tracks on ‘Widow’, recorded at The Cave Studio “Widow” runs “Deep REM”, “Widow”, “No One Can Have You”, “Death Mag”, “Ahead” and “Losing My Memory”. “Death Mag” runs 4:20. The line-up on the EP is Marisa Prietto on lead vocals, synth, bass and guitar, Josiah Mazzaschi on guitar, synth, programming and backing vocals, Nicole Fiorentino on bass and backing vocals, and Nicki Nevlin on guitar. Digital pre-orders are open on Bandcamp, with the download offered in 24-bit/44.1kHz. A “Widow” listening party is listed for 24 September 2026, the day before release. The EP is Bizou’s first new music since the single “Ursula” in October 2023. It is also their first release on Moonboot Records; the band issued their 2018 to 2021 records themselves. Widow by Bizou About Bizou Bizou formed in Los Angeles in 2017 around lead vocalist Marisa Prietto, guitarist and producer Josiah Mazzaschi, bassist Nicole Fiorentino and guitarist Nicki Nevlin. Prietto had previously sung with Wax Idols and Glaare, Mazzaschi came from Light FM, and Fiorentino had played bass with Smashing Pumpkins and Veruca Salt. The band describe their sound on Bandcamp as “driving post-punk bass + wall of sheeny shoegaze guitars + shifting scales of synths + the propulsive rhythms of darkwave […] all fused together with dreamy vocals”, naming Curve, Cranes, Garbage and PJ Harvey as reference points. Bizou opened with the single “Superstition” on 25 October 2018. The self-titled EP “Bizou” followed on 1 March 2019 on cassette and digital, then the EP “stilllifeburning” on 10 April 2020. The nine-track debut album “Tragic Lover” arrived on 4 June 2021, also recorded at The Cave Studio. Two singles closed that phase: an LCD Soundsystem cover, “Tribulations”, on 24 July 2023, and “Ursula” on 20 October 2023. Prietto and Mazzaschi reconvened at The Cave Studio in the summer of 2025. Those sessions produced “Widow”, which now brings Bizou back after nearly three years without a release.

items.body: Swiss pianist and composer Raphael Loher releases “Figuren” on 4 September 2026 through the Lucerne publishing platform Präsens Editionen. The eight-track album comes out digitally and as a limited vinyl edition with artwork and four inlays by Ukrainian-American artist Mykola Haleta. Loher built the record from his own concert recordings rather than from new performances. The tracks are titled “Figuren I” through “Figuren VIII”. Figuren by Raphael Loher How Raphael Loher made ‘Figuren’ The source material is ten intimate concert recordings of Loher performing pieces from “Keemuun”, his debut album. He took those tapes into a residency in the Blenio Valley in Ticino, where he separated out individual melodies, tones and resonances and reassembled them into new configurations. That work produced around thirty initial pieces and also fed his second album, “Hug of Gravity”. He then ran the fragments through a Revox B77 tape machine, shifting their pitch before digitising and reshaping them again. The results range from layered rhythmic microstructures to sparse melodic fragments and long looping passages. Präsens Editionen describes the album as “shaped by intuition, experimentation, and a deliberate distance from his primary instrument – the piano.” Loher expands the piano itself with preparations, effect pedals and tape, which puts the record closer to ambient and electronic composition than to solo piano recital. Raphael Loher live dates 2026 Loher tours Europe from the release date onward: 4 September – Meakusma Festival, Eupen, Belgium (solo) 5 September – Bad Bonn Kilbi, Düdingen, Switzerland (solo, and with Remo Helfenstein) 12 September – Trial & Error Festival, Tribute to Franziska Lingg, Lucerne, Switzerland 30 September – Periscope, Lyon, France (solo) 3 October – Festival Pour Les Oiseaux, Le Havre, France (solo) 30 October – Heiliggeistkapelle, Lucerne, Switzerland (solo) About Raphael Loher Raphael Loher is based in Lucerne, Switzerland, and combines experimental electronic music, ambient and minimalist composition in his work. His debut solo album “Keemuun” came out on three:four records in October 2022. His second, “Hug of Gravity”, followed on the Swiss experimental label Hallow Ground in 2025. He plays in two trios. Baumschule pairs him with guitarist Manuel Troller and drummer Julian Sartorius for long-form improvisation, also released through three:four records. KALI Trio, formed in 2015 with guitarist Urs Müller and drummer Nicolas Stocker, released its third album “The Playful Abstract” in early 2025, and co-wrote the score for “Nemesis”, the documentary by Swiss director Thomas Imbach, alongside Lukas Langenegger. Loher has also played and recorded with Gerry Hemingway of the Anthony Braxton Quartet and with Martina Lussi. He has toured across Europe and appeared at the Montreux Jazz Festival, Willisau Jazz Festival, Cully Jazz Festival, One Of A Million Festival, Jazzfestival Schaffhausen and Unerhört Festival, among others, and his records have been played on BBC 6 Music and BBC Radio 3. “Figuren” is his third album and his first for Präsens Editionen, a Lucerne platform founded in 2011 that publishes magazines, books and records. It moves his catalogue further from live piano documentation and towards tape-based composition.

items._cn_summary: 瑞士钢琴家与作曲家 Raphael Loher 发布新专辑《Figuren》，收录八首曲目，素材并非来自新录音，而是取自其首张专辑《Keemuun》的十场小型音乐会现场录音。他在提契诺布勒尼奥山谷的驻留期间将旋律、单音与共鸣逐一分离重组为约三十段雏形，并经过 Revox B77 开盘磁带机变速处理、重新数字化与塑形。最终成品涵盖层叠的节奏微观结构、稀疏的旋律碎片以及长循环段落，融合钢琴预制、效果器踏板与磁带操作，跨越氛围与电子作曲领域。发行方为卢塞恩独立厂牌 Präsens Editionen，提供数字与限量黑胶版本，邀请乌克兰裔美国艺术家 Mykola Haleta 担纲美术设计。发行后将巡演欧洲多个场地。

items.body: German electronic composer Volker Rapp released “Silent Running” on 14 August 2026 through the Argentine label Cyclical Dreams. The 18-track album follows the narrative of Douglas Trumbull’s 1972 science-fiction film of the same name, and is out digitally and as a CD edition. Rapp traces the project back more than fifty years. He states: “Silent Running has been one of my favorite films ever since I saw it on German television on April 26, 1974.” How Volker Rapp built ‘Silent Running’ The tracklist reads as a synopsis. It opens with “The last forests of Earth” and “The arks Berkshire, Valley Forge, Sequoia and Mojave”, introduces “Freeman Lowell, gardener and guardian”, then moves through “Daily Routine”, “Service robots Dewey, Huey and Louie”, “Order to destroy the domes”, “What are we doing here”, “Lonely Decision #1”, “Realising the Domes”, “Silent Running to Saturn”, “The Lord of the Rings”, “Through the Rings and Louie is lost”, “Berkshire is calling”, “Remorse”, “Lonely Decision #2”, “Preparing the Last Dome and Dewey”, “Valley Forge and Lowell are lost” and “Infinity”. Those titles track the film closely. In Trumbull’s picture, Bruce Dern plays botanist Freeman Lowell, who tends the last of Earth’s forests in domes aboard the freighter Valley Forge near Saturn, assisted by three service drones he names Huey, Dewey and Louie. Trumbull had supervised the special photographic effects on “2001: A Space Odyssey” in 1968; “Silent Running” was the first of only two features he directed, the other being “Brainstorm” in 1983. He died on 7 February 2022. Rapp built the record around period-correct instrumentation, working with the ARP 2600 and SEM alongside a Juno 6, Prophet 5, MS-20, DX7 and Synclavier, plus Arturia software. He is explicit that the album stands on its own rather than functioning as a replacement score, noting: “This version is not synchronized with the film; it runs 73 minutes compared to 85 minutes in the 2002 DVD version.” Silent Running [CYD 0164] by vOLKER rAPP Cyclical Dreams handled the artwork; Amp Puttipong supplied the photography. About Volker Rapp Volker Rapp was born on 10 October 1964 in Wuppertal, Germany, and works as a composer, musician, photographer and writer. He ran the Demo Art project from 1992 to 2005 and has also recorded as part of the duo Volker & Volker. His recent output has come almost entirely through Cyclical Dreams, the Buenos Aires label founded in early 2020 by Pablo Bilbao, Lucas Tripaldi and Esteban Menash, which concentrates on Berlin School, ambient, soundscape, space music and drone. Rapp’s titles for the label include “d7-d5” in March 2023, “Blade Runner 2099” in July 2024 and “Phase IV”. Earlier self-released records include “Mars Missions 2021”, issued in February 2021, along with “Declination”, “DUNE Spots”, “Valletta (il-Belt)”, “St. Petersburg” and “Session 8 – My Tribute to Klaus Schulze”. Film and space themes run through most of that catalogue, and Cyclical Dreams has released comparable long-form work by other artists in the same field, including D*Time’s “Nightwoven” in May 2026 and Christian Wittman’s “Andromeda” in January 2026. “Silent Running” is Rapp’s longest sequence for the label to date and his most direct treatment of a single film.

items._cn_summary: 德国电子作曲家Volker Rapp于2026年8月通过阿根廷厂牌Cyclical Dreams发行了18轨专辑《Silent Running》，灵感源自Douglas Trumbull 1972年的同名科幻电影。专辑以电影叙事为线索，从地球最后的森林讲到主角Lowell驾驶飞船飞越土星环的孤独旅程。Rapp使用ARP 2600、SEM、Prophet 5、MS-20、DX7等复刻时代感的合成器硬件，搭配Arturia软件构建声响。这张作品定位为独立聆听体验而非电影配乐替代品，时长73分钟。Rapp长期活跃于Demo Art项目及Volker & Volker二人组，近年作品多由专注柏林学派、环境音景与太空音乐的Cyclical Dreams厂牌发行。该厂牌由布宜诺斯艾利斯三位创办人于2020年成立，是南美电子音乐场景中的活跃力量。

items.body: Belgian dark electro and EBM project Deadly Sins has issued “Red”, a six-track digital EP on the Antwerp label DressCode Black. The label sets 21 August 2026 as the release date across streaming platforms; the EP went up on the label’s Bandcamp page on 12 August. C.VII produced the record and Arnte handled the mastering. The EP pairs the original with an alternate reading and four remixes: “Red”, “Red (Mystic Classic Version)”, “Red (Novakill Remix)”, “Red (Pyrroline Remix)”, “Red (Dreadfool Remix)” and “Red (SEXGUN Remix)”. DressCode Black describes the remix set as “four radically different interpretations from prominent artists within the international underground scene, alongside the atmospheric Mystic Classic Version of the original.” Red by DEADLY SINS The four remixers pull the track in different directions. Pyrroline reworks it as electro-industrial, Novakill pushes it towards the dancefloor, Dreadfool takes it into harder EBM, and SEXGUN strips it back to a minimal, repetitive form. Deadly Sins at La Luna Obscura in Ostend The release date coincides with a live appearance. Deadly Sins plays the second edition of La Luna Obscura at Elysée in Ostend, Belgium, on Friday 21 August 2026. The Friday bill also carries Haujobb, This Morn’ Omina, Cattac, Matt Hart and Skren. This Morn’ Omina’s set marks 30 years of the project, which Mika Goedrijk started in Roeselare in 1996. Haujobb last released the album “The Machine in the Ghost” in September 2024. About Deadly Sins Deadly Sins is the solo project of C.VII, one half of the Belgian EBM duo WÜLF7, which he formed in 2017 with Sebastian Blondwulf. WÜLF7 describe their own style as DEBM, short for Dark Electro Body Melancholic. Working alone as Deadly Sins, C.VII combines EBM rhythms, dark electro arrangements and industrial textures with lyrics written in the first person. The project’s first release was the EP “Preface”, also on DressCode Black. DressCode Black is based in Antwerp and operates as a sub-label of Detroit-Berlin, releasing EBM, electro, new wave and industrial records. Its catalogue includes Darkvolt, Rogue Unit, Causenation, Mindshore, The Ordure and Atoms Inc., with remix work from Rhys Fulber, CJ Bolland, Orphx, Blac Kolor and Statiqbloom across earlier titles. “Red” continues the label’s run of remix-led singles and EPs, and lands the same day Deadly Sins takes the La Luna Obscura stage.

items.body: Minimal synth and darkwave artist Nao Katafuchi has released the video for “Lonely Fire”, the title track of the album Kernkrach issued on 26 June 2026. Vienna-based video artist Berivan Sayici handled direction, camera and editing. It is the second video taken from the record, following “Kieta Ashita”, which Christopher Gorski shot and directed in Hamburg. Katafuchi describes the song as a piece about keeping hope intact when the surrounding circumstances do not cooperate. Its central line runs: “Even if all else fails, your treasure remains the same.” What is on the Nao Katafuchi album ‘Lonely Fire’ The album runs ten tracks: “Kieta Ashita”, “Lonely Fire”, “Love And Superstitions”, “A Flash Point”, “All For Nothing”, “Anesthesia”, “In Between Times”, “A Sensetive Matter”, “Crying In The Shadow” and “State Of Mind”. Katafuchi sings in both Japanese and English across the record, over analogue synthesizer and drum-machine arrangements. Kernkrach pressed it in an edition of 150 hand-numbered copies on black vinyl with a silk-screen print and an insert. The label, based in Münster and founded in 2002 by Jörg Steinmeyer, has specialised in minimal wave, NDW and synth-pop for over two decades, and had already co-issued Katafuchi’s 2019 LP “Stahlgrau”. The album is also available digitally through the label’s Bandcamp page. Lonely Fire by NAO KATAFUCHI The video arrives after a run of South American shows. In July 2026 Katafuchi toured Latin America alongside Je T’aime and Staatseinde, playing Bogotá, Santiago, Lima and Mexico City. About Nao Katafuchi Nao Katafuchi grew up in the suburbs of Tokyo and moved to New York in the early 1990s, settling on the Lower East Side. He began performing under his own name in the orbit of Wierd Records, the label and weekly party that anchored the city’s minimal synth revival. His debut EP “Yumegoto” appeared on WT Records in 2012, followed by the LP “Émergence” on Nadanna, a sister label of Anna Logue Records, in 2015. He relocated to Germany in late 2015 and has been based there since. His third record, the LP “Stahlgrau”, came out in autumn 2019 as a joint release between Kernkrach, TONN Recordings and Castle Records. Live, he has shared stages with ChameleonsVox, Rational Youth, Psyche, Attrition and Parade Ground. His music mixes cold, cinematic synthesizer textures with a vocal approach that sits closer to spoken melancholy than to conventional singing, and he alternates Japanese and English lyrics on record. “Lonely Fire”, released in June 2026, is his fourth full-length and his second album issued with Kernkrach’s involvement. The new title-track video is the second clip drawn from it.

items.body: Top PicksExist – Beyond Purpose (proggy prog-death)I was going to write up the new Warforged album, but I've been in bed sick all day, so I don't haven't had the time or energy to listen to it yet, let alone think about and evaluate it. Instead, I'm going to recommend this new Exist EP, which not only had the courtesy of dropping a couple of days earlier, but is also only a polite three tracks and seventeen minutes long! This more compact presentation goes a long way toward making this sort of music more easily digestible, and also might just be the best seventeen minutes Exist have put out yet. I very much appreciated the more progressive direction they took on previous full-length Hijacking the Zeitgeist (2024), and the band have only leaned harder into that direction here, while also bringing a more modern-sounding, heavy edge to things. If nothing else, it serves as a fantastic appetiser to this week's more substantial and dense progressive metal offering(s), and hopefully Exist's future direction as well. items.album: Event Review: Viljandi Folk Music Festival 2026 (Viljandi, Estonia; Thursday 23rd to Sunday 26th July 2026)
