items.body: It is Monday morning, checkout time at Grand Hotel Viljandi, and a German festival goer with his wristband still on hands back his room card and asks what a double costs. Not for tonight, he specifies, for the same weekend next July, when Viljandi Folk comes round again, and preferably the very same room he has just spent four nights in. The receptionist explains that the system will not take a booking more than 11 months out. He takes this badly. He has plainly been turning it over for a while, perhaps since Thursday’s wild folk dances, perhaps during the downpour on Sunday night just before the grand finale, and now there is nothing to be done with the thought except carry it home.  That is a fairly standard state to leave Viljandi in. The town has something to do with it. Seventeen thousand people live on a ridge above a long glacial lake in southern Estonia, forest running down to the water on the far shore and the ruins of a 13th-century Livonian Order castle at the centre, the ground falling away in wide grass terraces cut by deep ravines. Those terraces are the festival: four outdoor stages sitting in the folds of the hills, Kaevumägi (Well Hill) at the top, the two Cherry Hills (Kirsimägi I & II) below it, and the Song Festival Grounds down on the flat. Two indoor rooms handle the rest: the Traditional Music Centre beside the ruins, the Ait or granary as locals call it, and the Sakala Centre in town, carrying the quieter programme by day and the wilder dances by night. Everything is ten minutes’ walk from everything else. To cross between Kaevumägi and the ruins you take the suspension bridge, 50 metres of it slung over a 13-metre trench and still swaying under everyone who steps on. Black sheep graze the slopes throughout, unbothered by any of it. And the festival is not only up on the ticketed grounds. It spills straight down into the old town, where two free stages run from lunchtime to eleven at night across all four days: the Green Stage on Laidoneri Square, where the dance schools set out workshops so anyone can learn the steps, and Sõprade Hoov on Lossi Street, a village-party yard open to any musician who fancies a turn. Seventy concerts happen out here, matching the paying stages exactly, strung along a street lined with a craft and design market where nobody checks a wristband. The programmed players are only half of it. Buskers of every age sprout across town, under gazebos and on pavements, some barely tall enough to hold the instrument, playing to whoever slows down. What carries across those slopes, alleyways and squares is pärimusmuusika, a word the English ‘folk’ flattens badly. For four days in late July this town does not commemorate its traditions so much as live inside them and shove them somewhere new. Most of what you hear sits on archival foundations: village fiddle tunes, bagpipe repertoire, regilaul runic song, the older Estonian and Finno-Ugric layers that were collected, catalogued and came within a generation of vanishing. Yet none of it is handled as museum material. This year’s theme, ‘To Each Their Own Instrument,’ was taken literally. Stages were packed with uncommon, traditional instruments most people couldn’t name, and within a day half of them were queuing to try one. Inside the Ait, the festival kept a second timetable. On three of the four nights, Thursday, Friday and Saturday, its great hall turned into Tantsumaja, the dance house, running from around 11pm until three or four in the morning while a rotating cast of folk musicians kept the tunes coming in relay. What happened on the floor was not a taught routine so much as a shared fluency: circles and couples moved through the room side by side, skill levels visibly ranging from a first attempt to real virtuosity, yet the general standard stayed remarkably high, dancers who had grown up on this repertoire picking out the shape of a tune they had never heard before and finding the steps inside it before the first verse was out. It all began, as it always does, with the parade winding through town on the Thursday early afternoon, before mayor Jaak Pihlak handed the ceremonial key to festival chief Ando Kiviberg, who has run this since its first edition in 1993. Just over 7,000 people came through the gates across that afternoon and evening, more day-one pass buyers than last year. In the Ait, six students turned the theme into a play, To Each Their Own Instrument, staged by director Lee Taul with a cast drawn from the Viljandi Culture Academy, the Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre and Tartu’s Eller college. Bagpipe, kannel and Teppo-type accordion were carried through the story by players still young enough to be studying them, the archive walking and talking rather than sitting in a case. The same idea took physical form a few streets over, on Pikk Street beside St John’s Church, where Pilliküla opened to the public for the first time: an ‘instrument village’ of close to 80 free workshops where anyone could sit down with a teacher and coax a first note out of a kannel, a bagpipe, a jaw harp, a fiddle, a talharpa or an accordion. “Musical heritage lives on as long as playing an instrument is common enough among the people,” Kiviberg said of the idea behind Pilliküla, the point being that a tradition survives by being played, not preserved. You could see the results all over town that weekend. Children busked on the hills and street corners with whatever they could play, one girl of maybe twelve and her violin set up between two stages with her case open for coins, taking more by evening than some of the market stalls. Up on the stages, the theme got loud. On II Kirsimägi that first afternoon, Gangar dug century-old dance tunes out of Norway’s national archives and ran them through a rock band. The Oslo five-piece build off springar and gangar rhythms, the old triple-time and walking dances they take their name from, Hardanger fiddle ringing over a rhythm section that a rhythm section hammering underneath, and drive the lot flat out. They played here in 2022, so they knew the crowd would dance, and it did. Down on the Song Festival Grounds, the sounds pulled from much further away. The Zawose Queens held the first Tanzanian booking in Viljandi’s history, and the sky opened just as they were due on, the kind of delay that empties a field. It did not. People pulled up hoods and waited, and by the time Pendo Zawose and her niece Leah came on, the wait had sharpened the air: Wagogo polyphony over ilimba thumb pianos and chizeze fiddle, a London rhythm section laying psychedelic rock beneath, a rain-soaked crowd that had chosen to be there. Their grandfather Hukwe Zawose carried this music around the world but never once let the women of his family sing lead; two generations on, his daughter and granddaughter stood at the front of the stage. The rain never really let up on the first evening, and neither did the appetite for dancing in it. Manhu closed Kaevumägi from half nine, five Sani players from the farming villages of the Stone Forest of Yunnan, together since 2003. They build from the lusheng, a bamboo mouth-organ whose drone sets the whole thing running, then stack the three-string adiza and call-and-response singing on top, with bass and drum kit worked so far underneath that the village music always keeps the upper hand. This is the sound of Sani daily life, drinking songs, welcome songs, love songs, seasonal tunes, nearly all of it built to move to, and they run a set the same way: a tune, a stop to walk the crowd through the steps, then the tune again, faster. Not a full sentence of English passed between the five of them and none was needed. One lifted a single leaf to his lips and bent a melody out of it; the steps were called by demonstration, arms up, follow this. By the last stretch a cold, soaked Estonian crowd that had never heard Sani music in its life was strung across the grass doing Yunnan courtship dances in the rain. Outdoors, the weather could be worn like a badge. Indoors, it exposed the festival’s one real weakness. Early shows had already packed the Ait to the walls. Over at the Sakala Centre, TõnisMägi, whose “Koit” became an anthem of the 1988 Singing Revolution, sold out fast enough to leave a queue stranded at a closed door, though these days the noise around him owes as much to his divisive public stances as to his songs. It happened repeatedly over the next three days: too many people, too few seats, and indoor rooms never built for crowds this size. Friday opened, in the early afternoon, on Ruhnu, with music and tales that had come closer than most to disappearing for good. Sounds and Stories from Ruhnu Island takes its name from a speck in the Gulf of Riga, Runö in Swedish, that held a few hundred ethnic Swedes and their own fiddle tradition until 1944, when the Soviet advance emptied the island almost overnight and left the repertoire alive only on tape. Fiddlers Karoliina Kreintaal and Lee Taul, with storyteller Kairi Leivo, have spent years playing it back off those recordings, and here they did it as a one-off. Ruhnu-born storyteller Jüri Keskpaik told the island’s life from the inside, its weddings, feasts, church and sea, while three members of the Nordic supergroup Groupa sat in: fiddler Mats Edén, flautist Jonas Simonson, and Terje Isungset, the Norwegian percussionist who builds his instruments from wood, stone and ice, all three back on Kaevumägi a few hours later for Groupa‘s own set. Behind them the whole time ran the island itself, archive film of Ruhnu’s shoreline, its people, customs and dances, a vanished community moving on screen while its own tunes played live underneath. Later that afternoon Mari Kalkun, born and raised in the Võru country of Estonia’s south-east and one of the few keeping its endangered Võro language sung, brought her kannel up against the kokle of Latvian player Laima Jansone. The kannel and the kokle are cousins, box zithers grown from the same ancient Baltic instrument and drifted so far apart that their traditions barely recognise one another now. Set them back together and that separation is nowhere to be heard: Kalkun’s playing drifting and psychedelic, her voice carrying the Võro songs she has spent a career prising out of the archive, against Jansone’s harder, more rhythmic attack, the two instruments circling, answering, now and then locking into a single line as though they had never parted. Then Kalkun left the stage entirely, microphone in hand, and walked into the middle of the field to sing from there, the crowd falling quiet and closing around her as she moved. In the evening, Amaro Duho kept their tradition in the family, literally. Matild Dobi assembled the band in 2021 from her own children, four decades after she helped start Ando Drom, one of the great names in Hungarian Roma music, and the point was to hold the songs together rather than let them scatter. It showed. Oláh Roma tradition on guitar, tambura and accordion, their own tunes threaded through the inherited ones, all of it played with the loose, unforced ease of people who do this around a table at home and happened, that night, to be doing it in front of a few thousand strangers. Estonian tradition can be handled far less gently, and Mandoterror proved it: a distorted rhythm section and a mandolin screaming where a lead guitar should be, five players who take Estonian folk melody and hit it at Nordic-metal weight. Kristjan Kuusmik stood out front on vocals, Tanel Sakrits‘ mandolin carrying the tunes a fiddle would usually hold, the old material cranked through songs from last year’s Nõiajaht and the anthem ‘Oru Leeni’. There is no compromise in it. The melodies land as though they were originally written for the extra volume: fast, sharp, and carrying clean across the grounds. The bigger stages found their real heat once it got dark, starting with Zetod on the Song Festival Grounds, the set that, by the reckoning of more or less everyone there, was where the festival properly began. Formed in Värska in 2003, they take Seto leelo, the old polyphonic singing of Estonia’s south-eastern border country, and play it at the speed and volume of a punk band: short hard songs stacked back to back, every word in Seto dialect, the pit moving from the first number and a whole field firing the lines back. In keeping with the year’s theme they built the set around four fiddles, one apiece, over accordion, bass and drums, the old dance tunes and archive material driven hard and fast. The singing that once went slow and unaccompanied, one voice leading and the rest answering, comes out here distorted and double-time, and nobody down the front drops a syllable. Most of the pull is frontman Jalmar Vabarna, who has fronted the band since they were teenagers and, off the stage, happens to be the elected ülemsootska, earthly stand-in for the Seto king. Same job either way, really, carrying his own corner of the country in front of as many people as will have it. By Saturday the site was full, 11,000 through the gates and the biggest crowd of the four days, the paths between stages packed from early afternoon as people wove from one set to the next. It all spilled onto the Song Festival Grounds, where HrayBery had the whole arena linking hands. The Polish-Ukrainian band rebuild village dance music from old scores and field recordings of the San river valley, a border region of eastern Galicia once shared by Poles, Ukrainians, Jews and Roma before post-war deportations scattered its people. They looked the part, in the Sunday best of a century ago: straw boater hats over dark suits and waistcoats for the men, high-collared white blouses and pale skirts for the women. Two fiddles, hammered dulcimer and frame drum drove the kolomyjkas, mazurkas, polkas and kozaks, and the crowd read the cue: great circling chains across the concrete, ring inside ring, while the grass banks behind filled with people watching them turn. A couple of hours later, still on the Grounds, the picture shrank from a full folk band to two women over a single instrument. Duo Ruut are Ann-Lisett Rebane and Katariina Kivi, who sit facing each other across one kannel, close enough to touch, one plucking while the other bows or drums the body, their voices soaring into harmonies that can hold a field still. Here they broke that on purpose, billing the set as Duo Ruut³ and pulling in Indrek Mällo on bass, Jaan Jaago on electric guitar, and on percussion Tõnu Tubli, who drummed a decade in Trad.Attack! and had already remixed the duo’s tunes on his own record. Outdoors, the expanded setup carried and got people moving, but it cost something too: the fine, quiet tension of two players negotiating one instrument is what makes them extraordinary, and a rhythm section inevitably paints over it. Still, once a real beat was locked under the runo song, the Grounds went from hushed to dancing. Over on II Kirsimägi, the boundary between the stage and the dirt dissolved entirely. Orkesta Mendoza opened with ‘Cumbia Volcadora’, six of them in matching suits, though nothing stayed buttoned down for long. Sergio Mendoza ran the set from the keys with an accordion slung across his chest, and on his shout of “¡Derecha! ¡Izquierda!” the whole field threw its hands right, then left, in time with him. Quetzal Guerrero sawed at the violin like an acrobat, Ozzy Acosta’s percussion kept the cumbia turning underneath, and Victor Hugo drove the band from the kit. Mendoza grew up in Ambos Nogales, the town the US-Mexico border splits in two, and the Orkesta plays what that town might sound like with the line gone: mambo, cumbia and ranchera rammed into surf guitar, psychedelia and indie rock. The Grounds kept filling as night came on, until the weekend’s largest crowd, some 8,000—packed in for Puuluup. Ramo Teder and Marko Veisson play the talharpa, a bowed lyre all but extinct outside the island of Vormsi, except they drum, bow, pluck, and brush it, feeding horsehair through loopers until a knocking, creaking rhythm rises out of a single ancient instrument. For a few numbers they brought out company: Tubli was back behind a kit, slamming real drums into a stage the pair usually run on loops and horsehair alone. In tuxedos and flat deadpan, Veisson’s voice rumbling low beneath Teder’s higher line, they sang in Estonian and a language of their own invention, stopping dead between numbers to sell the crowd straight-faced nonsense about what they’d just played. It was Veisson’s 50th, and when the field found out, thousands sang him happy birthday. He answered the only way that suited the night: throwing himself off the front to crowd-surf the field. They tried out new dance routines on the spot, saving their wildest choreography for a set that felt looser and warmer than usual. By the end, Duo Ruut were up there too: Rebane and Kivi crowding the microphones alongside Teder, Veisson, and Tubli, all five packed around the stand to see it out. Puuluup had warmed the field. OOPUS came to pound it. Mari Meentalo fed bagpipe, jaw harp and regilaul into a looper and handed the loops to Johannes Ahun’s analogue Roland synths, thousand-year-old runic song coming back out of the machines as acid house, while Aleksander Sprohgis’ lights, pinned to the beat, cracked across II Kirsimägi every time the bassline turned over and Raho Aadla danced it out at the front of the stage. OOPUS bill themselves as folk on acid and mean it to the letter: the bagpipe drone sat under a squelching acid line as though it had been waiting a millennium for exactly that, with their latest Reivlender playing as one long build. By mid-set a crowd that had spent the day watching thumb pianos and kannels was going properly, sweatily off, the oldest material on the whole bill turned into the closest thing Viljandi had to a nightclub. After midnight the festival split its mood in two. Kaevumägi turned inward for Kuula Hetke, the flute duo of Kärt Pihlap and Katariina Tirmaste, whose name translates as “listen to the moment” and whose method lives up to it: they take melodies from the home regions of their great-grandparents, Mulgimaa and Võrumaa, thread their own writing through them, and pull the whole thing apart and back together on stage. Two flutes, voice and electronics built into slow, elemental soundscapes, and beside them the visual artist Okeiko painted a video world in real time, improvising brushstrokes to match every shift in the music. The Song Festival Grounds went the other way, loud and communal, as Tuulebant+ marked ten years with a birthday set. What began as a handful of young Estonian lads deciding to play together has become a fixture of the dance floors, acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and lõõts (the Estonian button accordion) under four voices, driving the kind of brisk, folk-rooted dance music that owes a clear debt to Untsakad and the Kukerpillid before them. For the anniversary they swelled the core band out with guests borrowed from other line-ups across the weekend, the plus in the name doing real work, and sent the last of the night’s crowd home dancing. Sunday came in warm and dry and ended wringing wet. The early afternoon on I Kirsimägi got a soft landing from Tell Your Birds, an Estonian, Latvian and Italian quartet who assemble their music from old tapes and Baltic tunes, running Estonian and Latvian folk melodies and field-recorded voices through electronics into long, drifting drones. Fiddle, bowed lyre and balafon carried the tunes up front while the fourth of them worked synths and effects beneath, turning a grey start into something to wake up slowly to.  By late afternoon, the sun had pulled the crowd onto Kaevumägi for Nancy Vieira, who brought Cape Verde to Viljandi, and morna to the festival for the first time in its history. Widely seen as the heir to Cesária Évora, Vieira carries that same slow, aching island sound. Born in Guinea-Bissau to Cape Verdean parents before moving to Lisbon at 14, she embodies the exact displacement morna is written about: the voice of the person who left. Backed only by guitar, cavaquinho, light percussion, and her own cool, unhurried lead, her set folded fado, Brazilian rhythms, and West African lines into songs from her 2024 album Gente. Then came the shift: for the final numbers, she invited the crowd right up onto the stage, turning the show into a full-tilt dance through the fast, bouncing tunes of Ano Nobo. The set the weekend had quietly been saving arrived that evening, and it went to Amy Laurenson. She had barely made the festival at all, held up by flight delays, cancellations, and baggage mishandling alongside guitarist Miguel Girão, reaching Viljandi just minutes before their Saturday slot on Kaevumägi in the rain and wind. Sunday finally did her justice, placing her at a grand piano inside the Ait. There, the Shetland pianist takes fiddle tunes written for a bow and hands them to the keys as a lead voice rather than accompaniment: reels arriving with their drive intact and their phrasing completely rethought. Out of the weather, the room went dead silent and stayed that way. It was the finest hour of the four days. Fittingly, the last word went to a band from the festival’s own backyard. Angus formed in 2010 out of Viljandi and its Culture Academy, and have spent the sixteen years since turning out a warm, unhurried reggae, ska and dub sung in Estonian, their 2023 record Vibratsioon hailed by Raadio 2 as the flagship of Estonian reggae-rock. Seven of them shut the festival down from the Song Festival Grounds, joined by guest vocalist Sofia-Liis Liiv, playing out into a downpour to a soaked crowd that skanked through the mud and bouncing along to thick dub basslines and hip-hop rhymes. Before the final fade, frontman Anton Ventsel signed the weekend off with a line worth keeping: “Have a good evening, a safe journey home, and folk is forever.” A local band, on the last stage, in the wet, closing a festival their own town has built its name on. Viljandi did not have its biggest year, but it had a better one than that. The man at the hotel desk had the right instinct and the wrong month. The next edition runs 22nd to 25th July 2027, worth writing down now, because he was not wrong about the room either.   The Viljandi Folk Music Festival returns in 2027, running 22nd to 25th July Ticket sales open in December, but keep an eye out HERE   [See image gallery at rhythmpassport.com] The post Event Review: Viljandi Folk Music Festival 2026 (Viljandi, Estonia; Thursday 23rd to Sunday 26th July 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Dau, the moniker of UK ambient musician Phil Self, is about to release his solo debut, Zed Zed. Arriving via Phantom Limb’s new sub-label imprint Spirituals, which promotes ‘high grade, emotive ambient and experimental music from emerging artists from across the world’, Zed Zed is a beautifully-crafted and intricately-woven record, utilising classical chamber orchestration and blending it with an ambient core. Self is involved in many other projects, from the UK instrumental sextet yndi halda to performing in the live band of folk-rock singer-songwriter Will Varley. Self also runs the Isolation Choir, a non-profit initiative for the elderly and the vulnerable, where musicians and non-musicians alike are invited to contribute remotely to pieced-together ensemble performances (the first video of which caught the eye of Brian Eno, who was so moved by the performance and the compassionate message behind the project that he offered his services for the second). Zed Zed features bowed guitar, reed organ, and voice, but Self also includes recordings of water bowls, falling rain, and sounds from his kitchen, which produces a warm, comfortable, and homely atmosphere, adding degrees of personality and intimacy within the familiar environment of home. The human qualities of empathy, kindness, and care are literally at the centre of the music, a point at which it can brightly shine, and it also reflects Self’s own personality, the music acting as a conduit for his inner kindness. The music unravels with patience, slowly developing and building upon itself. Perhaps most importantly, Zed Zed is free of computer processing; digital editing and computer interference is rejected. The record is entirely acoustic and proud of the fact, featuring real-time performances and nothing but acoustic instrumentation. A deep ambient heart beats within its music, which is all the more evident in the dulled harmonic resonance of its water bowl. And along with the sound of dripping water, reverberating gongs help to produce calming sensations and feelings of immense relief. With graceful movements, the music never seems to put a foot wrong. ‘Sundowning’ closes the album as an overlapping family of lean, slanting strings provide the last flares of light. Even with the sunset and its representation of ending and finality, the music’s message is one of enduring beauty, optimism, and appreciation, retaining its grace right up until its end. PSALM003: Zed Zed by Dau www.phantomlimblabel.bandcamp.com

items._cn_summary: 这是英国环境音乐人Phil Self以Dau名义发行的首张全长专辑，全部采用纯声学录制，拒绝任何数字处理与电脑编辑。乐器配置以弓拉吉他、簧风琴与人声为核心，并大量融入水碗、雨水、厨房声响等日常环境录音，营造出温暖、私密且具有家居感的声音氛围。古典室内乐编制与环境音乐内核交织，弦乐缓慢铺陈、钹声回荡，与水滴声共同构建出冥想般的空间感。专辑末尾的《Sundowning》以倾斜的弦乐群收束，传达出对美的持续感知与乐观情绪。制作上强调实时演奏与原声乐器的真实质感，音乐也映射出艺术家在慈善合唱项目中体现的同理心与关怀精神。整体手法克制而耐心，适合在安静环境中反复聆听。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦于俄乌冲突中被掳走的乌克兰儿童这一沉重主题，由乌克兰裔加拿大歌手Marichka发起，集合加拿大与乌克兰两组女性音乐人共同演绎。音乐以传统乌克兰民歌与原创作品交织，核心编制为弓弦乐器，搭配班杜拉琴、钢琴与双陶笛等乐器，人声时而温柔内敛、时而激烈尖锐。乐评指出其音乐与声乐品质达到较高水准，即便不借助主题背景也足以独立成立，而歌词翻译所呈现的内容更令听者动容。作为传统民谣与世界音乐的范畴，该作品虽不涉及明显的实验或电子元素，但其东欧文化根源、社会议题介入以及传统与现代编制的结合，为听众提供了独特的文化与情感体验。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以墨西哥牛仔（vaqueros）十九世纪前往夏威夷赶牛的历史为线索，将墨西哥与夏威夷的民谣传统编织在一起。十六首曲目包含西班牙语与夏威夷语互译的古老歌谣、新创作以及美国传统民谣，由尤克里里、墨西哥竖琴、手风琴与吉他形成统一的声响底色。Taj Mahal与David Hidalgo作为核心人物参与编排与演唱，Sonny Lim的滑棒吉他与lap steel为作品增添了即兴色彩。录音在加州圣巴勃罗的工作室五天内完成，大量同期录制保留了现场的自发感。学徒学生与传奇音乐人同台，体现了语言、文化、年龄与性别层面的多元协作。从洛杉矶到夏威夷的跨太平洋迁徙故事被音乐重新讲述，伍迪·格思里的《Deportee》在此被赋予新的社会意涵。整体呈现为一次有历史纵深与文化融合意识的世界音乐实践。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张EP由北欧民谣圈资深主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目以传统音乐为底，乐队成员各自带入不同视角进行重新诠释。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗犷的奔跑节奏展示主唱极富说服力的嗓音；唯一原创曲《Nordgård》借助口琴与风笛形成持续推进力；传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》以扬琴铺设精致背景；终曲《Ormsö》为纯器乐演奏，口琴与长笛、弦乐交织出奇特而令人兴奋的失衡感。整体氛围古老而略带吱嘎质感，呈现出一支已相当成熟且技艺精湛的乐队的亮相作。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / soundscape
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区的街头完成，二十五位遭受枪支暴力影响的居民参与录制，年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等。录制地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家的前廊，正值特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队之日。专辑没有添加任何音乐元素，全部由现场环境声与人声讲述构成，呈现出一种田野录音式的纪实声响美学。一位失去两个儿子的长者在讲述时情感崩溃，反复说着'对不起'，这种未经修饰的真实声音比任何编排都更具冲击力。项目收益将捐赠给致力于以公共卫生方式终结暴力的组织Cure Violence Global。专辑揭示了暴力在社区中的普遍程度，并让那些被遗忘的角落发出自己的声音。

items.body:
GUEST COLUMN
NO. 340
「どこかで〜中村八大という人」 第１回
2026年8月15日
さがゆき

photos: from Saga’s private collection

1931年1月20日、青島 (チンタオ) にて大音楽家誕生す。戦後の荒れ果てたとんでもなく貧しい日本に、元気の源になるような＜上を向いて歩こう＞＜明日があるさ！＞…等をはじめ、魂が震える名曲を次から次へと白黒TV番組『夢で逢いましょう』から産み出してくれた人。幼少期から東京音楽学校（現・東京藝術大学）の附属児童学園でピアノと作曲の英才教育を受け、上京したばかりの頃からすでにベテラン奏者を驚かせる腕前を持っており、その自信を裏付ける、余り知られていない意外な話が…実は色々ある。

これは一般的にはほとんど知られていない話。フリージャスの先駆者、SAX奏者のOrnette Coleman (オーネットコールマン) の演奏に八大さんは興味を持っており、ある日、彼の演奏に直接触れようと渡米。オーネットが出演しているジャズクラブへ出かけ、自分は日本のジャズピアニスト。何か一緒にやりましょう！と…今で言うシット・イン。八大さんが弾き始めたらめちゃくちゃカッコよくて、オーネットはビックリ！日本のハチダイ素晴らしい！と大喜び！熱いハグをして、ひと晩中一緒に演奏した…！オーネットをも唸らせちゃう八大さん…凄い！！！

そんな側面は、今の若い人達はまず知らないかも。
私は八大さん作曲の美しい曲を八大さんのピアノで歌っていた時、ジャズ・ナンバーを歌う時と同じような、何にも縛られない自由な気持ちで歌えていた事が嬉しく蘇る。
日本に溢れるほどの名曲を残してくれた…だけでは無い…トンガリまくった硬派なJAZZミュージシャン、でもある…んですよね。だから何年経っても色褪せる事のない「スタンダード・ナンバー」として未来永劫、多くの人に愛され続ける曲ばかりを作曲されたのではないかな…。八大さん、あの曲はきっとこんな風に演奏したかったのかな…って一緒に音楽やってた者だから分かる事が…ある。

学校出たての若かりし頃の八大さんの話をひとつ。 ある日バイト探しに都内のとあるキャバレーに出向き、自分の演奏聞いてもらえませんか、とバンマスに道場破り。「おー、ぼうず、ピアノ弾けんのか？なんかやってみろ」、とバンマス。「はい」…と、もの凄い演奏を披露した八大さん。
「おー、ぼうず、なかなかやるじゃねぇか！じゃ明日から来な！」すると八大さん、「お兄さん方、幾らもらってるんですか？」
バンマス「おぅ、２千円だぜ」
八大さん「じゃ僕、３千円貰います。お兄さん達と音楽違うんで」(金額はハッキリ分からないので当てずっぽうイメージ)
お兄さん…「お…おぅ…分かったぜ。よろしくな！！」
パチパチパチパチ…….素晴らしい！
世の中、こうあるべきって見本！
中村八大、こんな人です！最高！！！

スマホの写真をどんどん繰って行くように時代は遡り話は前後するけど…私が八大さんとご一緒するようになって、いつだったか、FMだかTVだか覚えていないが、何かの生収録でスタジオで演奏、という時の忘れられない思い出。
曲も何だったかなぁ…とにかくジャズのナンバー。行き方はまずボーカルがワンコーラス、テーマを歌い〜アドリブは……など、おおよその構成は予め決まっていたのだが、何だかその時もの凄くいい演奏になり、皆んな乗っちゃって！私はサビから歌詞でエンディング行く感じじゃなく、ワンコーラス、アドリブ取って…結局サイズがオーバーして番組に最後まで入らなかった…。
終わったら当時のマネージャー渋谷さんが、「さがさん酷いじゃないですか〜！お尻切れちゃったじゃないですか。なんで決まった通りにやってくれなかったんですか〜！」そしたら八大さん、珍しく大きな声で、「バカやろう！何年俺の音楽聴いて来たんだ！あの時音楽が最高に膨らんだだろう？それが一番大切な事だ！ケツなんか切れたって構わない。切ればいいんだ！いい音楽は何にも縛られちゃ駄目なんだ！イキイキ自由にやらなきゃジャズじゃないんだ！！」って！カッコいい〜っ！全く仰せの通りです！！大尊敬〜っ！！ 八大さんは＜上を向いて歩こう＞、とか＜遠くへ行きたい＞だけの人じゃない。オーネットを唸らせたジャズマンなんだからね！

中村八大さんとの最初のご縁を紐解くと、私がまだ中学２年生になったばかりのある夏の日に遡る。その頃、鎌倉由比ヶ浜の自宅からよく出かけて いた「江ノ島ヨットハーバー」などのパーティーや「赤坂プリンスホテル」のラウンジ、「Venus」というレストラン…などで、独学で身に付けたジャズボーカルを大人のプロやアマチュアのミュージシャンたちのバンドで歌っていた。あの頃の自分はまったく化粧もせず  (子供ですものね)  恐れをまだ知らない生意気で硬派な女の子だった。歌だけは誰にも負ける気はしていなかったけど…。 鎌倉の海が一望できる「Tic-Tac」というレストランで大学生のバンドの人達と定期的にライブをしていた。ギター、ベース、ドラム、サックス、それにボーカルは私、という編成だった。レパートリーはジャズとボサノバ。いつもラストには大好きな曲＜目をとじて＞が自分たちのバンドのテーマソングだった。
※後に八大さんとご一緒するようになって、＜目を閉じて＞って知ってる？と言われた時に、「あ、この曲、私のバンドのテーマソングなんです」、と私。八大さん…「これ、僕の曲なんだよ」…って笑ってらした。恥ずかしかったな〜！

「Tic-Tac」に場面は戻る。
子供がジャズを歌ってると評判を聞き、色々な人が聴きに来てくれていた中にある日、中村八大さんがスカウトにいらした…らしい。(知らなかった) 八大さんは直接私にではなく、バンマスだったドラムの”T氏”に、歌の子を紹介して欲しいとおっしゃったのだと…(知らなかった！)
メンバーたちは、自分のバンドの目玉である看板娘のボーカリストを取られたら困るからと、私を楽屋に隠して、なんと八大さんと私を会わせないようにしてしまったのだと (知らなかった…)
だいぶ時が経ってからドラムの”T氏”から、実は…と、恐る恐るその時の話の顛末を初めて聞かされ本当に驚いた。こともあろうに天下の中村八 大さんとのご縁を揉み消してしまうなんて…しみじみ申し訳ない話。
もしあの時、ちゃんと八大さんと会えていたらどんな人生になっていたのかな……。 その後当時のメンバーもバラバラになり消息も途絶え、その話は風とともに どこかへ消えてしまっていた…。
でも、神様はご縁のある方とは、たとえどんなことがあっても、忘れずにご縁をつないで下さるのだ。のちに私はそれを身をもって体験することになる。
items._genre: jazz / vocal jazz / Japanese popular song
items._cn_summary: 本文为歌手さがゆき撰写的纪念专栏，回顾日本作曲家兼钢琴家中村八大的音乐人生。文章并非传统唱片乐评，而是通过轶事回忆呈现八大的艺术形象：早年赴美与自由爵士先驱Ornette Coleman即兴合奏，年轻时在キャバレー以道场破式自荐并要求高于资深乐手的报酬，以及在电视直播中坚持音乐完整性而不顾节目时长限制等故事。作者结合自己中学时期在餐厅演唱八大曲目，以及后来与其合作的亲身经历，论述八大不仅是《上を向いて歩こう》等国民名曲的作者，更是一位深具自由精神的硬派爵士钢琴家。文章带有浓郁的个人追忆色彩，对理解日本战后音乐史中的爵士脉络有一定参考价值。

items.body:
CONCERTS/LIVE SHOWS
NO. 340
#1424 コルトレーン・ナイト
2026年8月15日
細川周平

text by Shuhei Hosokawa  細川周平

2026年7月14日　＠京都 Rag

出演：
高橋知己 (ts)
竹内直 (ts, bcl)
喜屋武弥 (p)
畠山令 (b)
石田博嗣 (ds)

コルトレーンナイトはドラムスの石田博嗣が1992年より始めているトリビュート・コンボで、高橋知己、竹内直の２テナーをレギュラーとし、ピアノとベースは数年ごとに入れ替えてきた。7、80年代にエルヴィン・ジョーンズとジョン・コルトレーンに感化を受けたドラムスとテナーのベテラン３人と、その後のスタイルに拠る若いピアノとベース２人の対面クインテットで、かつて大学のモダンジャズ研でさえ聴かれたあの四角四面のインパルスもどきの再現ではなく、きっちりいまどきの展開を果たしている。今年は喜屋武弥（ピアノ）と畠山令（ベース）が呼び出された。コルトレーン（1926～1967）の生誕百周年と60回忌が重なり、京都の本拠地RagではミスターＪ．Ｃ．の命日（７月17日）にちなんで日程が組まれ、特別気合が入っていたように思う。聴く側も気合が入り、曲目をメモしてみた。ほとんどは既知の曲と分かっていて、リーダーの志向を教えてくれるのはもちろんだし、昔のジャズ記憶、コルトレーン熱を思い出す楽しみにも通じると考えたからだ。元の曲を思い出すのはトリビュート・バンドならではの楽しみで、それなしには存在理由も見当たらない。昔の再現、焼き直しにつとめるだけではない。

一曲目は「ミスター・Ｐ.Ｃ.」、ポール・チェンバースに捧げられたブルース・フォーマットの曲で、コルトレーン流ハードバップのウォーミングアップとして、このコンボのオープニングによく選ばれる。よし、このノリで行きましょうとメンバー、客をひとつにまとめる。初演収録のアトランチック盤『ジャイアント・ステップス』は革新的なタイトル曲ばかりでなく、それ以外の新曲にも創意がみなぎって聴き通して飽きさせない。多くのヴァージョンが録音されていて、ウェイン・ショーターとエルヴィン・ジョーンズの合流したライブや、ジョン・スコフィールドとジャック・デジョネットの共演というのも今回初めて知った。インパルス時代のカルテットに記憶が突出しがちだが、コルトレーンはそれまでにマイルスのプレスティジ・クインテットを離れ、革新的なハードバッパーとして、シーンのリーダーシップを執っていた。

続いて同じアルバムに初録音され、コルトレーンのオリジナルのなかでもっとも有名なうちの一曲「ナイーマ」に、竹内直はバス・クラリネットを持ち込んだ。この一曲のために毎年横浜から楽器を担いでくると、石田のトークが笑わせる。ぼくがコルトレーンの衝撃を受けた70年代半ばには、コルトレーン＆ドルフィーのクインテットの60年代前半ヨーロッパツアー録音が大きな発見で、ファンはジャズ喫茶の爆音オーディオで、今日はベルリン明日はオスロと録音でツアーのお伴をして舞い上がったものだが、竹内直はきっちりドルフィーの楽器を選んで、レーベルのオフィシャル盤の外へコルトレーンナイトを導いてくれる。このお伴がいると高橋知己のテナーはますますコルトレーン寄りに聞こえる。続くはタッド・ダメロンがコルトレーンをゲストに招いたプレスティジ盤『鳥のさえずり』から「ニッド」。この軽いスウィングは今では気持ちよいが、重厚好みの当時は無視していた。ゲストのピアノ、ベースがやっと場を得て本領発揮と聴こえた。

コルトレーンは「マイ・フェイヴァリット・シングス」でソプラノ・サックスを発見して、表現域を拡げ、信者を増やしフリーにも向かうのだが、石田のバンドはテナーに限定し、50年代の、モード奏法以前の曲を中心に選曲し、エルヴィン流で叩き直して敬意を示し、作曲家としてのＪ．Ｃ．の卓越ぶりに意識を向ける。第一部の最後はソプラノの定番「アフロブルー」で、２テナーに置き換えたうえ、ドラムス・ソロがぐっと出て石田の見せ場をつくる。曲の流れにからだを任せて出番をまっとうする。

第二部の始まりは「モーメント・ノーティス」と「クレッセント」が選ばれた。曲名を言われるとアルバム・ジャケットが浮かび上がってくる妙な回路は、ＬＰをありがたがっていた青春の名残で、コルトレーンナイトはふらふらっとノスタルジックだ。本当に望まれる観客ではないかもしれない。

終盤にかけてテナーを独りずつ立てるカルテット編成コーナーがあり、竹内はブルーノート盤『ソウル・トレイン』より「アーニーのテーマ」、高橋はインパルス時代の『エリントン＆コルトレーン』より「インナ・センチメンタル・ムード」を選んできた。有名な『バラード』のほかにも、コルトレーンは歌ものが素晴らしく、テーマだけで曲を完璧に仕上げてしまう。小細工がない。爆走ばかりがコルトレーンではない。二人は敬意を込めて吹く。バラード特集のコルトレーンナイトがあってもよい（ドラムスの見せ場はなくなってしまうのだが）。

プログラムの最後は恒例の「至上の愛　第二部決意」で、元のアルバムは深いメッセージとともに大学生に愛聴され、両面30分を一気に聴きとおすのが暗黙の了解で、この部分はA面後半の山場だった。４部構成コンセプトアルバムの一部だけを選んで演奏するのは、当時はありえない選択だったと思う。二人のテナー奏者はインパルス時代の曲もそれ以前も、原曲のコード枠を超えフリーに向かうのを常とするが、晩年のコルトレーンとそれ以降を連想するというより、サックスを吹き始めたころの無垢を蘇らせているようだ。アンコールは「ブルートレイン」で旋律がとっつきやすいため、日本のアマチュア連もよく演奏していた。そのうえで最後の最後の時間を使って、『マイ・フェイヴァリット・シングス』から「エヴリタイム・ウィー・セイ・グッバイ」のテーマだけを演奏して客を追い出した。

今年は生誕百周年にちなんだトリビュート企画が日米欧各地で催されているだろうが、コルトレーンナイトはそれとは別種、筋金入りの崇拝が込められている。1966年の来日と翌年の逝去、それから神格化が始まり、レコードを拠り所に演奏者と評論家と熱烈な聴き手がジャズ喫茶のヒーローに祀り上げ、世界でも独特のコルトレーン共同体を作り上げたと思う。エルヴィン・ジョーンズが長期滞日して、石田博嗣のような純真なドラマーを生み出したことは驚くべきことで、コルトレーンナイトとは一種のエルヴィンナイトでもある。未発表テイクや映像がいくら公開されてもこの感慨には程遠く、ライブ演奏でのみ達しうる敬意の境地である。気持ちがぐっときて、かつてのヒーローの記念Tシャツを買って５人にサインしてもらった。着ると頭のなかはニューポート？バードランド？じゃない、キョート！

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是已故巴西艺术家塞萨尔·亚历山大的遗作重新发行，亚历山大因新冠并发症去世约五年后由Cryo Chamber厂牌推出此先前鲜为人知的录音。乐评指出，亚历山大主要以暗潮氛围音乐闻名，但其作品实际范畴更为宽泛。《The Yasu Ether Project》作为遗作再版，聚焦于氛围与延绵音色的构建，延续了他一贯的深沉音景探索。整张专辑的动机源自对已故创作者的艺术梳理，意在让更多听众重新接触这位因疫情离世的音乐人未曾广为人知的声音实验。由于原文内容极为简短，仅透露艺术家背景与作品再版事实，缺乏对具体声音手法、创作细节或音乐结构的深入描述，因此无法对其艺术成就做更详尽的评估。

items.body:
One of the most distinctive and legendary vocal/dub albums of all time, recorded in 1981 by the “dub dentist” Keith Hudson, ‘Playing It Cool & Playing It Right’ is now back in circulation for the first time in over 20 years, when it was first given overdue flowers via Basic Channel And Honest Jon’s ‘Basic Replay’ programme. It still burns with a rare energy, making it an untouchable, foundational text for the ages.

Keith Hudson (1946-1984) was one of dub reggae’s most distinctive innovators, renowned for a run of classic solo albums and productions for U-Roy, Big Youth, Ken Boothe and Horace Andy between 1972 and his untimely passing in 1984. However, Hudson's late period is where the real imperial juice can be found, a time that saw him move from Jamaican to London and New York studios, applying his unfathomable production style to a heavily americanised strain of vocal Soul. ‘Playing It Cool & Playing It Right’ is the pinnacle of that late period, an album that builds layer upon layer of alchemical brilliance.

Hudson’s combination of hooks and complex, highly unusual production is really unlike anything else from the period, or since, crooning in a soul mode made more haunting by a discreetly judicious application of tape FX, endlessly heavy subs, and mixing desk tricks deployed to delirious, almost psycho-acoustic effect.  The album was originally meant to feature one of Hudson's teenage sons to voice the dubs, but in the event the Love Joys, Wayne Jarrett, and inimitably Hudson himself featured at the microphone, with the dozen cuts co-produced by Wackies founder Lloyd ‘Bullwackie’ Barnes - the only collaboration between the two producers. It was originally issued on Hudson’s own label, Joint International, with subsequent pressings on Basic Replay in 2003, making it increasingly sought-after in the years since. 

Alongside reggae’s first concept album, ‘Flesh of My Skin, Blood of My Blood’, ‘Playing It Cool’ remains one the genre’s most important and unusual releases, picking up new disciples with every new wave of listeners taken aback by its stark, brooding blooze and brittle, spectral rendering.
items._genre: dub reggae / vocal dub / soul dub
items._cn_summary: 这张1981年录制的专辑是dub音乐史上极为独特的人声与dub混音作品，融合了雷鬼节奏与美式灵魂乐元素。制作人Keith Hudson在牙买加、伦敦及纽约录音室间穿梭，将深沉的低频、磁带特效与调音台技巧层层叠加于灵魂乐风格的人声之上，营造出近乎迷幻声学效应的听感。专辑人声由Love Joys、Wayne Jarrett及Hudson本人演绎，原本计划由其子献声但最终未能实现。整张作品由Hudson与Wackies厂牌创始人Lloyd Barnes联合制作，是两人唯一的合作成果。文本以不断叠加的方式构建声响层次，呈现出幽暗、冥想般的灵魂dub美学，是其晚期创作的巅峰之作，与另一张开创性专辑《Flesh of My Skin》并列为该类型最重要的录音之一。

items.body:
Proper, tracky, Chi-style budgers from the badboy Delroy Edwards, back to his vintage tricks on spiritual home L.A. Club Resource

The jakbeat is strong on this one, laid down direct and cruddy in the best sense with drum machines and  synths toiled into driving grooves that sound like they could have emerged during the mid ‘80s early years of house. Covering the spectrum of jakbeat flavours, he crosses from the title tune’s sultry swerve to hypnotic bass goop in ‘Put That’, cruising from the rude Adonis like keys of ‘Bring The House’ to a smart glimmer of FM synthesis smeared into ‘How’d You Do That’, and some Faces drums-style machine tickets on ‘Don’t Ya Know’, saving the punchiest tackle for the percolated funk and honk of ’Sweet Geese’, and dope nods to Gene Hunt on ‘House Blitz.’
items._genre: house / jakbeat / deep house / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将芝加哥浩室传统的鼓机律动与洛杉矶地下俱乐部美学相融合，呈现出粗粝而生猛的低保真质感。Delroy Edwards 运用经典的模拟鼓机与合成器，营造出仿佛来自八十年代浩室黄金年代的驾驶感groove。曲目风格多变，从标题曲的暧昧律动到催眠低音、从类Adonis风格的明亮键盘到FM合成器的朦胧光泽、再到致敬Gene Hunt的硬朗浩室作品，跨度涵盖了jakbeat的多种风味。整体制作强调原始质感与俱乐部实用主义，没有过多修饰，每首曲目都直击舞池功能，是一张服务于DJ和舞池的纯粹俱乐部作品。

items.body:
All killer, no filler trotters from a golden period of Lee ‘Scratch’ Perry’s foundational work at fabled studio, The Black Ark.

This 3rd in a prized series spies the wee madman conjuring multidimensional spectres from vocal recordings of regular spars: Max Romeo, The Jolly Brothers, Leroy Sibbles, The Mistic, and Devon Irons. Perry’s visionary, innovative application of studio-as-instrument tekkerz come to the fore in the music’s layered diffusions, which we may take for granted in contemporary music, but was radical back then, and whose uncanny appeal has only steeped with age. 

Including a solo standout in the ghostly, harmonised roots wooze of his ‘Dread Lion’ gem as King Scratch, it spans the signature, lysergic sparkle of his ‘Conscious Man’cut with The Jolly Brothers, thru a stepping 12” mix of Max Romeo’s ‘Norman’ (1978), and heat-hazed sway to Leroy Sibbles’ ‘Garden of Life’, along with The Mistic’s eyes-down devotional ‘Forward With Jah’, and sloshing nyabingi of ‘When Jah Comes’ for Devon Irons.
items._genre: dub / reggae / roots / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了Lee 'Scratch' Perry在传奇的Black Ark录音棚（1977-1979年）制作的五首经典discomix作品。Perry以录音棚为乐器，通过层叠混音、回声处理和多维度声效叠加，将Max Romeo、The Jolly Brothers、Leroy Sibbles、The Mistic、Devon Irons等合作者的人声录音解构重组。这些制作手法在当时极为前卫，对后世电子音乐制作影响深远，至今仍散发着独特魅力。专辑涵盖了根植雷鬼的迷幻律动、nyabingi鼓乐风格以及以King Scratch名义呈现的独立作品，展现了Perry将人声素材转化为超维度声景的实验精神。

items.body: Portion Control released a video for “Displaced Hybrid Refugee” on August 14, 2026, the same day their first archival box set, “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…”, arrived on Artoffact Records as a 4xCD set, a digital edition and a limited red vinyl LP. The London electronic and industrial group posted the video to their own Portion Control VMAG channel. Portion Control rebuild ‘Refugee’ as ‘Displaced Hybrid Refugee’ “Displaced Hybrid Refugee” sits at track 56 of the 77-track set and reworks “Refugee”, originally on the 1984 album “..Step Forward”. The band explain where the footage came from rather than what the song means: “This song is a rework of ‘Refugee’ and the video is built from the visuals used whenever we play it live.” It is the second rebuild of that song to surface from the project. Rhys Fulber of Front Line Assembly produced “Refugee (Rhys Fulber Rebuild)”, the first preview issued when the box set was announced. What the ‘Hit The Pulse to Purge’ box set collects The set gathers the 1983 mini-LP “Hit The Pulse”, the albums “..Step Forward” (1984) and “Psycho Bod Saves The World” (1986), the 12-inch singles “The Great Divide”, “Go-Talk” and “Raise The Pulse”, and the “Purge” EP (1986), plus B-sides, compilation tracks, rarities, remixes, demos and two concert recordings from 1984 and 1985. Paul Lavigne remastered all 77 tracks at Kontrast Mastering. Sixteen are previously unreleased and a further twelve appear on CD and digitally for the first time. The 4xCD edition comes in a five-panel ecopak with a 24-page booklet of archive photos, designed by Stefan Alt of ant-zen. The red vinyl LP carries ten tracks. 1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge… by portion control Side-Line covered the set when Artoffact announced the box set “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…” in June. Two further previews followed over the summer: the live recording “Tex-Mex”, taped at Dolce Vita in Lausanne in December 1985, and the demo “H.O.T. Matter” from the “Psycho Bod Saves The World” period. All three earlier tracks are on the box set alongside “Displaced Hybrid Refugee”. The 4xCD box, the LP, the digital edition and a run of six vinyl test pressings are sold through Bandcamp. The set is also on Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music, with physical copies handled in the UK by Lexer Music. Portion Control live dates October 24, 2026 – Zwickau, Germany – Elektrisch Festival July 1-4, 2027 – Canterbury, United Kingdom – Shadowlands About Portion Control Portion Control formed in South London in 1979 around Dean Piavani, Ian Sharp and John Whybrew. The group built a minimal, rhythm-led sound from sequenced synthesisers, drum machines, early samplers and clipped vocals, and issued a run of cassettes before their first vinyl album, “I Staggered Mentally”, in 1982. The mini-LP “Hit The Pulse” followed in 1983 and “..Step Forward” in 1984, the year they toured with Depeche Mode. “Psycho Bod Saves The World” closed the period in 1986. Their records from these years are cited as an influence on Nitzer Ebb, Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly, Nine Inch Nails and Orbital. The band stopped in the late 1980s and returned in 2004 with “Wellcome”, followed by “Filthy White Guy” (2006) and “Pure Form” (2012). Side-Line spoke to them in 2020 in an interview with Portion Control, and covered the 2022 reissue of the “Dissolve” material after the original run was pressed on self-destroying discs. Three “SEED” EPs appeared between 2020 and 2025, the last of them, “SEED EP3.1”, marking the point where Portion Control joined Artoffact in late 2025. “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…” is the first box set in the reissue programme that deal set up, and “Displaced Hybrid Refugee” is the track the band chose to mark its release.

items._cn_summary: Portion Control 是一支来自南伦敦的电子工业团体，1979年成立，以序列合成器、鼓机和早期采样器构建极简律动驱动的声响。该档案盒装收录了乐队1983至1986年间的重要作品，包括迷你LP《Hit The Pulse》、专辑《..Step Forward》和《Psycho Bod Saves The World》，以及多张单曲和EP的B面、合辑曲目、稀有版本、混音、 demo 和两场1984至1985年的现场录音，共77首曲目，其中16首为首次发行，12首首次以CD和数字形式呈现。Rhys Fulber（Front Line Assembly成员）参与了部分曲目的重建制作。盒装由Artoffact Records发行，Paul Lavigne负责母带处理，Stefan Alt设计装帧，整体定位为早期英国工业与电子场景的文献性回顾，强调历史资料的完整性和场景脉络的保存，而非新作品的创作表达。

items.body: Pittsburgh industrial project ShadowMouth and Cleveland vocal trio The Elder Goths released the double single “The Promise of Alchemy/The Death of Chemistry” on 12 August 2026 through Death of the Party Records. The two tracks are the final preview of ShadowMouth’s debut album “Modern Alchemy”, due in autumn 2026. How ShadowMouth and The Elder Goths built the two tracks Rick Polo and Brooks Farris wrote and performed the music. The Elder Goths, made up of Cassandra Bishop, Lauren O’Janpa and Gina Schultz, sing on both sides. Bishop wrote the lyrics for “The Promise of Alchemy”, which runs 2:29, and Schultz wrote the lyrics for “The Death of Chemistry”, which runs 2:24. Farris produced, engineered and mastered the pair at Electric Fox Studios. Polo had not met the three singers before he asked them to record, and he describes the approach as a gamble that changed the shape of the release. “These songs were the result of me taking a shot in the dark and reaching out The Elder Goths group, who I had never met before, and asked if they would provide some of the striking beautifully haunting harmonies that are immediately apparent when first hearing their work,” Polo stated. “But it turned out to be so much more than I could have imagined. The end result was an intense and and really heartfelt delivery which absolutely blew me away. This collaboration felt too important not to highlight. So we decided to release this a single ahead of the record.” The double single is available on Bandcamp. The Promise of Alchemy/The Death of Chemistry by ShadowMouth & The Elder Goths About ShadowMouth ShadowMouth formed in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania in 2023 as the project of songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Rick Polo, who also plays in Baroque Monody and Heck Vektor. Producer and drummer Brooks Farris of Electric Fox Studios completes the working pair. The project opened with the double single “Poison Nostalgia/Twenty Four Hours” on 4 October 2024, with Dombroski guesting on “Poison Nostalgia”. The debut EP “Purification By Fire” followed on 22 November 2024. Four singles came next: “False (Prophets) Profits” on 20 January 2025, “Your Words, Not Mine” on 21 May 2025, “We Are Sentient” on 1 August 2025 and “DOOM SCROLLERS vs HOLY ROLLERS” on 29 October 2025. The Elder Goths formed in 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio, after Cassandra Bishop, Lauren O’Janpa and Gina Schultz met through the city’s underground scene. “The Promise of Alchemy/The Death of Chemistry” is their first recorded appearance with ShadowMouth. With the twin tracks out, ShadowMouth close a run of seven releases in under two years and move to “Modern Alchemy”, the project’s first album.
items._genre: industrial / darkwave / goth
items._cn_summary: 匹兹堡工业项目 ShadowMouth 与克利夫兰暗潮人声三重唱 The Elder Goths 合作发布双面单曲，作为首张专辑《Modern Alchemy》的预热。词曲作者与制作人 Rick Polo 和 Brooks Farris 负责器乐部分，三位歌手 Cassandra Bishop、Lauren O'Janpa 和 Gina Schultz 分别创作了两首歌的歌词。Polo 表示他之前从未见过这三位歌手，通过盲选邀约促成了合作，结果获得了超出预期的情感表达，因此决定将这首合作单独提前发行。整张专辑建立在工业与暗潮的交叉地带，人声合奏成为作品的核心音色来源。从描述来看，作品偏向合作概念的展示，声音设计上的实验性提及有限，更多是类型框架内的常规工业暗潮融合，而非突破性的声音探索。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body:
R.I.P. 渋谷毅
MONTHLY EDITORIAL
FROM THE EDITOR’S DESK　稲岡邦彌
ある音楽プロデューサーの軌跡　稲岡邦弥
NO. 340
From the Editor’s Desk #28 渋谷毅との仕事
2026年8月15日
稲岡邦彌

text: Kenny Inaoka 稲岡邦彌

ギターの中牟礼貞則さんに続いてピアノの渋谷毅さんが逝ってしまった。渋谷さんは1939年生まれだから中牟礼さん (1933~2026) の５つ年少。ふたりは毎晩のように首都圏を中心にライヴ・シーンに顔を出していたから、続けざまにふたりを失った今、クラブやファンは当分ロス感に苛まれるだろう。
中牟礼さんとは三吉”３吉”功郎さんとの子弟コンビでライヴ・アルバムを制作する唯一のチャンスをいただいたが、渋谷さんとは何度か制作の現場を共有させていただいた、
渋谷さんとの初めての仕事は彼のデビュー作となったトリオ・アルバム『Dream』(1975)。鹿児島でジャズクラブ「パノニカ」を経営していた中山信一郎さんから持ち込まれたカセット音源だった。当時のトリオレコードではこれも中山さん提供の菅野邦彦のカルテット・アルバム『Live!』(1973) をきっかけにミュージシャンたちの自主録音専用のレーベルNadjaを立ち上げていたのでスムースにリリースすることができた。幸いデビュー・アルバムが好評を得たので２年後にアルバムを制作することにした。渋谷さんはライヴでないと本領を発揮できないよとの忠告もあったが、飲み仲間でもある中山さんを鹿児島から呼び監修をお願いすることで乗り切った。料理好きだった渋谷さんがアルバムを『Cook-Note』(1977) と命名し、表紙の隅に可愛いゴキブリを配するユニークなアートワークとなった。渋谷さんのオリジナルに加え、終生のテーマとなるエリントンの<I Don’t Know About You>とヘンリー・マンシーニの <Soldier in the Rain>はこのアルバムが初出である。

渋谷さんに新人ヴォーカルのデビュー・アルバムのミュージカル・ディレクターをお願いしたことが２件ある。1977年の酒井俊と1981年の沖山秀子である。酒井俊は同僚の原田和男が担当。他社と競合だったとのことでフロントに３管を配したアレンジで渋谷さんに万全を期してもらっている。『Shun』は内藤忠行が表紙写真を担当。酒井とは専属のような形で２作目はLAで現地のソウル系バンドを起用、３作目は坂本龍一がプロデュースを担当した。沖山秀子は映画界で話題を振りまいていた女優でフォト・ジャーナリストの杉田誠一の持ち込み。某メジャーにドタキャンされたとかで泣きつかれた。今度は渋谷さんに泣きついてミュージカル・ディレクターをお願いした。渋谷さんは音出し寸前にスタジオにスコアを持って駆け込んできたが、いずれも気心の知れたミュージシャンたちばかりなので、そつなくこなしてくれた。沖山は初めての経験だったが度胸と勘の良さでなんとか乗り切ってくれた。沖山が遺した唯一のアルバム『Summertime』の表紙写真は沖山の故郷・沖永良部島へロケを敢行した杉田誠一が撮影、自身代表作と自負。渋谷さんは映画関係者で埋め尽くされた六本木ピットインでのアルバム発売記念ライヴからその後のクラブ出演までしばらく沖山に付き合ってくれた。沖山はその後、録音に参加してくれた渋谷さんと中牟礼さんを従えて下北沢の名店Lady Janeに何度か出演したと大木雄高オーナーのブログにある。1977年には酒井俊に続いてもう１作渋谷さんにミュージカル・ディレクターをお願いしている。植松孝夫の代表作として名を遺している『Straight Ahead』だ。渋谷さんは植松を高く評価、同僚の原田和男が担当した。アートワークは内藤忠行が腕を振るっている。
しばらくぶりに渋谷さんと顔を合わせたのは、2022年10月9日、伊香保の World Jazz Museum 21だった。パリから帰国中のサックス奏者仲野麻紀との共演。永年の仲野の渋谷さんへの思い入れが奏功したか、想定以上の出来にすぐさま渋谷さんにCD化を申し入れ、幸いにも同意を得ることができ、『アマドコロ摘んだ春』が誕生した。
最後に出会ったのは、TVを通じてだった。6月16日、あきらめていたNHK8Kプレミアム・コンサートが放映直前に自宅のKITVでも受信できることを知った。渋谷さんが奏でるスタインウェイのコンサート・グランドはどこかよそいきの響きがしていた。シンガーソングライター沼尾翔子との共演が終わると、渋谷さんはひとりで心ゆくまでピアノに向き合っていた。50年前に録音したマンシーニの <Soldier in the Rain>や板橋文夫の <Good-bye>が流れてきた。
渋谷さんの訃報に接したのはそれからまもなくのことだった。（文中敬称略）

渋谷毅はいつも音楽とじかに向き合っている。そして音のひと粒ひと粒が輝いている。だから渋谷毅のピアノはどのような場所でもその場の空気によく馴染む。たとえ10人で満席の小さなクラブでも大きなコンサート・ホールでも、少々ガタのきたアップライト・ピアノでも渋谷毅の独特の音色が響き、その場の空気にすっと馴染んでしまう。そこに作為などは全く感じられず、しごく日常的なところが渋谷毅の凄いところである。

2007年の春、『フェイマス・メロディーズ』(VACM-1335 2007年)と『フェイマス・コンポーザーズ』(VACM-1336  2007年)レコーディングの構想を練っているときに渋谷さんと何度か打ち合わせをさせていただいた。私の頭に描くイメージを言葉で伝えるのは難しいので、渋谷さんが弾いたら原曲のもつメロディーや綾をこえて渋谷さんの世界が広がると想われる曲を60曲ほど選び出し、曲目リストと代表的、と云うよりも私が好む演奏をMDに落として聴いて頂いた。
レコーディング当日の2007年6月4日、渋谷さんは沢山の譜面をかかえて半蔵門の「TFMホール」に現れた。譜面のなかには私の曲目リストからの曲もあったが渋谷さんが選んだ曲も沢山あった。
＜ダニー・ボーイ＞、＜ポルカドット・アンド・ムーンビームス＞、第30回日本アカデミー賞、最優秀音楽賞を受賞した映画「嫌われ松子の一生」から＜キャンデイ・ツリー＞など二人で選んだ曲が次々と演奏されJTのオーディオ・マイスター、及川公生さんが渋谷さんの音とホールの気配を媒体に刻んでゆく。小休止のあとだったか、渋谷さんは＜金髪のジェニー＞と＜デイ・ドリーム＞そして＜スノー・フォール＞をメドレーで弾き始めた。フォスターとエリントン／ストレイホーンそしてクロード・ソーンフィルという一見なんの関連もなさそうな3曲をごく自然に結びつけ、あたかも自作曲のように5分51秒にまとめた。そこには、きっかけはそれぞれの曲であっても、つきつめて聴いてゆくとひらめきに満ち、品格のあるロマンティックな詩の世界が浮かび上がってくる。どんなに耳馴染んだ名曲でも渋谷毅というフィルターを通過すると今までとは違った清新な響きがよみがえるのである。

渋谷毅は1939年の生まれ。この秋で72歳になるがピアノから生み出す音はいつもフレッシュで若々しい。東京芸大付属高校～東京芸大作曲科というエリート・コースを歩みながら学生時代からジャズの現場に好んで現れた。あまり知られてはいないがジョージ川口＆ビッグフォー、シャープス・アンド・フラッツ、ウエスト・ライナーズなど歴代の名グループでも演奏してきている。高校時代、菊地雅章(p)と同期だったこともこの道に入るきっかけのひとつだったのかも知れない。今、二人は方向こそ違え、それぞれがなにものにも変えがたい独特の美の世界を築き上げ、絶えず聴くものを魅了し続けている。

たとえば、人は誰でもストレスで息詰まるような感覚に向かうことが一度や二度は経験するだろう。そんな時渋谷さんの＜ソリチュード＞を聴く。ワンコーラスも聴かないうちに胸が一杯になって涙がこぼれ落ちる。そして涙のあとに安らぎをとりもどす。甘さはないけれど背筋を正した渋谷毅のピアノが落ち着きと寛ぎを与えてくれるのである。

渋谷さんは一見、クールな面持ちを見せるが本当は一途な面とちょっと短気な面と粘り強さをもっていて、なによりも驚かされるのは、こと音楽と向き合っているときのタフさである。
『エッセンシャル・エリントン』(1999) や『フェイマス・メロディーズ』のレコーディング時のことでもあるが、渋谷さんはテイクをたくさん録る人である。何度かテイクを重ねて自ら＜ま、いいか＞とOKを出すが、＜もう一回、念のためにね＞と更にテイクを重ねる。曲によっては8テイク～10テイクに及ぶこともある。そして収録後の選曲の段階でラスト・テイクではなく最初にOKサインを出したテイクに戻ることもままあるのである。＜僕はあきらめが悪いから(笑)＞と渋谷さんはおっしゃるが、ベストなものを創ろうと目標を定めて収録に臨んだときには、もっといい演奏ができるんじゃないかという想いで、際限なく集中して自分に対して貪欲になるタイプなのである。

渋谷毅はデューク・エリントンやセロニアス・モンクと肩をならべるジャズの王道を歩んでいる。ソロからトリオ、エッセンシャル・エリントン、渋谷毅オーケストラ、さらに渋谷毅オーケストラのメンバーとのデュオ活動などで鍵盤に向かっている姿は姿勢を正した哲学者かのように映る。しかし鍵盤から出る音は艶やかで余韻があり、一音で渋谷毅とわかる輝きと深みがある。そしてその音に惹きつけられるように共演するミュージシャンの誰もが自然と渋谷毅の思い描く色彩を音で描きはじめてしまう。まさに渋谷マジックである。しかし、その一方で平田王子や金子マリ、松倉如子、清水秀子、さがゆき等々の女性ヴォーカリストとのデュオもしばしば行い、「渋谷さんといっしょ」というグループでは自らが歌も歌っている。また、映画音楽や佐良直美の曲を作曲するなどその活動は多岐に亘っているが、そのどれもが渋谷毅の真実であり渋谷毅そのものの実像が浮かび上がってくるところが凄い。そして、その永いキャリアのどこをとっても、いつ聴いても瑞々しい風情で存在感を漂わせている。

こうした多くの分野で精力的に活躍している渋谷毅をすべて聴くのはたいへんである。渋谷毅の世界にひたるのにはピアノ・ソロを聴くのが手っ取り早い。渋谷毅のピアノ・ソロにはこうした渋谷毅のあらゆる要素の芯の部分が随所に聴くことができる最もシンプルなスタイルだからである。よい空間で渋谷毅のピアノ・ソロを聴きたい、という声なき声も多いが渋谷さんは今回それに応えてくれた。来年2012年の1月13日(金)に東京・杉並区のホール、『座・高円寺』でピアノ・ソロと俊英ギタリスト市野元彦とのデュオというプログラム「渋谷毅＠座高円寺」が実現したのである。あらためて渋谷毅のエッセンスをストレートに体現する格好の企画と今から心待ちにしている。

items._cn_summary: 这是一篇对日本钢琴家渋谷毅的纪念性乐评，追溯其从东京艺大到爵士现场的生涯轨迹。文章重点讲述2007年两张专辑《Famous Melodies》与《Famous Composers》的录制过程，包括曲目筛选、多次录制以及乐手挑选的幕后细节。渋谷毅以诠释经典爵士曲目见长，将丹尼男孩、埃林顿、波特等名曲以独特的钢琴音色重新呈现。文中还涉及他与女性歌手的二重奏、电影音乐作曲等多元活动，以及2012年座高圆寺钢琴独奏音乐会的预告。整体行文偏回顾性与悼念性，属于传统爵士范畴的深度人物侧写。

All songs arranged by Emmet Cohen

本稿を起こすにあたり、本作品の主役エメット・コーエンに触れる前に鈴木鎮一に言及しなければなるまい。
1898年名古屋市に日本初のバイオリン製造会社を興した父政吉の三男として生まれ、長じて帝国音楽学校のバイオリン教授となった鈴木鎮一は音楽の早期教育を提唱し、幼児が父母の言葉を聞いているうちに自然に話せるようになることに着目し、母国語と同じように耳から音楽を教える母語教育法「スズキ・メソード」を確立していく。
太平洋戦争後、鈴木は1946年に長野県松本市に松本音楽院を開設、併せて全国幼児教育同志会を発足させ、2年後の1948年に才能教育研究会と改称し、さらに1950年に文部省より「社団法人 才能教育研究会」として認可され、今日に至る。鈴木鎮一は「スズキ・メソード」普及の主導的人物に他ならない。
その「スズキ・メソード」は発祥の日本よりもアメリカで多くの生徒が学んでいて、世界中に40万人を超える生徒がいる。音楽教育が主体ではあるが、それが本来の目的ではなく、音楽によって子供の心を豊かにし、自信をつけることにあるとしている教育法で、その教育理念は「どの子も育つ、育て方ひとつ」というもの。

エメット・コーエンは1990年フロリダ州マイアミの出身。3歳からこの「スズキ・メソード」でピアノを習い始める。ニュージャージー州のモントクレア高校時代にジャズ・アンサンブルの一員として活動、2012年にマイアミ大学フロスト音楽校で音楽学士号を、2014年にはマンハッタン音楽院で音楽修士号を取得している新進気鋭の若手ピアニスト。コーエンは世界各国でのコンサートツアーの他、COVID-19のパンデミック期からは自宅からのコンテンツ配信「Live from Emmet’s Place」を毎週行い、自己の演奏の普及に努めている。コーエンにとって最も重要なプロジェクトが「Master Legacy Series」でこれは2016年以来著名なジャズの巨匠をフィーチャーした演奏をプロデュースしているもの。これまでにヒューストン・パーソン、ジミー・コブ、ロン・カーター、ベニー・ゴルソン、アルバート・ヒース、ジョージ・コールマンとコラボレーションを組んでいる。この「Master Legacy Series」を始めるきっかけとなったのが2013年にテナー・サックスのレジェンド、ジミー・ヒースと５時間にわたるバス移動中、ヒースが往年の巨匠たちについての逸話を語ってくれたことだったという。世代間のギャップを知り、世代から世代へ知識の伝承と伝統の松明を引き継ぐことを決意したというコーエンのこうした取組みは「スズキ・メソード」の精神を見事に体現したものと言えないだろうか。

本作品『Universal Truth』は正に「Master Legacy Series」のひとつの到達点といえるアルバムかもしれない。現在N.Y.で最も多忙なドラマーの一人ジョー・ファーンズワース（1968年マサチューセッツ州生れ）、バークリー音楽大学とジュリアード音楽院を出てAtelier Sawanoに２枚のリーダー作を持つN.Y.在住のベーシスト中村恭志（1982年東京都生れ）とのレギュラートリオを軸に、ロン・カーター（ｂ）、ジョージ・コールマン（ts）、ジェレミー・ペルト（tp）、ティヴォン・ぺニコット(ts)をゲストとして迎えた本作品は、バド・パウエル、セロニアス・モンク、ジョン・コルトレーン、マイルス・デイヴィス、ジミー・ヒースらのイディオムを伝承して温故知新の体裁を取りながらも、コーエン自身の強烈なアイデンティティを融合させて更なる高みへと昇華させる知性と卓越した技倆の発露に他ならないからだ。

＜01＞ Budo　バド・パウエル作。パウエルのタッチを彷彿させるテーマから一転コーエンの緩急自在のソロワークが光る。王道のバップ色を濃厚に見せながら、途中のベースとのユニゾン、ドラムとのインタープレイなど聴き処の多いレギュラートリオによる冒頭の１曲。

＜02＞ Well, You Needn’t　セロニアス・モンク作。ドライヴの効いたイントロから J. ペルトのブリリアントなトランペットが時空を切り裂くように弾け、コーエンのピアノが原曲の強力な磁場を越えて新たな地平を拓いていく力強いストーリー展開が見事だ。

唯一のスタンダード＜03＞ My Funny Valentine　作詞ロレンツ・ハート、作曲リチャード・ロジャース。G.コールマンがテーマからソロへとテンダーな吹奏を聴かせる。これがあのコールマンかと思う程に柔和なブロウで驚かされる。成熟というべきか枯淡というべきか。それを強靭なタッチでスパイシーに変換するコーエンの力業が聴きもの。

＜04＞ Gingerbread Boy　ジミー・ヒース作。J. ペルトのミュート・トランペットがフィーチャーされるこの曲、R. カーターの強力なウォーキング・ベースが演奏をグルーヴィーな方向へ誘う牽引力になっている。‘50年代風のアーシーなビート感に思い切り浸れる心地良さをどう表現しようか。

＜05＞ I. Eternal Glimpse　ここからはコーエンの自作３曲が組曲風に続く。 tp、ts を加えたクインテント編成で、変拍子のテーマからストレートアヘッドな４ビートの波が押し寄せて、コーエンのエッジの効いたソロが鍵盤をグルーヴィーに跳ね回る。２管はソロもある一方、アンサンブル的な使われ方がコーエンの工夫。

＜06＞ II. Compassion　２管によるビターなバラッド。ミュート・トランペット、テナー共にバックコーラス的なプレゼンスで、楽曲に奥行きと陰影を与えるアトモスフィアの役割を果していることでコーエンのソロが浮き上がる仕掛け。

＜07＞ III. Universal Truth　スピリチュアルなテイストを持ったこの楽曲、演奏の色彩感と空気感を際立たせるという役割の２管の扱いはコーエンの独自性に他ならない。コーエンのフルスロットルの疾走感が光る。またこの曲ではJ. ペルトの力強いアタックと T. ぺニコットの力感溢れるブロウが気を吐いていて拾いもの。

＜08＞ Blue Train　ジョン・コルトレーン作。Blue Note盤のオリジナルではトロンボーンを交えた３管編成だったが、ここではテナー２本とトランペットの３管。咆哮するコールマンのテナーに続くコーエンのピアノはオリジナル演奏のムードをそのままに、原作者コルトレーンに敬意を表しているようだ。流麗なコーエンのピアノに耳を奪われているうちにエンディングを迎える。

コーエンは、Downbeat誌の取材に応え自身の活動について次のように語っている。「主な目標の一つは、ジャズの魅力にまだ気づいていない人々をこの音楽へ招待することです。楽しくて親しみやすいものにすると同時に、聴き手に新たな刺激を与える方法も見つけたいと思っています。アメリカのジャズの巨匠たちとの接点を提供することに喜びを感じるのです」
コーエンをこうしたジャズ啓発活動へと突き動かした原動力こそが「スズキ・メソード」にあると断ずるのは筆者の勝手な思い入れだろうか。

本作品は古き良き時代への単なるノスタルジーや現存する巨匠たちへの敬意を表しただけの作品ではない。コンテンポラリーなインテリジェンスに支配されがちな21世紀のジャズシーンに対し、ビバップ～ハードパップというジャズの伝統的にして根源的なエナジーとスピリットを強力無比な楔（くさび）として打ち込んでいるとは言えまいか。

items._cn_summary: 这是Emmet Cohen的专辑《Universal Truth》的乐评，属于主流爵士范畴。专辑以钢琴、贝斯、鼓为核心三重奏，客座乐手包括Ron Carter、George Coleman、Jeremy Pelt和Tivon Pennicott。曲目多为经典曲目翻奏，如Bud Powell的《Budo》、Monk的《Well, You Needn't》、《My Funny Valentine》、Jimmy Heath的《Gingerbread Boy》以及Coltrane的《Blue Train》。Cohen从三岁起学习铃木教学法钢琴，其'Master Legacy Series'致力于传承爵士巨匠的传统。乐评花了大量篇幅介绍铃木镇一和Cohen的教育背景，正文仅评述了前四首曲目。整体属于对经典爵士曲目温故知新的演绎，强调传统传承与技艺展示，但缺乏显著的实验性或创新突破。

items._cn_summary: Somi Kakoma 是一位拥有卢旺达-乌干达-美国多重文化背景的声乐家、作曲家和剧场创作者。文章标题暗示她的作品正处于世界爵士风格的成熟期，融合了跨大西洋的文化叙事与剧场化的呈现方式。卢旺达与乌干达的非洲根源为她的创作提供了独特的文化视角，但她的人物定位偏向主流爵士乐评视野，而非实验或前卫边缘。作为跨界创作者，她将声乐、戏剧与爵士作曲结合，呈现出一种融合性的艺术表达，但内容仅是简短摘要，缺乏具体的音乐细节和深度评论，无法全面评估其声音设计的创新程度与跨领域融合的实际手法。

items.body:
Smiling C trail their Shams Dinn diamond with this bounty of Washington Go-Go picks from the short-lived Aset label’s Whax, Treo, and Latonya, all recorded and originally released c. 1986-88. Like the Shams LP, A Totally New Sound brims with pure soulful optimism and home-baked charm, but rather than early Arabic rap and ‘80s boogie, this one surveys a blindspot in most collections with some of the rarest and most special Go-Go Records in existence. 

All eight song were written by the Aset label’s in-house players, revolving song-writers Mbu Mbulu and O Jabbo, and includes their semi-released instrumental Skip, along with three beauties by the 11 year old singer Latonya which are almost worth entry alone, plus one wild one by the Whax duo, and three from Treo, the trio of Cathy Young, Delores Lidell and Linda Lawson.

Seriously, the Latonya tracks are what pop dreams are made of - precocious yet innocent, flush with colourful melodies and driven by that bustling Go-Go hustle, the super infectious Dance Time is a ready-made anthem, while Eyes Of A Child and We Will Teach The Adults weirdly also recall early ‘80s Belgian cold wave crossed with Langley Schools Music Project, or something.

The Aset Players’ Skip reveals the boogie mechanics under their pop hood, while Whax tend to the freakier side with a spot of Rick James-ian flair, and Treo’s close harmonies come out perfectly pop-wise in Demands Demands Demands, but Second Is Too Close and the forlorn romance of When Your Love Is Gone feels too weird to be pop proper, and that’s where the magick lies in this LP, between Aset’s mainstream ambition and a realness of expression that can’t be missed.
items._genre: go-go / funk / soul / cold wave
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了1986至1988年间华盛顿Aset厂牌旗下艺人作品的重新整理，涵盖Whax、Treo和年仅11岁的Latonya等较少被关注的Go-Go音乐作品。整体呈现纯正放克律动与早期八十年代Boogie质感，编曲以鼓机与贝斯线为主轴，旋律朗朗上口且制作偏向商业流行审美。Latonya的演唱稚嫩却真诚，色彩鲜明的旋律配合Go-Go特有的忙碌律动成为亮点；Treo三人和声则靠近纯流行框架，但部分曲目因情感表达过于怪异而偏离主流流行可接受范围。Aset Players的器乐作品暴露出其旋律外壳下的放克机械结构，Whax则在Rick James风格中增添几分怪奇色彩。作为一张区域性复古Go-Go合辑，其价值更多在于历史档案层面而非音乐本身的实验性，与先锋、爵士、电子或暗潮等取向均距离较远。

items.body:
First full collaborative LP from Open Mike Eagle & Kenny Segal after nearly twenty years of friendship and occasional collaboration.

"It’s five years in a blender. It’s every troublesome misunderstanding of a half-decade relationship distorted and stretched into an absurdist black comedy mini-series on wax. It’s the sound of every fight we ever had, playing simultaneously. It’s several consecutive voice notes that you did not listen to, and instead read the transcription. It’s fifteen songs from iconoclastic rapper Mike Eagle and innovative producer Kenny Segal. It’s the world’s first half-whimsical break-up album. It’s DOOMED!

It’s also LA. Maybe not first and foremost, but Los Angeles runs deep in this record’s present, and its lineage. The story of any big city is also one of transplants. DJ Premier in New York, Tupac in California. If you build it, they will come. Mike and Kenny both arrived in LA as young, aspiring artists who were drawn to the scene around groundbreaking rap crew Project Blowed. They have been friends—and occasional collaborators—for almost twenty years. Despite that, DOOMED! is the first time the two have put together a full body of work. But everything happens in its time, and fate worked to bring them together at the exact moment that would allow the duo to create something extraordinary. Mike, fresh off a string of multi-producer records and processing the end of a tumultuous relationship, was in need of creative catharsis.

Meanwhile, Kenny had locked in on his next challenge after a recent string of critically acclaimed collaborations not only with rappers like billy woods, and K-the-I???, but also jazz trio Human Error Club and bluesy indie rocker Benjamin Booker.

“In recent years, Kenny made it very clear that he wasn’t trying to keep having one or two beats on my projects; he wanted to build something,” Open Mike Eagle explains. “I was able to convince him to let me use a couple beats for Neighborhood Gods Unlimited with the caveat that we would focus on our thing next. Then my relationship fell apart right when we started working, and it was like, ‘Perfect, I have a lot to say about this.’

Here are some more particularly interesting insights from the man himself:

“If DOOMED! is prestige TV, then think of “Out To Lunch” as the pilot where we meet a man who’s not all there because his head is still in yesterday, and the following as a brief synopsis. There’s a song that starts at an argument about the color of a rental car. There’s a song about trying to write a pair of lovers’ initials in wet concrete and the stick breaking. There’s a song that’s a prayer about finding the strength not to look at my ex’s social media. There’s a song about a character from Adventure Time who’s a piece of shit that I identify with. Each vision is a crashed airplane halfway on the border of dream and nightmare, bitter and sweet, sadness and freedom. Every one of Kenny’s beats is a chunk of ore from a different comet. I used each one as a canvas to paint my impression of a dead world.""
