items.body:
Moving sideways from Warp to Domino, Simian Mobile Disco's James Ellis Ford challenges himself on his second solo full-length, crafting a set of Sakamoto-inspired synth pop from his hospital bed.

Ford's always been capable of producing pitch-perfect pop - his appearance on records from everyone from the Pet Shop Boys to Depeche Mode is a testament to that - but 'Lost in Another World' is a more personal affair. It was written and produced in hospital after he'd been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia last year, "on the ward between rounds of chemo." Thankfully his condition has improved - he posted earlier this month that he's got no more treatment in store - but the album stands as a vulnerable reflection of a difficult time. Ford describes it as a "pep talk", and it draws on some of his most enduring influences, Yellow Magic Orchestra and Japan, to channel its complicated tangle of emotions. 

On the opening track (and lead single) 'Overtones', Ford's voice hovers over plasticky rhythmelodic sequences and rubbery '80s drums and you'd be forgiven for assuming it's a lost city pop demo. Ford doesn't let the energy fall off, either, waltzing through slow-motion melancholia on the tentatively beautiful 'Here Today' and John Foxx-style synth pop on 'This Too Shall Pass'. Ultimately, it's surprisingly hopeful material, infused with genuine feeling.

items._cn_summary: 这是Simian Mobile Disco成员James Ellis Ford的第二张个人全长专辑，从Warp转投Domino厂牌发行。专辑在他被诊断出急性髓系白血病后于医院病床上完成制作，化疗间隙在病房中编写并录制。音乐风格深受坂本龙一、Yellow Magic Orchestra和Japan乐队影响，合成器流行与八十年代新浪潮元素贯穿始终。开场曲《Overtones》带有city pop的复古质感，人声漂浮于塑料感的节奏序列与弹性鼓点之上；《Here Today》呈现慢速忧郁旋律；《This Too Shall Pass》呈现John Foxx式冷峻合成器流行。整体情感层次复杂，既记录了艰难时期的脆弱反思，也透出令人意外的希望感，Ford本人将其形容为一种自我激励。

items.body:
Scoring a graphic novel based on a dream he had in 2024, John Carpenter gets the band back together, turning in an album that'll delight fans of 'Lost Themes'.

We know full well that Hollywood doesn't seem interested in making Carpenter's films a reality any more - he's said as much, quite publicly. So what's the next best thing? Well, a graphic novel. 'Cathedral' was written by Carpenter alongside his wife (and long-time creative partner) Sandy King and, like all great Carpenter projects, it had to have a home-brewed score to ease it along. So who better to make the dream a reality than his regular bandmates Cody Carpenter and Daniel Davies? Chronologically, this one fits in right after 2024's 'Lost Themes No. 4: Noir', but fans of Carpenter's earlier (eerier) biz will be happy to hear that he's reaching a little further back this time. 

There's of course the hard rock influence that's been present since at least 'They Live', but every so often there's a glimmer of the earworm-laden synth pop that elevated 'Escape from New York', and the iconic 'Assault on Precinct 13'. Just peep the 'Halloween'-style piano breakdown on 'Inside Out', the 'In the Mouth of Madness' mood on opener 'Primeval' or the classic horror flex of 'Abandoned Cathedral', with its organs, orchestral swells and all-important Mellotron choirs.

items.body:
Death Is Not The End return to the soul-stir sound of deep south Sacred Harp Singers in 1993 - although it could feasibly be any time since the advent of portable tape recording - in the blessed company of the Union Grove Baptist Church, Ozark, Alabama. Feels just right in this humidity…

The Wiregrass Singers' Dewey Williams began learning the shape-note tradition in his childhood. He studied under Judge Jackson, who authored the landmark 1934 hymnbook The Colored Sacred Harp. In 1971, Williams formally organized The Wiregrass Sacred Harp Singers to preserve the music full-time. This unified troupe began touring nationally and leading workshops, which ultimately launched them onto stages at the Smithsonian and Newport folk festivals up until Williams' passing in 1995 when the group disbanded. The African-American Sacred Harp tradition in the Wiregrass region has steeply declined since the start of the 21st century, due to an aging generation of singers, and today it is largely sustained through archival preservation and occasional multi-book singing meetups.

This raw recording, made at the Union Grove Baptist Church, Ozark in mid-April 1993 finds the group singing from B. F. White’s The Sacred Harp (1844), which together with his brother-in-law William Walker’s Southern Harmony (1835) formed the musical backbone of generations of Southern music and Southern musical styles.
items._genre: sacred harp / shape-note / a cappella / folk
items._cn_summary: 这是Death Is Not The End厂牌发行的阿拉巴马州Wiregrass Sacred Harp Singers合唱团于1993年在Ozark联合浸信会录制的现场录音。乐团由Dewey Williams于1971年创立，致力于保存非裔美国人圣咏传统。他们演唱的是1844年B.F. White所著《The Sacred Harp》圣歌集中的曲目，与William Walker的《Southern Harmony》共同构成了南方音乐的根基。录音以原始、粗犷的方式呈现了无伴奏合唱，声音充满穿透力。然而这一传统民谣形式与评测者偏好的实验、前卫、电子、爵士等风格距离较远，世界音乐属性可作一定加分，但整体缺乏实验性元素和跨界融合特征。

items.body: Review by Steve Conrad — An Apocalyptic COVID-Confectionary ConstructionApocalyptic: "Relating to or predicting widespread destruction or the collapse of civilization." (American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language).I mean, look at this cover art- it positions the Rock Boutique as the last outpost of...something...before one ventures into the apocalyptic wilderness- the Elon Musk-esque rocket ship preparing to exit the planet (whichever planet this may be), the more-angular St. Louis arch, the slightly blood-shot mechanical eye in full surveillance mode, and the almost confectionary-appearing glowing purple...objects, which are (menacingly?) beginning to multiply within Morri's domain.And the "wheel in the sky"- biblical Ezekiel reference- and yes, what the heck is that reference? While the stream (with fiery twinkles) wends its way through the landscape.The COVID-ConfectionSo, on this third album from Chicago, USA's "progressive rock collective, REFESTRAMUS, the stage is set for the seven (on Bandcamp, nine) tracks featured on "Morri's Rock Boutique).I'm hearing these tracks- whichever version of the album you choose- as "COVID-Confection" since according to the band's bio- drummer/songwriter/lyricist Derek Ferguson formed the first incarnation of REFESTRAMUS during the initial onslaught of the worldwide global scourge of COVID, and the music on this album at least for me- an early progressive rock geek- reeks of the sort of touches that made Styx a lot of money, as well as the grandeur and flourishes that endeared many of us folks-of-a-certain-age to the progressive genre.I remember a faintly condescending review (probably in Rolling Stone, which in those days was holy writ for me) of one of the 70's era KANSAS albums, in which the all-knowing reviewer said something like, "it's fairly decent music, but with wedding-cake arrangements". Little did this reviewer know that these "wedding cake" arrangements were exactly what made some of us geeks sit up and pay attention!Which is to say that on this album, where are many "confectionary" sections that delight an aging geek, and might delight you as well, regardless of your age and geekiness. Keyboardist/vocalist Dyanne Potter Vogetlin provides standout synth and keyboard fills and flourishes that genuinely soar, that color the overall sound with richness and verve. One can hear this almost from the very beginning of the album.To this reviewer, the bass guitar and vocal prowess of Jan Christiana are almost other-worldly. Upon first hearing, I wondered who on earth could actually sing that high, with that kind of power and control? Well, Jan can. I suspect Jan also has a lot to do with the vocal arrangements, which are lush and varied, and become an additional "unsung" instrument in the confectionary construction of "Morri's Rock Boutique".So yes, even on the opening "Storms" and then certainly on the (Russian folk tale-based) "The Cossack's Dream", we get the kind of grandeur and sweep of early era progressive and glam-rock music. I had to think of AVIARY and of course Styx, sometimes even Queen due to the vocal flourishes.None of this is to diminish or minimize the contributions of each musician- it is a "rock collective" of accomplished musicians who play supremely well together, and given a spacious production by Ian Beaubout. The variety of approaches on this album is also worth mentioning, including the Russian, and later the Asian touches complete with instrumentation like shamisen, koto, and shakuhachi found on "Lakeview Samurai"- engagingly sung by Nam Chumo.Lakeview Samurai appeals to me like confection- surface sweetness, not so much substance. I can get the references to some of the current cultural scene, and the side-by-side transposition of the ancient and venerable samurai code. Everything is done well, it simply doesn't touch me very deeply, nor perhaps, fit within the framework of this album.Same goes for "Hell or NYC", pointing out the stereotypes (and perhaps well-deserved) of the coldness and rudeness of the vast population of that enormous and varied city. The sax touches and the film-noir story-telling is captivating- yet still, confection, for better or worse.I guess the themes being explored allow different interpretations- for me, the overall affect of the collection of tracks is that it seems like "pastiche", rather than coherent whole- in the sense of the "hodgepodge" definition of pastiche. And maybe that's Derek's point and his intention.In ConclusionIt's excellently done, catchy, filled with verve and variety, demonstrating fine musicianship from each participant in this production- progressive rock luminaries and newcomers too. AND at the same time, for better or worse, confectionary. I'm going with 3.5 candied stars, but rounding up to 4 thanks to the overall fine effort given.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自芝加哥的进步摇滚集体REFESTRAMUS，是其第三张作品。评论者将音乐形容为'COVID时期的甜点制作'，指的是编曲中大量华丽的键盘装饰、宏大的和声铺排以及层层叠叠的人声编排。乐评明确将其与七十八十年代的Styx、Kansas等剧院式流行/进步摇滚相比较，强调其'婚礼蛋糕式'的编曲结构——即以旋律优美、器乐华丽为核心，但并非以实验性或前卫性取胜。键盘手Dyanne Potter Vogetlet的合成器演奏和贝斯手/主唱Jan Christiana的高音域表现是评论重点。对于偏好实验前卫、自由爵士或电子音乐的听众而言，这张作品偏向传统主流进步摇滚的范畴，融合度与创新性均较为有限。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Cornwall's anachronistic Arthurian spacemen return with their seventh full-length studio album release since their formation (in Edinburgh) in 2010 and second in two years (which is unusually fast for them). 1. "Song of the Rainforest" (21:20) a vocal-less and more keyboard-generated epic than the usual Emerald Dawn offerings. Also, it feels as if the presence and contributions of Dave Greenaway and Tom Jackson here are on the same level of importance (and dynamics) as those of Ally and Tree. (36/40)- i. "Balance" - after a long 90-second intro of cave dripping sounds and two alternating sustained organ chords slowly establishing their pace and fullness and then the entrance and establishment of bass and drums into an awesome funk-lite vamp groove of two gorgeous Mellotron-like chords Ally enters with his seering electric guitar to deliver one of his best guitar solos ever--for five minutes! The contagious groove established by Dave Greenaway and Tom Jackson is awesome. - ii. Incursions - a stop-and-pause precedes a very slow switch to Smooth Reggae groove over which Ally solos with his tenor sax. As Trees synth strings enter (and Ally's tenor sax desists), the beat is sped up (we're now into the ninth minute), which prompts Ally to switch to his soprano sax--which gives Tree a little more room and license to embellish with her variety of synth strings riffs: often matching or meeting Ally's sax lines with her own.- iii. "Loss" - in the 11th minute another interlude of synth strings intervals paves the way for a heavier, almost ominous motif to set up with Tom's more tribalistic tom-tom-centered (synthetic talking drum?) drumming and Dave's heavily-wowed bass play being stomped over by some deep monster-saw keyboard and guitar riffs. The keyboards continue riffing--kind of soloing--for a couple of minutes over this motif before . . . - iv. "Regret" - the 14th minute has the establishment of a peaceful, perhaps sad motif of jungle/tropical sounds (including Tree's Amazonian flute) woven loosely around one another until the 18th minute when saw synth chords take over and Ally returns to shredding emotionally on his guitar. One of the most evocative, sensitive, and surprisingly tight--even thoughtful--sections of any Emerald Dawn song I've ever encountered. 2. "Rivers of Tears" (14:58) opens with a jaunty journey of jazz-classical-sounding solo piano play. Among the most impressive and pretty keyboard play I've ever heard from Tree! At 1:40 bass, drums, and, eventually, Ally's "reverberated-into-the-background" electric guitar slowly enter. Tree continues to tinkle the ivories within and behind the guitar, bass, and drums while adding some washes of synth strings to the mix as Ally continues shredding (as he does). Then Ally stops, making room for Tree to expand her piano note play as Tom and Dave slowly, gradually slow down and drop out. a pause/break at 3:30 results in the unleashing of Tree's reverb-drenched voice over only the banks of synth strings chords and still tinkling piano note play (mostly in progressing arpeggios)--which eventually becomes just synth strings as we enter into another little pause around 5:30. Here Tree establishes a chord progression with the repetition of four descending arpeggiated chords over which the rhythm section joins in and Ally deploys his tenor sax. Another pause at the seven-minute mark leads into a transference of the play of the descending chord pattern to synth strings as Tom and Dave kick back and Ally switches to electric guitar. Here Dave's bass playing is a bit rote and uninventive while the embellishments that Tom adds to his drumming feel a bit forced and "required" while Ally's guitar shredding sounds/feels . . . the same as ever. A little pause at the end of the tenth minute is filled with Tree's vocal lines until the band re-emerges with a kind of two-chord "tropical" vamp. Yet another stop and transition at 11:45 as the band shifts into a much more dark and ominous section--launched off as Tree shouts out a "Poison. Into. It's veins." declaration. This section could almost be coming from NIL or KING CRIMSON--even with Tree's operatic high-note repeat delivery of the word "poison." The motif then morphs in the second half of the 14th minute into something more akin to a Led Zeppelin descending chord progression--which it plays out to the song's end with embellishing accents coming from Ally's synths and Tom's drums. Not bad! (26.375/30)- i. "The Natural Cycle" - ii. "Disruption" 3. "Paradise" (8:56) opening with some excitingly pregnant synthesizer play--chords, bass, and peppy upper register riffs--which subside when Tree's plaintive, melancholy voice enters at 0:33 to introduce the song's theme. By the one minute mark she pauses wherein Tom and Mark enter with a cool, jazzy, STING "Englishman in New York"-like motif (which then happens to support Tree's "Englishman in New York" vocal melody lines). Nice bass line beneath Tree's organ chords as Ally enters with a bluesier Gilmour-like approach to his injections of guitar riffs and flurries. Around the four-minute mark the band slows things down, Tree's voice softens, while Mark and Tom's play kind of moves into greater prominence as Ally and Tree's keyboard play slides more into the background of the mix. Interesting! And I like it: I like having the bass and drums mixed in front of the keys, guitars, and saxes. The synth strings and guitar soloing in the next two minutes feel much more like the sound palette of Polish NeoProg masters COLLAGE's great textures on their Moonshine masterpiece (especially "The Blues"). In the seventh minute one of the keys begins to repeat and develop a melody line from THE MOODY BLUES' "Nights in White Satin," to which Tom backs down for a bit, but then everybody ramps up again into a fully-COLLAGE motif in which the synth strings continue soloing as other synth chords continue to deploy the "Nights in White Satin" chords and melody-reminders. Brilliant! And this is how they choose to end the song, the album! Awesome! Despite the "borrowing" of the sound palette and melody/chords, I finally feel as if The Emerald Dawn have arrived to the gates of top-tier prog, the symphonic side! (18.75/20)- i. "Losing Paradise"- ii. "Harmony Regained"Total Time 45:14I like the more sophisticated complexities ED are injecting into their compositions as it diminishes the dreaded monotony wrought of their old style of endlessly jamming over simple and often drawn-out single- and/or double-chorded vamps. Either their music theory has improved or they've decided to let go of the stoner-rock approach to song-rendering and employ more symphonic structuring for their music--whatever it is, I like it!A-/4.5 stars; a stunningly-improved advancement of compositional design yields the best album of The Emerald Dawn's career--one that has them knocking on the door of the Valhalla of the Symphonic Prog masters! I'm bumping up this rating into masterpiece status for the surprising display of growth as well as this being, in my opinion, Emerald Dawn's best album yet.
items._genre: neo-prog / symphonic prog / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这是一张新前卫摇滚（Neo-Prog）专辑，延续了七十年代交响前卫摇滚的编制与审美。乐评详细描述了超过二十分钟的器乐史诗如何以键盘为主导展开，融合管风琴持续音、合成器弦乐、萨克斯独奏与电吉他shredding段落，在funk、reggae与部落鼓击节奏之间切换。创作者将丛林环境音与合成器模拟乐器并置，营造出带有叙事感的氛围画面。整体手法偏向传统前卫摇滚的内部扩张逻辑，虽有部分乐器编排细节颇具匠心，但在声音设计与结构创新上缺乏对前卫摇滚既有范式的突破，与实验音乐、爵士即兴或电子领域的真正融合相距较远。

items.body: Oxford band Shaven Primates released the four-track EP “Kill The Algorithm” on TAD Records on 31 July 2026. The EP runs 17 minutes and 53 seconds. What Shaven Primates address on ‘Kill The Algorithm’ The EP opens with “Saviour” (4:26), then moves through “Pioneer Way” (3:30) and “Feed” (4:28) before the title track “Kill The Algorithm” (5:28). Across the four songs the band take on dependency, tabloid conditioning, grievance politics and the mechanics of social media. “Pioneer Way” sets its argument in a Britain of workplace exhaustion and scapegoating, with the line “Commonplace everyday wreck of the UK”. The title track turns on the repeated command of its own name. Shaven Primates describe themselves on Bandcamp as “a 5-piece dark-wave, art-rock, post-punk band that seeks to push the boundaries of the genre”, adding that their “music is a narrative of human emotion and experience; fear, love and anger resonate through the orchestration, giving a deeply cathartic release”. “Kill The Algorithm” is on Spotify. The band’s Bandcamp page currently lists their three earlier releases only, so the EP cannot be bought there yet. About Shaven Primates Shaven Primates are based in Oxford, UK, and mix darkwave, art-rock and post-punk with harder guitar work. The band’s own summary of that mix is short: their music is “a narrative of human emotion and experience”. Their Bandcamp discography begins with “Child Of Dirt” on 26 November 2021, followed by “Birds Aren’t Real” on 28 July 2023 and “Chasing The Dragon” on 13 December 2024. Neither Discogs nor Wikipedia holds an entry for the band, so the Bandcamp listings remain the clearest record of their releases. “Kill The Algorithm” is their first release since “Chasing The Dragon” in December 2024, and the first to carry the TAD Records imprint.

items._cn_summary: 本文为牛津乐队Shaven Primates四曲EP《Kill The Algorithm》的发布资讯，发布于独立厂牌TAD Records。文章介绍了曲目时长与编排顺序，提炼了各曲的主题：依赖感、小报式条件反射、怨愤政治以及社交媒体机制，并引用了'Pioneer Way'中关于英国职场疲惫与替罪氛围的歌词，以及标题曲以反复念诵为支点的结构。乐队自我定位为五人制的暗黑浪潮、艺术摇滚与后朋克混合，描述其音乐为人类情感与体验的叙事，恐惧、爱与愤怒贯穿编配，带来宣泄式释放。文章以背景资料为主，梳理了乐队此前的三张作品年表，指出该EP是2024年12月以来的首次发行，也是首次携带TAD Records厂牌标识的作品。文章未对音乐本体进行深入评论或听感分析。

items.body: Hocico‘s debut full-length album, “Odio Bajo El Alma,” turns 29 on 14 August. The Mexican electro-industrial duo released the record on 14 August 1997 through the Mexican label Opción Sónica, with European distribution handled by Out Of Line. ‘Odio Bajo El Alma’ tracklist and credits “Odio Bajo El Alma” was Hocico’s first official release after three self-produced cassette demos – “Misuse, Abuse and Accident” (1993), “Autoagresión Persistente” (1994) and “Triste Desprecio” (1996). The album was produced by Edmundo Navas, with engineering handled by the band alongside Rogelio Gómez. It was issued on CD and cassette in Mexico, later reissued in Germany through Out Of Line and Sub/Mission Records, and reissued again on vinyl by Out Of Line in 2019. The album runs 11 tracks: “Cuando la Maldad Despierta” “Odio en el Alma” “Beings of Relief” “Final Resource” “Hell on Earth” “Gota de Sangre” “Temple of Lies” “Sexo Bajo Testosterona (Frenetik Mix ’96)” “Sad Scorn” “Slow Death” “Face to Face” The record is available to stream via Spotify. According to Wikipedia, “Odio Bajo El Alma” was well received across Europe and the Americas and introduced audiences outside Mexico to a style of electronic music few realized was being made there. Before the album’s release, Hocico had been part of a Mexico City collective called La Corporación, alongside acts such as Cenobita, Ogo, Encefálisis and Deus Ex Machina, that supported and promoted the country’s electronic underground. About Hocico Hocico is a Mexican electro-industrial duo formed in 1993 in Mexico City by cousins Eric García, performing as Erk Aicrag, and Óscar Mayorga, performing as Racso Agroyam. García writes the lyrics and performs vocals, while Mayorga handles programming. Both had experimented with electronic music since their teens, drawing on industrial acts such as Skinny Puppy. Their musical partnership began in 1989 in a group called Niñera Degenerada, and in 1992 the two left that project to form Hocico de Perro, later shortened simply to Hocico. Between 1993 and 1996 the duo self-released three cassette demos before issuing “Odio Bajo El Alma” in 1997 on Opción Sónica with Out Of Line handling European distribution. The end of the decade brought the live album “Los Hijos Del Infierno,” recorded during Hocico’s 1998 European tour, and the studio follow-up “Sangre Hirviente” (1999), which reached number 19 on the CMJ RPM chart in the United States. Hocico played the Zillo festival in Germany and the Euro Rock festival in Belgium in 1999, returned to Germany’s Woodstage festival in 2000 in front of more than 20,000 people, and opened for Rammstein during that band’s 2001 Mexican tour. “Signos De Aberración” followed in 2002, then “Wrack And Ruin” in 2004, after which the band paused new studio material. During the break, García launched his solo project Rabia Sorda and relocated to Leipzig, Germany, while Mayorga remained based in Mexico City. Hocico resumed with “Memorias Atrás” in 2008 and has released an album roughly every two years since: “Tiempos de Furia” (2010), “El Ultimo Minuto” (2012), “Los días caminando en el fuego” (2013), “Ofensor” (2015), “The Spell of the Spider” (2017, which reached number 42 on the German national charts) and “Artificial Extinction” (2019, an album centered on artificial intelligence as a threat to humanity, which peaked at number 30 in Germany). “Hyperviolent” followed in 2022. Side-Line has continued to track the band’s output, including the Hey Tú EP expansion with Prayers and, most recently, the ‘Unseen Horror Scenes’ album, released in May 2026. Twenty-nine years after “Odio Bajo El Alma” introduced the duo to audiences outside Mexico, the album remains the starting point of that catalog.

items.body: 45 Grave released the album “Pick Your Poison” on 14 August 2012 through Frontier Records. The Los Angeles deathrock band’s album turns 14 this year and stood as its first collection of new material in 27 years, following the group’s 1985 breakup after “Sleep in Safety.” Dinah Cancer had reformed 45 Grave in 2004 and rebuilt the lineup several times over the following years. By 2010, the band settled into a configuration of Cancer on vocals, guitarist Frank Agnew (the Adolescents, T.S.O.L.), bassist Brandden Blackwell and drummer Tom Coyne, the lineup that recorded “Pick Your Poison.” The album mixes newly written songs with older, previously unrecorded material and a re-worked version of “Night of the Demons,” for which a video was produced. “Pick Your Poison” contains ten tracks: “Pick Your Poison,” “Night of the Demons,” “Child of Fear,” “Akira,” “A Desert Dream,” “Lucky 214,” “Highway 666,” “Johnny,” “Sorceress” and “Winds of Change.” Frontier Records issued the album on CD and vinyl. Pick Your Poison by 45 Grave About 45 Grave 45 Grave formed in Los Angeles in 1979, growing out of a related project called Vox Pop. The original lineup paired vocalist Dinah Cancer, formerly of Castration Squad, with guitarist Paul B. Cutler, bassist Rob Graves (also known as Rob Ritter, formerly of the Bags and the Gun Club) and drummer Don Bolles of the Germs. The band’s name came from a thrift-store button reading “WE DIG 45 GRAVE.” Alongside Christian Death, 45 Grave is recognized as one of the earliest American gothic rock acts, developing a hybrid of horror punk and gothic rock that came to be known as deathrock. The band’s sole studio album from its original run, “Sleep in Safety,” followed the 1981 single “Black Cross” and built on the earlier fast-paced version of “Partytime,” later slowed down and reworked for the album. A remixed version of “Partytime” appeared on the soundtrack to the 1985 film “The Return of the Living Dead” and became an MTV staple. 45 Grave broke up in 1985. A brief reunion in 1988 produced the live album “Only the Good Die Young,” but the band split again after bassist Rob Graves died in 1990. Dinah Cancer revived 45 Grave in 2004 to mark the band’s 25th anniversary, working through several lineup changes before settling by 2010 on guitarist Frank Agnew, bassist Brandden Blackwell and drummer Tom Coyne. That lineup recorded “Pick Your Poison,” released on Frontier Records on 14 August 2012 as the band’s first collection of new material in 27 years. Guitarist Dylan Thomas, formerly of the Dickies, joined in 2014, and the band has continued to perform since, including a two-day billing at the Cruel World festival in Pasadena in 2022 alongside Bauhaus, Devo, Blondie and Morrissey.

items.body: Soundedit has announced the lineup for its 18th edition, running in Łódź, Poland, from 23 to 27 October 2026. The festival confirmed Marc Almond of Soft Cell, former Kraftwerk drummer Wolfgang Flür, The Stranglers founder Hugh Cornwell, producer Howie B and The Wolfgang Press among the performing artists. Tickets are on sale through Ticketmaster and Eventim. Soundedit is built around the people who shape recorded sound rather than around a single genre, and pairs a concert programme with what it describes as the largest pro-audio educational programme in Europe. Soundedit 2026 lineup and dates The confirmed performers are: Howie B – the producer known for his work with U2, Björk and Massive Attack, returning to the festival with new original material Hugh Cornwell – the original singer and guitarist of The Stranglers, performing with his full band, including “Golden Brown” and “No More Heroes” Wolfgang Flür – electronic music pioneer and Kraftwerk’s drummer from 1973 to 1987 Marc Almond – the Soft Cell vocalist behind “Tainted Love” The Wolfgang Press – presenting new material following their return to live performance Maszynowa – premiering their album “Supernowa” Kasia Lins – with her Obywatelka K.L. project, built on the music of new wave band Republika and Grzegorz Ciechowski Dezerter – marking 45 years, with material from their 2026 album “Wolny wybieg” Lech Janerka – appearing as part of his farewell tour K-2 – the duo of Ziemowit Kosmowski and Agata Poremba-Kosmowska Almond performs as the surviving half of Soft Cell, following the death of Dave Ball in October 2025. The Wolfgang Press last released the album “A 2nd Shape” in 2024, their first in nearly three decades. The Man with the Golden Ear award and 50 years of punk The festival weekend ends with the Man with the Golden Ear award, given for contributions to recorded sound. The 2026 recipient is Ziemowit Kosmowski, the Polish punk and new wave musician who founded Brak and Rendez-Vous. He also performs during the festival with K-2, the duo he runs with his wife Agata Poremba-Kosmowska. Further recipients are still to be announced. Soundedit is also marking 50 years of punk rock with a photo exhibition at the Łódź Photographic Society Gallery, alongside meetings, workshops and awards tied to the anniversary. After the concert weekend, the pro-audio programme runs on 26 and 27 October at the DoubleTree by Hilton hotel and Klub Wytwórnia, with over a hundred masterclasses, workshops and lectures. The festival expects over 1,000 delegates each day, covering topics from live sound mixing to room acoustics measurement, led by working producers and academic staff. About Soundedit Soundedit was established in Łódź in 2009 by music producer, composer and radio broadcaster Maciej Werk, founder and frontman of the Polish rock band Hedone. He set it up to direct attention to record producers, sound designers and sound engineers rather than to performers alone, and it remains the only festival with that specific focus. Since its first edition, the festival has combined concerts by Polish and international artists with a technical and educational strand, and has drawn both industry delegates and general audiences to Łódź each autumn. Its Man with the Golden Ear statuette has become the event’s central annual honour; Lech Janerka, who plays this year’s edition on his farewell tour, received it in 2014. The 2026 programme is the festival’s 18th, and its lineup leans heavily on artists whose work shaped synth-pop, post-punk and electronic music, from Kraftwerk and Soft Cell through The Stranglers and The Wolfgang Press.

items.album: The Arms of Someone New expand ‘Love, Power & Justice’ to 38 tracks on Projekt
items.excerpt: Projekt has released the 40th anniversary deluxe edition of “Love, Power & Justice” by The Arms of Someone New. The set went up on 14 August 2026 as a name-your-price download on the label’s Bandcamp page, and runs to 38 tracks across three parts. The material dates from 1986, when Mel Eberle and Steve Jones recorded it in Champaign-Urbana, Illinois. Projekt first issued it on CD in July 2000 through its Projekt: Archive imprint. The 2026 edition returns to the original tapes.
items.body: Projekt has released the 40th anniversary deluxe edition of “Love, Power & Justice” by The Arms of Someone New. The set went up on 14 August 2026 as a name-your-price download on the label’s Bandcamp page, and runs to 38 tracks across three parts. The material dates from 1986, when Mel Eberle and Steve Jones recorded it in Champaign-Urbana, Illinois. Projekt first issued it on CD in July 2000 through its Projekt: Archive imprint. The 2026 edition returns to the original tapes. Love, Power & Justice (2026 40th anniversary deluxe edition) by The Arms of Someone New What the ‘Love, Power & Justice’ deluxe edition contains The first part is a new 2026 mix of the eleven-track album: “Silhouette”, “Hollywood”, “No City Fun”, “Next Year in Jerusalem”, “Summer Dress”, “Your Evening At Home”, “The Sense of an Ending”, “Believe Me”, “Our Town”, “Everything At Once” and the opening piece. The second part collects fifteen previously unreleased and alternate recordings from the same period, among them “Dear Friend”, “The Far Cafe”, “Dreaming of Home”, “4 O’Clock”, “Finding My Way Back Home”, “December 1910 (Vietnam instrumental)”, “Vietnam (Business is Business)”, “Carry the Day” and “Lady on Train”, plus 4-track versions of “The Sense of an Ending” and “Summer Dress”, demo versions of “Summer Dress”, “In Between” and “Radio Now”, and a 2026 remaster of “Uptown”. The third part restores the 1986 mix in a 2026 remaster, so the set carries both readings of the album in full. The artwork has been reworked for the reissue. Projekt also still lists final copies of the 2000 CD in a jewel box. Eberle and Jones will host a listening party on Saturday 29 August 2026 at 20:00 CEST, running through the expanded edition in text chat on Bandcamp. About The Arms of Someone New Mel Eberle and Steve Jones formed The Arms of Someone New in 1983 while students in Champaign-Urbana, Illinois. Their reference points were The Beatles and psychedelia on one side and the melancholy end of Factory Records and The Cure around “Faith” on the other. They worked with simple synthesizers, a Roland TR-707 drum machine and heavily reverbed guitars, with vocals kept low in the arrangements. Their debut album “Susan Sleepwalking” appeared in 1985 on their own Office Records imprint, with Nick Rudd contributing guitar and vocals to two tracks. “Love, Power & Justice” followed, recorded with contributions from musicians who would go on to form the dream pop act Area, including guitarist Henry Frayne, later of Lanterna, and Lynn Canfield. Frayne holds writing credits on “Hollywood” and “Believe Me”; Canfield on “Our Town” and “Uptown”. Brendan Gamble also played on the sessions. Projekt has handled the duo’s catalogue since the 2000 CD. The label put “Tape Recordings 1983-1985” on Bandcamp in March 2026, and issued a three-disc 40th anniversary edition of “Susan Sleepwalking” in October 2025. The “Love, Power & Justice” set completes that pair, and is the first time the album has been remixed rather than reissued as recorded.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

近年体調を崩され活動縮小を余儀なくされていた古野さんの復調を捉えた盟友達による好企画。私自身は’21/4以来となった今宵の主役・古野さんに加え主宰者・大友さん等我が国のジャズ界を長年に亘り牽引し続けるヴァチュオーゾ達が居並ぶ画は如何にも壮観。Ｓ.リバース〈Beatrice〉で幕開けし、〈Desert Ｍoonlight＝月の砂漠〉や2nd.set冒頭にピアノトリオで供された市川さんオリジナル〈Ｋ’s Museum〉、更には古野さん入魂のアルコプレイをフィーチャーした〈Black Orpheus〉等々を織り成しつつ大友さんの泣きのアルトをフィーチャーしたソウルバラード〈Ｗhen a Man Loves a Woman〉で本編を締めた後、満場のアンコールに応えたＢ.ティモンズ〈Ｍoanin’〉で目出たくお開きとなった今宵のステージでは、所謂著名なアメリカン乃至はジャズスタンダードを多く含む全11編が題に採られたが、そこでは、テーマ部を丁寧に扱い、アドリヴ部に至るや、豊富なアイデアと鍛え抜かれた技の数々に溢れた説得力のあるソロの応酬及び気の利いたバッキングでアンサンブルとしてじっくりと聴かせにかかる。といったやうに。全編に亘り意気に乗ったジャズ音楽の醍醐味を存分に味わった。

items.body:
音質マイスター萩原光男のサウンドチェック
NO. 340
#25 『シンディ・ブラックマン・サンタナ／コヒーレンス』
2026年8月15日
萩原光男

text:Mitsuo Hagiwara 萩原光男

Mack Avenue BSMF-5149. ¥3,500+税（8/21リリース予定）

Cindy Blackman Santana: Drums (All), Spoken Word (4, 6)
Aurelien Budynek: Guitar (1-3, 7, 10, 11, 13-17)
Felix Pastorius: Bass (1-3, 7, 10-17)
Emilio Modeste: Saxophone (1-3, 7, 10-17)
Zaccai Curtis: Keyboards (1-3, 7, 10-16)

Carlos Santana: Guitar (3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 17)
Snoop Dog: Shout-Out Intro (3)
Matt Garison: Bass (4, 5, 6)
Dave Eggar: Strings (7, 8, 11-14)
Ray Angry: Keyboards (8)
John McLaughlin: Guitar (9), Organ (9)
Alonso Broz: Bass (9)

1. Illumination
2. Blue Whale
3. The Message is Love
4. Coherence Tapestry
5. Coherence
6. Coherence Embrace
7. Peace Please
8. Psychedelic Movie House
9. Guitar Love
10. Capri
11. SyZyGy
12. Circe
13. Eclipse
14. Soon a Queen
15. Sunday
16. Music
17. Sanctuary

1.まえがき

アメリカン・ジャズ・ロックを、アメリカン・オーディオの底力で、たっぷり味わいました。ロック・ファンの私としてはひさびさに聴くカルロス・サンタナです。近頃再婚したとのこと、ドラマーの奥さんとの仲睦まじき演奏か、とタカをくくって聴きました。当家のベッドサイド・オーディオでは、まさにその域を出ませんでした。試聴の最後は、筆者所有の大型システムで聴くのですが、パパ・サンタナのギターの咆哮と、重戦車の如きドラムワークに圧倒されました。

「私が日本製オーディオを使わないのは、日本製はサラリーマン・オーディオだから。オーディオに浸るのであれば、遊び人オーディオで聴かなければ！」(筆者加筆編集) と、著書の中で語ったのは、ジャズ&オーディオ評論家 寺島靖国翁です。

当家の最終試聴システム、マッキントッシュ・アンプで鳴らすJBL4320は、そんなアメリカの「遊び人オーディオ」なのです。アメリカ人は車でもSUV（Sport Utility Vehicle) と言って、遊びのために実用性や悪路走破性を備えながら、日常のドライブやレジャーなど幅広い用途で使える乗用車を作ってしまう国の人々の作るオーディオです。これで聴くパパ・サンタナのギターは荒野をつんざく雷鳴のよう、それに呼応するシンディ・B・サンタナのドラムは重戦車です。ベッドサイド・オーディオで心地よく鳴っていたアルバムは、その音にまさにSUVの如き悪路さえ突っ走る重厚さでステージをアリゾナ砂漠に変え、迫り来るのでした。

2. カルロス・サンタナの今

サンタナのギターと言えば、あの＜ブラック・マジック・ウーマン＞の「キーン」と鳴り響いて中高域を駆け巡る速弾きのギターです。＜ブラック・マジック・ウーマン＞はピーター・グリーンが作曲し、「フリートウッド・マック」で演奏した曲です。このカバーをサンタナが1970年に、アルバム『天の守護神』に収録して大ヒットさせました。
サンタナと筆者の関わりですが、＜ブラック・マジック・ウーマン＞の1970年代の次は、1990年代のオーディオ・バブル期に、DVDデモ・サラウンドソースでの彼のステージ演奏でした。あらためて近年の彼の活動を確認すると、たくさんのステージをこなしツアーも行っているとのこと。そして2010年にジャズ・ロック・ドラマーのシンディ・ブラックマンと結婚したのです。ミュージシャン同士の結婚ですから、カルロス・サンタナも、愛情とともに、音楽の新展開を狙ったこともあるはずです。今回のアルバムを聴くと、カルロス・サンタナは、ギターにかけた武人から、戦隊を組むに至ったロック・ジャズの隊長、と言った音楽に聞こえます。音的にも、陶酔的なエキセントリックなギターワークから、客演とはいえ重戦車を率いるギターに変身しています。

3．このアルバムの音

①編成
このアルバムは、ギター3本、ベースギター、ドラム、と管楽器が入っていることで音楽的な厚みを増しています。編成の大きさで味わえる迫力感、音の響きの豊かさも、このアルバムの魅力です。

②ドラムの低音
筆者所有のアメリカ製「遊び人オーディオ」で聴くとパワーと電源安定度があるので、ドラムのベースが太く迫力があり、女性のドラマーと甘くみてはいけません。10曲目はこのトラックだけ他の曲とはちがって、特別にキーが低く、重厚な迫力で圧倒されます。まさに聴きどころです。

③楽器の配置・定位
曲目ごとの楽器の定位・配置も大きな聴きどころです。ギターがエコー豊かにすべてを包み込む様に広がり、ベースの残響はオフで前面に聞こえます。この定位に関しては、当方の大型システムで、低音高音とも高ダイナミック・レンジのシステムで味わえました。
特に、遊び人オーディオ、と言ってしまいましたが、筆者使用のマッキントッシュ・アンプなどアメリカのパワーアンプは、出力パワーに対して必要以上に電源の余裕があります。この様なものづくりは、当然、低音の安定した再生能力に貢献しているわけで、低音イコール音場の安定した広がりの再生が可能となり、この点からも、音場や定位の再現が優れているわけで、当然今回のアルバムはそれに応えるだけのパフォーマンスを持って制作されているのです。

4．アルバム試聴記

各曲の音を次の様に聴きました。

＊１曲目：  バスドラ、ドスドスと大迫力。ロックアルバムと感じました。しぶとくバスドラをキックし続けるのがシンディ・ブラックマン・サンタナのスタイルか。非常な説得力を感じる。アルバム全体を通してだが、ブラスの演奏が音楽に厚みを付けている。

＊３曲目：これぞカルロス・サンタナ！！というギターです。
ギターのまさに咆哮から始まり、筆者の様なロックファンを虜にしてしまいます。
エキセントリックなギターワークが空間に鳴り響き漂う。その高域に時折り低域でブファブファとファズを効かせる、ややお決まりのエレキギター・フレーズは、ギター好き殺し、とさえ言ってしまいましょう。
そのギターの高域にバスドラの重低音が良くバランスしています。
このギターのハイのヒステリックな叫びは、まさにパパ・サンタナここにあり、というところ、このアルバムの聴きどころです。

他の曲も素晴らしいですがオールド・ファッションとは言え、多くの人に聴いてほしい。筆者絶賛の３曲目です。

＊５曲目 ： パパ・サンタナが登場しますが、この曲含めて、３曲目以外は流している感じ。その様なわけで、３曲目があるからこのアルバムの価値がある、とさえ言えます。

＊６曲目 ： 40秒ほどの短い曲ですが、シンディ・B・サンタナの語りです。ややハスキーでフェードアウトしていく。coherenceと語り続けて暗示的。

＊８曲目  ：アダージョのテンポでパパ・サンタナ始め、複数のギターの協奏でエコーのかかり方なども良い感じ。この曲も、このアルバムの一つの典型のようです。

＊９曲目：  ＜Guitar Love＞と題されたこの曲は、ジョン・マクラフリン、パパ・サンタナも加わりそれぞれバラードっぽく演奏しています。後ろにエレピとギター一本がエコーがかかってひろがり、ベースとドラムスが前面に配置され音作りがドリーミーで良い。手慣れた音作りを感じます。

＊１０曲目：  バラードっぽく管楽器が前面にいて、ギターがややエコーを効かせてムーディーな音作り。冒頭からのドラムはこのトラックだけ特別にキーが低く迫力で圧倒する。シンディ・B・サンタナの面目躍如、というところか。

＊１６曲目：  最後を飾るにふさわしい、アップテンポでドラムが疾走して、ギターが追従する。ギターのファズ・エフェクターの音各種は聴いたことのあるもののオンパレード。最後を飾るにふさわしい。

5．あとがき

今回は、筆者所有の、遊び人オーディオという人もいるアメリカン・オーディオで、ジャズ＆ロックのもう一つ別の音楽が聴けました。筆者は、音楽に多感な時期をロックを聴いて過ごしたので、この分野の音楽には思い入れがあります。

ところで、ロックミュージックの出現は時代の必然です。
1960年代1970年代はエレキミュージックの萌芽期、時代のエネルギーは活力ある若者にあり、ビジネス的にも大きなものになります。こうした背景で盛り上がったロック、カルロス・サンタナもこの盛り上がりの頂点にいたわけです。
今は、音楽はやや停滞期、すべての音楽に活力は感じられるものの時代を牽引する大きな流れは感じられません。こんな時は、時代の流れに素直についていきます。

AI、パワー、金額で大きくなったオーディオ、デジタル、ボーダーレス、そして過去に見出すステキなもの・機材と。

CDを受け取った時、ステレオタイプ、お決まりの音を心に描いてしまいましたが、聴き終わってみると、どうやら編集長の深い思いが潜んでいた様で、敬服の至りであります。

items._cn_summary: 该乐评以音响发烧视角展开，对一张爵士摇滚专辑进行试听记录。专辑由鼓手Cindy Blackman Santana领衔，邀得多位乐手参与，吉他与鼓构成核心，萨克斯与键盘增添层次。评论者花了大量篇幅讨论美式音响系统的电源储备与音场定位能力，将专辑的低频冲击力与吉他咆哮声形容为雷鸣与重战车。曲目分析偏向传统摇滚听感，强调鼓点的持续冲击和吉他独奏的戏剧性，整体音乐语言倾向于主流爵士摇滚融合，与实验、前卫或电子方向相距甚远。评论本身更接近发烧器材测评而非音乐艺术评论。

items.body:
An ATL house and soul don hustles in-the-pocket bossa, broken beat, and deep boogie grooves, bolstered with Ben Hixon’s dubby Salsoul-style remix.

Marquinn Mason’s vocals elevate the session to classiest lounge club levels, dusting a jazz-soul flow to the Brazilian shuffle of ‘Bossa Beat’, and oiling the broken beat angularity of ‘Bounce’, before ideally adapting to the squashed electro-soul boogie of ‘Moving Steady’, and reminding of Omar-S joints with John F.M. ben Hixon’s remix only accentuates that comparison with a supple ATL-via-313-and-NYC Salsoul deep house appeal.
items._genre: deep house / boogie / broken beat / soul
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以亚特兰大为据点，融合放克、巴萨诺瓦律动与碎拍节奏，深陷浩室舞曲的舒适区。Marquinn Mason的人声贯穿始终，在爵士灵魂的流动与电子碎拍的棱角之间游走，辅以Ben Hixon偏Salsoul风格的混音版本，整体呈现出深夜俱乐部式的悠闲质感。制作强调律动与氛围，缺乏对声音边界的大胆探索，编曲结构偏保守，更注重情绪的圆润而非形式的突破。作为舞池实用主义的产物，它在放克/浩室爱好者中或有吸引力，但对于寻求前卫声响或实验性结构的听众而言，提供的惊喜有限。

items._cn_summary: 阿拉巴马州乡村摇滚乐队第三张专辑，由Dave Cobb继续操刀制作。专辑以饱满的音场和悠长的氛围为基调，福音风格的合唱在'Demons In Your Choir'中营造出壮阔的画面感。南方灵魂乐气质的慢板'Walking Away'是专辑中较为突出的作品，展现了乐队对传统根源音乐的扎实理解。整体制作精良，风格取向偏向美式南方音乐传统，在根源摇滚爱好者群体中具有一定吸引力，但对追求前卫与实验路线的听众而言，其手法相对传统保守，缺乏惊喜与突破。

items._cn_summary: 这是一档名为《Race The Sky》的广播节目第026期，主持人Cliff Furnald呈现了跨越九十年音乐史的杂烩式选曲。曲目涵盖范围极广，从Sophia Loren与Peter Sellers的经典对唱、David Bowie的代表作，到塞内加尔kora演奏家Dawda Jobarteh的西非竖琴音乐、尼日利亚Alhaji Waziri Oshomah的传统宗教音乐，以及佛得角Cape Verde风格的Eneida Marta作品。文中提到的Montparnasse Musique属于法国chanson实验，DOGO可能涉及非洲电子或汤加舞蹈音乐，Shagan可能为印度宝莱坞风格。整体编排偏向多元文化拼盘，缺乏统一美学线索，更接近音乐汇编而非主题策划。文章本身信息量极短，几乎没有深度评论或音乐分析，仅为节目曲目预告。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由三位音乐人通过多年邮件合作完成，以极简编曲和短小精悍的十八首小品构成，总时长仅三十四分钟。作品以原声吉他、尤克里里琴、滑棒吉他与清澈女声为核心，风格偏向美式民谣基底，融合乡村、布鲁斯与甜美的管风琴色彩。歌词主题围绕失去——失去爱情、失去信心，以及对世界怪诞的无奈接受。评论将其类比为Michelle Shocked、Cowboy Junkies与Dolly Parton式的传统美国根源音乐脉络。整体氛围如梦境般朦胧、节制、内敛，强调歌词的直接与编曲的克制。专辑将于2026年在多伦多Koerner Hall完整演出。

items._cn_summary: 本期节目以河流与沼泽为线索，汇集了多位民谣与根源音乐艺术家的作品，涵盖美国布鲁斯、民谣传承与欧洲民间音乐传统。曲目包括Dr John的纽奥尔良风格、Steve Earle的乡村摇滚、Johnny Cash的经典录音，以及来自东欧、斯堪的纳维亚与非洲的跨界艺人。整体编排偏向RootsWorld电台式的文化拼贴，侧重地域音乐传统的呈现，而非音乐本身的实验性或先锋性。对于关注前卫爵士、电子实验或暗潮工业等领域的听众而言，此节目偏向传统民俗的展示，缺乏声音设计层面的创新与跨界融合深度。原文仅为节目曲目单与播出平台信息，不含具体乐评文字，信息量极为有限。
